articleTitle: “Questomatic”: Automated Question Formulation System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The importance of automatically creating questions from text is growing, especially in a variety of industries.However, current AQG systems struggle with scalability, contextual accu-racy, and question diversity also existing systems often focus on objective questions, with less attention given to generating subjec-tive or open-ended questions.This paper introduces Questomatic, a novel system that leverages the BERT model, advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools, and a custom randomization algorithm to generate unique, contextually accurate, and diverse questions from input text and this study introduces a stan-dardized method for automated question development based on phrase structure and meaning analysis. Tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, and punctuation are among the activities that are carried out using several NLP libraries, including NLTK and Spacy. Strong NLP tool BERT has also been used in machine translation, named entity identification, sentiment analysis, and other fields. NLP has benefited greatly from BERT's sophisticated capabilities, opening the door for more developments. Natural language processing relies heavily on part-of-speech tagging, which finds the right tags for text. This tagging is used by NLP libraries to efficiently process paragraphs of text. This method can be used to create test questions for educational establish-ments such as universities, coaching facilities, and schools. This technique can also be used by students for self-evaluation, and colleges can utilize it to generate questions for their students.

articleTitle: Bridging Nature and Technology: ResNet-152 for Scene Visualization and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Applications like environmental monitoring, autonomous navigation, and urban planning involve basic computer vision tasks such as classification and visualization of natural scenes. In this work, model offer a deep learning-based method for the categorization and visualization of natural situations using ResNet-152, a potent convolutional neural network architecture. In order to enable the model to learn rich representations of complex natural environments, Article take advantage of ResNet-152's deep layers to extract high-level features from unprocessed image data. approach includes preprocessing a variety of natural scene image datasets and optimizing the already-trained ResNet-152 model to fit our particular classification job. After that, the suggested techniques were used to assess the model's performance on both training and validation datasets using measures including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. It also uses visualization approaches to get insights into the features the model learns and how it makes decisions. The outcomes the experiments show how well our method works for correctly categorizing a variety of natural settings, such as urban landscapes, beaches, mountains, seas and glaciers. In comparison to cutting-edge techniques, the ResNet-152 model performs competitively, demonstrating its ability to handle complicated visual input. With implications for a range of real-world applications, the suggested methodology presents a viable path for comprehending and interpreting natural settings through computer analysis.

articleTitle: A Review on the Identification of Face Mask Object from Multiple Environments Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Deep learning (DL) has revolutionized object detection, making it more accurate even in difficult situations. This review explores the capabilities of modern models and applications designed to detect masked or unmasked objects, especially in adverse conditions such as rain, blur, and changing illumination. We examine the effectiveness of existing deep learning techniques, including new design models such as convolutional neural networks (CNN) Transfer learning, YOLO and more conventional approaches like Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). In order to increase model resilience, we also go over a combination of feature extraction strategies, picture enhancement models Even with great progress, problems including managing various types of noise, detecting real time problems, and enhancing dependability in practical uses still need to be solved. This analysis emphasizes the need for more investigation to improve the accuracy and dependability of detection tools in real-world deployments utilizing both conventional and deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Efficient Distribution Automation Information Integration Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Efficient distribution automation information integration platform is designed and implemented in this study. A comprehensive distribution automation system can perform diverse functions, covering key areas such as substation automation, feeder automation and distribution demand-side management. Inspired by this, the study constructs the efficient distribution automation information integration platform plays a vital role within the smart grid framework to optimize the operation of the distribution automation system. The platform integrates advanced technologies such as relay protection, management control and data transmission to form a unified system that can monitor, respond and manage the grid operation status in real time. Key components include feeder terminal units, distribution terminal units and distribution transformer monitoring terminal units, which support remote data acquisition, system monitoring, fault handling and automatic isolation of fault areas. In particular, the automatic self-healing of abnormal operation modes that will enhance the system robustness is the further innovation of the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Multifaceted Approach to Lung Cancer Diagnosis Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research investigates the application of machine learning techniques for lung cancer prediction. A comprehensive dataset encompassing patient features and risk variables is analyzed to identify significant factors influencing lung cancer prognosis. Multivariate analysis techniques, including pair plots, violin plots, and scatter plots, are employed to explore the complex relationships between variables and their impact on lung cancer development. Three machine learning algorithms-support vector machine (SVM), decision tree, and K-nearest neighbors (KNN)-are evaluated for their predictive power using confusion matrices and ROC curves. Principal component analysis (PCA) is utilized to reduce the dimensionality of the dataset and improve model performance. The study addresses the limitations of existing lung cancer diagnosis systems, focusing on improving early detection accuracy. By leveraging advanced machine learning algorithms, this research aims to contribute to the development of more effective and accurate lung cancer prediction models.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine for Employee Churn Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Employee Churn which is also called employee attrition, is a major problem faced by an organization. We know that employees are the valuable assets of any organization. There is a big challenge in front of the company whenever an employee leaves. For finding the new replacement, the company needs a lot of time. It has to spend money to train a new person. Plus, the new person who is hired usually needs some time to attain good form at their new job and start making money for the company. So, losing employees unexpectedly can be really costly for a company. This research study constructs a novel model to predict Employee Churn rate by using two robust machine learning algorithms: Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine (SVM). The evaluation of the algorithms is done by using a dataset of employee records from a tech company. The study found that both the SVM and Logistic Regression algorithms performed well in predicting Employee Churn. The Logistic Regression algorithm achieved an accuracy of 87.52%, while Support Vector Machine had a slightly lower accuracy of 87.07<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. Hence, the study concludes that the most reliable and accurate model to predict Employee Churn rate is Logistic Regression.

articleTitle: Diabetic Prediction with Significant Factors by Random Forest-A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Diabetes is a major disease that is prevalent in an individual throughout one's life if once occurred. Unhealthy lifestyle and food habits are the main reasons, among others, to be affected by this disease. This paper is predicting diabetes for individuals by machine learning algorithm. A Random Forest (RF) classifier is employed to predict a diabetic patient on the basis of p-value and chi-value. For this study, 520 samples from Sylhet Diabetic Hospital were analyzed to predict whether a person is diabetic or non-diabetic. More than 98% accuracy is found in this study. Some factors are found that are highly significant and are responsible for diabetes diseases.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement Using Color Balance and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Low contrast images pose challenges in various applications, from surveillance to medical imaging. In this paper, an image enhancement scheme is proposed that combines Color Balance and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) techniques to address this issue. This approach aims to improve both visual quality and quantitative metrics such as entropy and average gradient. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is evaluated on a dataset of low contrast images and the results are compared with existing enhancement methods. The visual quality assessment, along with objective metrics, demonstrates the significant enhancement achieved by our approach, making it a promising solution for improving the usability of low contrast images in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Novel Deep Learning Approaches for Automated Taxonomic Identification of Plant Species of the Western Ghats Region
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study introduces two innovative deep learning models inspired by convolutional neural networks, designed to identify various plant species based on the unique characteristics of their leaves. Additionally, the paper discusses the development of a new dataset specifically for plants native to the Western Ghats region. The models draw inspiration from pre-trained architectures like VGG16 and AlexNet. A comparative analysis of the performance of these methods is also provided.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Exploration of Data Security Techniques Using Image Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Steganography, the practice of concealing information within digital media, has seen significant advancements through various tools like Steghide, OpenPuff, and OpenStego. However, the effectiveness and robustness of these tools in resisting steganalysis remain critical challenges. This work investigates the application of advanced steganalysis algorithms, including Shannon Entropy, Gaussian Mixture Model, Scale-Invariant Feature Transform, and Spatial Rich Model, using the Python ecosystem. A comparison of these algorithms with pre-existing tools is conducted to highlight the gaps in current methodologies. The proposed approach integrates deep learning techniques such as Simple CNN, Batch Normalization, and ResNetlOl to enhance accuracy and reduce loss in steganography.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enabled Robotic Trash Collector
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: India, being a holy country, experiences significant water pollution during festivals such as Ganpati-Visarjan, Navratri, and Durga Puja due to the disposal of waste into nearby water bodies. This pollution poses a serious threat to aquatic life. To address this challenge, this research presents the design and construction of a Machine Learning-enabled Robotic Trash Collector (MLRTC) that can remove floating trash from river banks, lakes, or ponds. The MLRTC is specifically designed to collect surface-level garbage, particularly non-biodegradable waste such as plastics that predominantly float on water bodies. The system integrates an onboard webcam, a Bluetooth sensor module for controlling, YOLOv3 algorithm for object detection, a motor driver for enhanced power output and precise control, and sunboard foam sheet for the prototype's construction. Some major challenges that we have faced while working on this robot are: first, the robot's reliance on solar power that is it may face difficulties in rainy or low light conditions. Over time, batteries may degrade and lose capacity, reducing the robot's lifespan and efficiency. Lakes can have unpredictable water conditions like waves or high currents which can affect the robot's stability. Also, there are obstacles like rocks and aquatic animals and therefore the robot needs to have reliable sensors to detect these obstacles in real-time. Even with automation, some human intervention is maintenance and empty debris collection units. The inclusion of the webcam and YOLOv3 algorithm enhances the robot's capability to detect and navigate around obstacles efficiently. The paper outlines the design, construction, and preliminary testing of the MLR TC, showcasing its potential for broader applications beyond simple pool cleaning. The integration of these technologies underscores the effectiveness of AI -driven robotic systems in combating environmental pollution, thereby contributing to sustainable waste management practices.

Author Keywords: MLRTC(Machine Learning enabled Robotic Trash Collector)

articleTitle: Enhancing Natural Language Processing: A Comprehensive Review of Retrieval Augmented Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising approach in natural language processing, combining retrieval and generation techniques to produce high-quality text. By incorporating external knowledge into the generation process, RAG addresses the limitations of generative models that rely solely on learned information. This review explores the foundational principles and architecture of RAG, which typically involves a two-step process: retrieving relevant information based on the input query and generating text informed by both the query and the retrieved knowledge. The review discusses key considerations for the retriever and generator components, as well as the integration of retrieved knowledge into the generative model. By understanding the underlying principles and architecture of RAG, researchers and practitioners can leverage this powerful technique to improve the quality and contextual relevance of text generation tasks.

articleTitle: Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Titanic Disaster Survival Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research investigates the factors that influenced survival rates among passengers on the Titanic, utilizing machine learning algorithms to analyze a dataset of 891 individuals. By examining attributes such as Age, Passenger class, Sex, Name, Embarked, and Fare, the study aims to identify correlations that may have contributed to higher survival probabilities. Various machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, CatBoost, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and Linear SVM, were implemented and evaluated on the dataset. The results demonstrate that the CatBoost algorithm outperformed the others, achieving the highest accuracy rate of 78.41<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>/0. Additionally, CatBoost exhibited superior performance in terms of True Positive and False Negative values, indicating its effectiveness in predicting survival. This research provides valuable insights into the factors that influenced survival on the Titanic and contributes to the understanding of historical events through the application of machine learning techniques.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Control Strategy for Power Management in a Grid Interactive Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Distributed Generators (DG) are the formation of multi-source micro grid in a single architecture. The DGs are designed to regulate the voltage, current and frequency as per to the power requirement observed from the load terminals. The design of an optimum control strategy will improve the performance of the DG to certain extent. The proposed work forms a DG control system in a Matlab/Simulink simulation setup with PV, fuel cell (PEMFC) and Ultra-Capacitor for providing a reliable and regulated output to a power grid. The PV system employed in the work is equipped with an MPPT algorithm for supplying maximum power to the connected system. Also to overcome the intermittent nature of the PV cells, the work employs an ultra-capacitor and PEMFC. The ultra- capacitor regulates the output by addressing against the thermodynamic effect of the PEMFC. The system has a control strategy with a power electronic based interfacing circuit along with controller setups for maintaining the power quality. Hence the permitted voltage and frequency level of the grid system is maintained by the DG.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Road Lane Monitoring System using Computer Vision Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Autonomous system that takes live feed from camera and processes images to detect lanes and collision possibilities such as people/animals coming in front., objects flying towards the vehicle etc. Direction and speed of objects relative to motion of vehicle is the main process being applied. Confusion matrix is used as the base for analysis of the model. First., the images of the road are taken and then lane lines are identified. Emotions from the face maybe used to judge the mentality of the pedestrians. Shape and movement of objects are used as a base classification for rigid and non-rigid objects. Activities on the sidewalk are identified to judge the randomness of motion of objects and its impact to the lane detection system. In autonomous driving., lane detection and collision avoidance are two primary challenges., especially in non-ideal driving environments such as damaged or missing lanes. This paper proposes a robust real-time lane detection system integrated with an advanced object recognition and anomaly detection model., capable of addressing lane ambiguity., recognizing potential collision threats., and understanding surrounding activities. The system leverages a combination of advanced image processing techniques., object detection models like YOLOv5 (You Only Look Once)., and predictive algorithms for decision-making. This algorithm demonstrates superior efficiency., achieving better accuracy and minimizing errors compared to existing technologies.

articleTitle: Detecting Drowsy Driving Through Eye Closure and Yawning : Azure Custom Vision System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: With growing concerns about road safety, the increasing number of accidents caused by driver drowsiness has become a major issue. This study addresses the detection of drowsy driving by employing deep learning techniques to recognize sleep states in drivers. Azure Custom Vision model is propounded to identify closed eyes in constant facial images of drivers. The proposed approach offers versatile applications such as human-computer interaction design, facial expression recognition, and fatigue detection in drivers. The AZURE Custom Vision utilizes the Convolutional Neural Network VGG16 model with Azure. A dataset is created by capturing the drowsy driving instances and are trained. Our model achieves a total detection accuracy of 99.3%, outperforming other existing algorithms in the field. For instance, RNN achieved an accuracy of 92%, while CNNs reported an accuracy of 96.51%. Compared to these models, our approach demonstrates superior accuracy, leveraging the deep hierarchical feature extraction capabilities of VGG16 to more effectively distinguish between drowsy and wakeful states.

articleTitle: Thermal Management for EV Batteries Using Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Maintaining the battery temperature within safe limits is critical for the performance and longevity of electric vehicles (EVs). Overheating can lead to reduced efficiency, accelerated degradation, and potential safety hazards such as thermal runaway. Effective thermal management ensures the battery remains within an optimal temperature range, balancing performance, safety, and longevity. In proposed work, we developed a temperature monitoring and control system using a Cortex M3 microcontroller to ensure that the battery operates within safe temperature ranges. The system continuously monitors the battery temperature and displays real-time readings on an LCD. If the temperature exceeds a predefined threshold, a DC fan is automatically activated to cool the battery. This method prevents overheating and thermal damage, enhancing the battery's health and efficiency. By integrating this thermal management system into EVs, we improve safety and reliability, reduce the risk of battery fires, and extend the battery's lifespan, resulting in lower replacement costs. This technology supports the increasing adoption of EVs, contributing to environmental sustainability and global efforts to reduce carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Convolutional Neural Networks for EEG Classification in Schizophrenia Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: To identify schizophrenia patients and healthy individuals, the technique classifies EEG data using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Schizophrenia poses tremendous difficulties for diagnosis as it is a complicated mental disorder with sensitive brain signals. Aiming at spotting trends between the two groups, the work trained a CNN model using EEG data. The findings underscored the complex nature of the brain activities of the disorder as the model fought to correctly identify schizophrenic patients even if it categorized healthy controls satisfactorily. Showing slight overfitting but generally good performance, the model displayed has a training accuracy of 62.65% and a validation accuracy of 64.55%. Although the model's sensitivity to schizophrenia patients was more restricted. This work highlights CNN's possibilities in mental health diagnosis as well as problems requiring work in model development and dataset extension. Future research will concentrate on improving the detection of schizophrenia in the model so improving early and accurate diagnosis in clinical environments.

articleTitle: Levelwise Degradation Classification of Ancient Stone Inscriptions Images using MobileNetV2: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach to classify ancient Karnataka stone inscriptions based on degradation levels using deep learning techniques. A custom dataset of 1,748 augmented images from 437 original images categorized into three degradation classes. The methodology employs MobileNetV2 architecture, benchmarked against CNN, ResNet50, and EfficientNet models. Through optimized preprocessing and augmentation techniques, the MobileNetV2-based model achieved 91% classification accuracy, significantly outperforming comparative models. This research offers an efficient, automated tool for assessing inscription conditions, contributing to digital archaeology and cultural heritage preservation. The study demonstrates the efficacy of lightweight deep learning models in historical artifact analysis and provides a foundation for future work in automated conservation strategies.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Agriculture: Detection of Plant Disease using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The threat of plant diseases to global food security highlights the importance of prompt and precise detection. for effective management. Traditional methods are labor-intensive and subjective, prompting the exploration of automated systems. By integrating the advancements in Deep learning and machine learning, this research study investigates the efficacy of algorithms like SVM, Random Forest, CNN, RNN, and ResNet in classifying plant diseases from leaf images. We aim to contribute to enhanced agricultural productivity and food security through automated disease detection.

articleTitle: MindCare: Machine Learning based Personalized Mental Health Monitor
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Mental health challenges are growing in recent years, emphasizing the need for effective monitoring and inter- vention systems. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to detect mental unstabilities by analyzing the text entered by the user. Utilizing a combination of sentiment analysis and machine learning techniques, the proposed system preprocesses text data to extract sentiment scores and other key features, which are then used to train models for accurate mental health assessments. The system also offers personalized recommendations based on the user's mental state. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach, with the model achieving accuracy of 82.31% for negative text classification. These results underscore the potential of the system to serve as a valuable tool in the early detection and management of mental health issues.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Post-Hoc Explainability Methods in AI: LIME, SHAP, and Grad-CAM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study presents a comparative evaluation of three prominent post-hoc explain ability methods: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), and Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping). The evaluation is performed using a simple Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model trained on the MNIST dataset. To achieve high accuracy, the CNN model was optimized through rigorous training and evaluation, reaching a test accuracy of approximately 98%. The evaluation involves applying each method to selected test images and comparing their effectiveness in terms of interpretability and visualization. LIME provides local feature importance by highlighting influential regions in the images, while SHAP offers a model-agnostic perspective with Shapley values that quantify feature contributions. Grad-CAM visualizes class-specific activation maps, showing which parts of the image contribute to predictions This study provides valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of each explainability method, helping practitioners understand their practical applications and choose the most suitable technique based on their specific needs.

articleTitle: Smart Walking Assistance for Visually Impaired People
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Blindness significantly obstructs a person's ability to navigate unfamiliar environments independently, impacting their ability to perform various tasks and responsibilities. Vision impairment is defined as having a visual acuity of 20/200 or worse in the better-seeing eye, even with optimal correction. Individuals with vision impairments rely on external assistance, which can come from people, guide dogs, or advanced technological devices, to make better decisions. To address these challenges, we propose a lightweight device that processes signals and alerts visually impaired individuals to obstacles, potholes, smoke, or water pools using distinct vibrating patterns. Additionally, the device includes a GPS module, enabling users to share their location for enhanced safety and assistance.

articleTitle: Health Genie: An AI-Powered Platform for Personalized Healthcare and Illness Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The proposed model combines modern technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning for predictive purposes. The model provides a novel approach for early disease diagnosis by utilizing machine learning algorithms and analysis, as well as health recommendations and insights into the projected disease. The model uses the frameworks, maintains the user's data, and then makes correct predictions. This paper describes the model's architecture, methodology, operation, and efficiency in detail.

articleTitle: Enhanced Heart Disease Prediction Through Optimized Ensemble Random Forest Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Nowadays, the necessity for precise early detection of heart disease is critical with the conventional methods. However, challenges such as handling imbalanced datasets, ensuring model interpretability, and avoiding overfitting persist in predictive models. This paper assesses the efficacy of various machine learning algorithms by analyzing a vast dataset of cardiovascular health indicators. The approaches employed consist of classifiers such as Logistic Regression, K- Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, Naive Bayes, Decision Trees, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, Stochastic Gradient Descent, and AdaBoost. Finally, these algorithms will be evaluated using performance indicators such as F1-score, ROC curves, DET curves, accuracy, precision, recall, and recall. The results indicated that the Decision Tree and Random Forest classifiers are the most adequate, each achieving an accuracy of 98.54% and near-perfect AUC scores of 0.99 and 1.00, respectively. This comparative analysis highlights the superiority of ensemble learning techniques in making robust predictions, thereby significantly contributing to the early detection and management of heart disease.

articleTitle: Optimizing Feature Selection Process Through Variation Inflation Factor for Air Pollution Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Air pollution, caused by various pollutants such as SO2, NO2, CO, and NH3, poses significant health risks. This research focuses on developing a machine learning-based system for air pollution monitoring and analysis. The system utilizes air quality monitoring stations to measure pollutant levels and calculates the Air Quality Index (AQI) to assess air quality. By comparing pollutant levels with permissible limits, the system can identify potential health risks and trigger necessary precautions. Feature selection techniques, such as Variation Inflation Factor and skewness, are employed to identify the most relevant features for accurate prediction. Weak learner algorithms, including Random Forest, Ada Boost, and Gradient Descent, are evaluated for their effectiveness in air pollution detection. The proposed system provides a valuable tool for monitoring air quality, identifying pollution hotspots, and informing public health interventions. By leveraging machine learning techniques, the system can enhance the accuracy and efficiency of air pollution analysis, contributing to improved air quality and public health.

articleTitle: A Study of Machine Learning Techniques for Predictive Analysis of Suicidal Tendency Across Different Age Groups
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Suicide is a serious public health concern, and life-saving early identification and prevention are essential. When it comes to forecasting suicide, risk based on a variety of criteria and signs, machine learning algorithms have shown encouraging results in recent years. This study uses machine learning techniques to predict suicide tendencies in various age groups. The first step in the research is to collect pertinent datasets including sociodemographic, clinical, behavioral, and psychiatric data on people who have attempted or succeeded in suicide. Preprocessing is done on these datasets to guarantee data quality, handle missing values, and normalize characteristics. Using evaluation measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, the best performing models are chosen to serve as the best suicide prediction classifiers. The findings show that suicide risk may be accurately, sensitively, and specifically predicted using machine learning techniques. With the help of the found predictive traits, at-risk people may get personalized treatments and support networks, as well as insights into the risk factors linked to suicide conduct. This study uses five different algorithms, wherein the support vector machine (SVM) emerges as the technique that performs the best, offering an accuracy of 0.89. The decision tree classifier comes as a close second, delivering the same accuracy. Following that, random forest obtains an accuracy of 0.84, KNN comes in second with 0.81, and gaussian naive bayes comes in third with 0.53.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Different YOLO Models for Real-Time Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Object detection in real-life applications plays a significant role, with advancements in technology enabling enhanced image classification and processing, reducing manual effort and increasing accuracy and speed. The proposed work involves a comparative analysis and hyper-parameterization of YOLO (You Only Look Once) modules, specifically YOLOv7, YOLOv8, and YOLOv9 models. These models utilise Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to process image layers by dividing images into boxes and then segmenting them into pixels for identification and classification based on various parameters. Initially applied to the COCO dataset, these models were further tested on customised datasets. Among the three, YOLOv9 demonstrates superior performance, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 52 at 0.5:0.95, compared to YOLOv7 and YOLOv8, which achieved mAPs of 35.2 and 39, respectively. Overall, YOLOv9 significantly reduces parameter usage and improves accuracy.

articleTitle: Automatic Irrigation and Crop Monitoring using Machine Learning and Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The Crop environmental monitoring system with intelligence multidimensional and multi-angle crop environment monitoring system is created to satisfy the demands of contemporary society for agricultural crop environmental monitoring. The system gathers, processes, and forwards data to the network module by connecting the appropriate data gathering sensors. Ultimately, the data is sent to the information processing center for accurate processing and analysis before being visually displayed. Ultimately, the system's ability to achieve the desired result, have a high application value, and effectively increase agricultural environment surveillance efficiency is fully demonstrated by the testing and verification of its operation. Low-cost intelligent modules for smart irrigation systems powered by IoT and AI In India, agriculture is the primary source of income for the majority of people. It is essential to use cutting edge technologies to safeguard priceless water supplies. In addition to serving as Industry 4.0's cornerstone, IoT improves smart agriculture. The goal of the research is to develop a cutting-edge, affordable system for intelligent irrigation. Self-talk and inter-device networking are made possible by IoT.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach using Machine Learning and NLP for Revolutionizing Pali Manuscript Conservation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The preservation and analysis of ancient Pali manuscripts are crucial for understanding India's cultural heritage. However, the unique shapes of Pali characters present significant challenges for accurate identification and classification. This research proposes a novel system that utilizes machine learning, image processing, and natural language processing (NLP) to convert Pali characters into understandable formats and decipher the Pali Prakrit language. By combining computer science and linguistics, the proposed model aims to effectively extract data from Pali literature. The proposed model was validated using the Government of India dataset, demonstrating improved character recognition accuracy and reduced memory footprint. This research contributes to the preservation of ancient Pali manuscripts and facilitates the study and understanding of this valuable cultural heritage.

articleTitle: Advanced Dual Module Weapon Detection for Public Safety and Surveillance System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research presents a novel weapon detection system that combines state-of-the-art technologies for enhanced security. The system integrates a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for precise image-based weapon classification and the YOLO algorithm for real-time detection in live camera feeds. The proposed system generates email alerts to promptly inform users of detected weapons, enabling timely action to mitigate risks. By combining these advanced modules, the proposed system offers an effective solution for addressing weapon-related violence and improving security measures in various environments.

articleTitle: Simhasth 2016 Feedback Dataset: A Domain Specific Sentiment Analysis Dataset and its Baseline Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a very important task in Natural Language Processing. Sentiment analysis is intended to find the emotion or feedback given in some review or text. Sentiment analysis is intensively explored in resource-rich languages like English, but for languages like Hindi there are only few resources for sentiment analysis studies. Here, a novel dataset for sentiment analysis in Hindi language is introduced, created from feedback on Simhasth 2016. Simhasth is a very important and huge spiritual and religious gathering of Hindu religious fellows held in Ujjain city of Madhya Pradesh in India. We collected feedback on the arrangements and experiences of visitors of Simhasth 2016. Feedbacks were originally collected as text on feedback paper sheets, then feedback texts were digitized as a feedback dataset. From this feedback dataset, after annotation and class balancing, we finally got the proposed dataset. We also performed some baseline performance evaluations on the dataset and compared various machine learning techniques for sentiment analysis. We used various machine learning techniques for evaluation. This feedback dataset has almost all feedback in Hindi. The dataset is now available as a resource for sentiment analysis in the Hindi language<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>.

articleTitle: MAC Address Spoofing and its Impact on Network Security
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research investigates the technique of MAC address spoofing, which allows users to bypass network restrictions by changing the unique identifier associated with their device's network interface. This research study aims to explore the methods and motivations behind MAC address spoofing attempts and assess their potential impact on network security. Here, participants are asked to provide the URL of the target web application and the desired MAC address to be spoofed. The application launches the browser with the modified MAC address, enabling the user to attempt to access the restricted application. The study's objectives include promoting responsible digital use, understanding the consequences of MAC address spoofing, and addressing the evolving security challenges in the digital age. By gaining insights into the techniques and motivations behind MAC address spoofing, this research contributes to enhancing network security and promoting responsible online behavior.

articleTitle: A Smart Waste Management System Using ESP8266
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study presents a comprehensive smart waste management system designed to enhance collection efficiency and sustainability through the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. Key components include ultrasonic sensors for detecting waste bin fill levels, soil moisture sensors for monitoring waste composition, and the ESP8266 Wi-Fi module for real- time data transmission. The system offers continuous real-time monitoring and analytics, allowing waste management authorities to dynamically adjust collection routes based on actual waste levels. This optimization reduces operational costs by minimizing unnecessary collection trips, decreasing fuel consumption, and lowering vehicle wear and tear. Additionally, the system enhances waste segregation and recycling processes, promoting a circular economy and reducing landfill waste. Beyond operational benefits, the system contributes to environmental sustain ability by reducing greenhouse gas emissions associated with waste collection and disposal. It also improves public health by preventing overfilled bins and related hazards. This paper details the design, implementation, and advantages of this innovative IoT -based waste management system, highlighting its potential to transform traditional waste management practices.

articleTitle: Educational Intelligent Chat Bot for Von Willebrand Disease Among Senegalese People
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Von Willebrand disease (VWD) is a blood disorder caused by a protein deficiency that prevents blood from clotting properly. The challenge faced by people with Von Willebrand disease is having access to limited information, users frequently believe they do not have access to all the information they require to manage their condition. The lack of technological literacy could make it difficult for them to interact efficiently and the language barrier is the biggest concern. The model of an educational intelligent chatbot for patients with Von Willebrand seeks to close information gaps and literacy, especially among Senegalese people. This chatbot uses voice recognition and machine learning to deliver accurate, culturally appropriate information in an approachable manner. This cutting-edge solution, which provides trustworthy instructional resources in a safe digital setting, is expected to greatly improve hemophilia sufferers' quality of life and ability to manage their condition with an emphasis on Senegalese people in particular, the creation of an Educational Intelligent Chatbot for Von Willebrand Patients tackles the urgent need for improved knowledge and education regarding Von- Willebrand. This sophisticated chatbot uses the most recent advancements in machine learning and speech recognition to provide accurate, culturally appropriate information in an interesting and approachable manner.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis for Multiple Disease Identification using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The availability of diverse health data, including medical records, genetic information, and lifestyle details, presents an opportunity to gain a comprehensive understanding of individual health profiles and disease risks. However, effectively integrating these disparate data sources remains a significant challenge. This study proposes a novel approach to address this challenge by combining deep learning techniques and ensemble methods. The proposed model is capable of simultaneously predicting an individual's risks for a range of major chronic and acute diseases, including cardiovascular disease, cancers, diabetes, and more. By integrating advanced machine learning techniques, the model can effectively integrate structured and unstructured data, capturing the complex relationships between different data types and disease outcomes. This approach enables early disease detection and facilitates timely intervention, leading to improved patient outcomes. The study highlights the importance of combining diverse data sources and employing machine learning techniques to develop accurate and comprehensive predictive models for multi-disease risk assessment. This research contributes to the advancement of personalized healthcare and preventive medicine.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Waste Fire Pollution Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The increasing occurrences of waste fires poses a significant environmental threat, deteriorating air quality and increasing global pollution levels. This research focuses on developing an advanced IoT-enabled device to detect waste fires and analyze the concentration of gases released during combustion. The primary goal is to predict the extent of pollution caused by waste fires in specific localities, providing real-time data monitoring. Given the critical nature of increasing pollution as a global issue, waste fires are substantial contributors. The IoT device is strategically deployed in fire-prone areas, continuously monitoring concentrations of key air pollutants such as CO, CO2, CH4, and PM2.5. The collected data undergoes comprehensive analysis to forecast potential pollution increases, with accuracy validated by nearby Air Quality Monitoring (AQM) stations. Using ARCGIS software, the data is mapped to provide a visual context for pollution levels, significantly enhancing the clarity and efficacy of the research findings. This integration aids in understanding the geographical distribution of pollution and serves as a valuable visual tool for conveying the extent of pollution in different locations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis on a Diabetic Disease Prediction Considering Various Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Diabetes is a serious health concern almost all over the countries as it impaired many organs in human body and rate of affected person is gradually increasing. Several significant factors have been incorporated for prediction of diabetic diseases through the machine learning attribute. In this study a non-communicable disease, diabetes, is predicted based on several machine learning approaches like Support vector machine (SVM), Decision tree (DT), Logistic regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Gaussian Naive Byes(GNB),Random Forest(RF). Data set of Sylhet Diabetic Hospital, Sylhet in Bangladesh containing 520 samples is collected from online source. Comparing the classifiers SVM shows the maximum accuracy 99%. Since a diabetic patient suffers immensely throughout the life, diagnosis along with proper medication is important.

articleTitle: Enhancing Three-Dimensional Human Digitization using Multi-Layer Pixel Alignment for High- Resolution Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research explores the application of neural networks to improve the resolution of 3D human images. While existing methods have focused on real-time applications, they often fall short in reconstructing high-resolution 3D images due to memory limitations. The proposed approach introduces a multi-layer architecture that supports end-to-end training, enabling it to focus on fine-level geometry details rather than coarse-level details commonly used in lower-resolution images. This innovative strategy results in significantly improved 3D image reconstruction quality. By addressing the challenges associated with high-resolution 3D image generation, this research contributes to advancements in various fields that rely on accurate and detailed human representations.

articleTitle: Vineyard Vision: Investigating Mask R -CNN and YOLOv8 for Grapevine Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Grapes whether as a fruit berry, wine, or raisins, are celebrated all around the world. Mostly characterized by a small round or oval shape, green to deep red color, and juicy pulp, grapes are the berries that extend their popularity from some of the well-known ancient cultures to the modern-day globalized world. This leads to grapes being grown in large quantities in vineyards with grape bunches distributed and spread across the field. Locating and monitoring these grape bunches is a very time-consuming and hectic task and requires a lot of human effort. The presented work endeavors to find an automated solution with the help of computer vision, utilizing instance segmentation and masking. The study delves into the two esteemed object detection and segmentation models, namely Mask R-CNN and YOLOv8, to identify the optimal model for the task. Comparing the two on accuracy, precision, and time, YOLOv8 with mAP 88%, takes the upper hand over Mask R-CNN with mAP 86% and establishes itself as a better reliable option for image segmentation in yards.

articleTitle: Integrating Safety and Security in Autonomous Vehicles: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Integrating safety and security in autonomous vehicles (AVs) is a critical concern as these technologies evolve towards widespread adoption. Robust systems must equip AVs to ensure operational reliability (safety) and protect against internal and external threats (security). This paper provides a comprehensive review of current methodologies for integrating safety and security in AVs, emphasizing the interdependent nature of these two aspects. We explore various collaborative frameworks that combine safety and security assessments, highlighting their effectiveness in providing a holistic view of vehicle resilience. Key areas of focus include advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for real-time threat detection and mitigation, the enhancement of digital twin technology for extensive simulation and validation, and the development of unified standards that harmonize safety and secu-rity requirements globally. Additionally, we compare traditional versus integrated approaches in AV development, underscoring the advantages of integrated methodologies. Future research directions are identified, including leveraging AI and ML for adaptive security solutions, enhancing digital twin capabilities, and fostering collaborative efforts among industry stakeholders, regulatory bodies, and academia. By addressing these aspects comprehensively, we aim to provide a roadmap for developing AV systems that are both safe and secure, ensuring their reliable operation in real-world environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Credit Card Fraud Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: A major issue of concern in the financial sector, credit card fraud puts risks to financial institutions as well as consumers. Machine learning methods have become rather successful instruments for spotting fraudulent transactions in recent years. This work compares the detection of credit card fraud employing two well-known machine learning techniques: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and XGBoost. With a publicly available credit card transaction dataset, this work evaluates the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of these algorithms. Furthermore taken into consideration to evaluate their fit for real-time fraud detection systems are the computational efficiency and scalability of ANNs and XGBoost. Among the five suggested methods, ANN shows best with an accuracy of 96.9%; among the classifiers, XGBoost shows best with an accuracy of 92.7%. The findings give financial institutions trying to install or enhance fraud detection systems direction as well as insights on the strengths and constraints of every method. This study supports the continuous initiatives to improve financial security by means of advanced machine learning approaches and fight credit card fraud.

articleTitle: AwGhO_Res_Trans: Adaptive Weighting Grasshopper Optimization-Based Residual Transformer for Autism Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In this model, input data is acquired from publicly available datasets and converted into a normalized form using the Min-Max normalization approach. The Pre-processing based on normalization is employed to scale the data within a specific range to reduce complexity. Following normalization, the most relevant features are selected using the Wrapper Feature Selection Model, which iteratively evaluates and selects appropriate features that enhance Autism detection accuracy. Finally, Autism detection is devised using the proposed Adaptive Weighting Grasshopper Optimization Residual Transformer (AwGhO_Res_Trans) model. The designed model demonstrated enhanced outcomes compared to the baseline models in Autism detection.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cloud Intrusion Detection Using Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The broad adoption of cloud computing (CC) as a new technology offering on-demand networked access to shared configurable computer resources has resulted in an increased need for data storage and service management. But at the same time, CC also opens up further vulnerabilities by throwing issues such as insider threats, data breaches and unauthorized access into the mix. The study suggests this mechanism as a cloud-based intrusion detection technique made up of optimization and machine learning algorithms that mitigate these issues. In the beginning, an input noiseless training data undergoes a Gaussian filter to improve the quality of data and remove any background noise. In this step, Random Forest Recursive feature elimination is used to select significant low-dimensional features with the help of correlation-based feature selector. Implemented on the Python platform using the CICIDS-2019 dataset, the proposed method's accuracy is validated and evaluated against various criteria, demonstrating superior performance compared to recent related studies and effectively enhancing intrusion detection in cloud computing.

articleTitle: Exploring Performance Characteristics of Static and Dynamic CMOS Designs Using Cadence Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In VLSI design, trade-offs between performance factors such as speed, power, and area are common. Using Cadence technologies, this research article offers a thorough investigation of the performance variations between static and dynamic CMOS systems. It draws attention to the trade-offs between power efficiency, speed, and area, with dynamic CMOS circuits providing quicker speeds and static CMOS circuits excelling in low power usage. Using simulations in Cadence, the study examines a variety of logic circuits, such as pseudo-NMOS, ratioed circuits, and domino logic, examining their power and latency characteristics. The high power dissipation of pseudo-NMOS inverters and the lower power but higher delay of Domino Logic inverters are important discoveries that highlight the significance of selecting the appropriate logic type depending on application requirements. The study emphasizes how useful Cadence tools are for maximizing the performance of CMOS circuits and offers vital information for contemporary VLSI design.

articleTitle: An Application of Deep Learning Techniques in Trajectory Planning of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research explores trajectory planning for Autonomous Vehicles, with a focus on optimizing routes for energy efficiency, safety, and regulatory compliance. Autonomous Vehicles utilize sensors, maps, and real-time traffic data to navigate dynamic and static obstacles, ensuring the safety of all road users. Collaborative planning, enabled by vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle- to-infrastructure communication, is emerging as a crucial aspect of autonomous vehicles development, promising to enhance traffic flow and efficiency. The study examines various machine learning techniques, particularly deep learning and reinforcement learning, employed to improve the quality and safety of autonomous vehicles trajectory planning. These techniques enable autonomous vehicles to learn from human driving behaviors, adapt to complex environments, and optimize navigation strategies. Moreover, the study highlights the significant advancements and future potential of deep learning and reinforcement learning in creating more efficient, safe, and reliable autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Deep Belief Network-based Decentralized Secure, Lightweight Data Auditing Scheme for Streaming Outsourcing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: A cloud storage environment is an emerging paradigm that provides storage services to various user categories to outsource their data. The multi-tenancy nature of cloud data storage leads to multiple security concerns like data breaches and unauthorized data access. The cloud user must outsource their private data to the cloud server. To mitigate those challenges and enhance data integrity in the multi-tenancy cloud environment, various researchers have designed and implemented many secure auditing schemes to ensure the data integrity of their outsourced data. However, these architectures often struggle with computation overhead and managing the data integrity verification among the streaming outsourcing data at runtime. They are also less capable of block-based audits due to improper data auditing structures. In this context, the proposed Decentralized lightweight data integrity verifying model for secure auditing of the streaming of outsourced data, implemented using a deep belief network, offers significant benefits. It secures the data on various layers of the neural network, constructs the feature map to compute the duplicate of the data, and enhances the attacker's data integrity and identity traceability to attain user revocation. The model's hidden layer efficiently processes the dynamic cloud data on insert, delete and update operations with less computation cost and time. It can eliminate duplication of data extracted from cloud databases. These features of our model significantly enhance data integrity and security, providing a robust solution for cloud data storage.

articleTitle: Improving Healthcare with Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Due to the evolving lifestyle choices and the state of the environment, people nowadays suffer from a wide range of ailments. Consequently, early illness prediction becomes a critical obligation. For doctors, however, making a meaningful prognosis based only on symptoms becomes too difficult. Predicting illness correctly is the hardest problem. ML is crucial in helping to anticipate illnesses and find treatments in order to solve this issue. Using disease data, MRIs, chest X-rays, and diabetes records, machine learning (ML) assists in diagnosing and treating various conditions. Given the patient's symptoms, we utilize techniques such as SVM, Decision Trees, Random Forest Classifier, Gaussian Bayes and Multinomial Bayes, and Gradient Boost to predict illnesses. Given an X-ray image, we employ CNN models such as VGG for image classification with transfer learning to predict if a person has tuberculosis, pneumonia, or is disease-free. Brain MRIs (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) can be used to predict brain tumors. With the aid of Support Vector Machines, we are able to forecast if the patient has a pituitary tumor, meningioma, glioma, or no tumor at all (SVM). Diabetes is predicted using a number of important variables, including age and body mass index (BMI). Random forest classifiers are what we use to determine if a person has diabetes or not.

articleTitle: Smart Solar Water Pumping: ANN-Enhanced MPPT System for Optimized Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In photovoltaic (PV) water pump systems, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controllers play a critical role due to the nonlinear IV characteristics of PV systems and the variability of their maximum power point with solar irradiation. These controllers ensure that the PV array operates at its highest power point under varying lighting conditions, thereby maximizing solar energy conversion. This study proposes an MPPT technique based on artificial neural networks (ANN) for brushless direct current (BLDC) motors powered by photovoltaics. The system comprises a solar array, a buck-boost converter, a three-phase voltage source inverter, and a BLDC motor. The proposed ANN controller generates a pulse width modulated (PWM) control signal to adjust the operational duty cycle of the buck-boost converter to the load, utilizing the output power of the PV array and the rotational speed of the DC motor as input signals. The ANN controller dynamically adjusts the internal and PV generator impedance to increase the engine speed, ensuring efficient operation across various solar irradiance levels. A comprehensive simulation of the system was conducted using MATLAB (R2022B)/SIMULINK to demonstrate the effectiveness of the ANN control strategy under different solar conditions.

articleTitle: IoT Based Forest Monitoring to Detect Illegal Logging & Fire Risks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Recently in the forest there is satellite based fire detection technique has been used which is unable to detect small fires. For illegal logging forest department don't have any system that is going to detect real-time forest fires on time instead of that they are using manpower that can do that. This study investigates the use of Internet of Things (IoT) technology in sophisticated forest fire and illicit logging detection systems. We suggest an Internet of Things (IoT)-based system that combines machine learning and ground sensors to improve early detection accuracy and reaction times for forest fires. 10T-enabled sensors give real-time data and continuously monitor the surrounding environment, enabling quick diagnosis and intervention to reduce fire damage. The study intends to improve forest conservation and management by utilizing IoT technology and tackling pressing environmental issues with creative and scalable solutions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Internet of Things based Medication Dispenser Reminder and Drug Expiration Health Monitoring and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The Internet of Things(IoT)Powered transportable medicine box the relentless demands of modern life, in addition to the difficulties presented by aging and a range of illnesses, frequently prompt people to establish regular habits in order to preserve their well-being. This is a common reality that affects a wide range of demographics, including businesspeople, housewives, children, teachers, and students. As these individuals manage busy schedules and responsibilities, they unavoidably put their health at danger. The envisioned system consists of an intelligent medication box equipped with sensors for health monitoring and diagnostics, as part of a sophisticated healthcare IoT platform. Patients and medical professionals can communicate more easily with this smart medicine box for the home thanks to the blynk app and Wi-Fi connectivity. Through frequent reminders, the technology ensures that patients take their pills on schedule. Using internet connectivity, the intelligent medicine box notifies the patient's caregiver in real time about the status of their pills on their smartphone.

articleTitle: Enriched Vitiligo Detection using ML and DL Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The loss of melanocytes caused by the chronic autoimmune disease vitiligo leads in depigmented patches of skin that are frequently hard to distinguish from other hypopigmented disorders. Effective therapy depends on early and precise detection, but the diagnostic techniques used today are very difficult. Modern machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques created for vitiligo detection and classification are reviewed and analyzed in this comprehensive work. Some the difficulties faced by deep learning models are overfitting, generalization, and poor data quality. Trust and interpretability are essential for therapeutic acceptance. Real-time processing and high computing requirements raise ethical and privacy issues. With a particular emphasis on distinguishing vitiligo from disorders that resemble scars, we investigate alternative convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning methods that have been employed in previous research.

articleTitle: Analysis of Neural Machine Translation for English to Hindi using Long Short-Term Memory Model and Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: By providing enhanced accuracy and fluency compared to traditional approaches, Neural Machine Translation (NMT) has transformed the area of machine translation. In this research paper, the specific task of translating English to Hindi using NMT techniques is discussed. Creation and assessment of NMT systems developed for this language pair, considering the linguistic complexities and cultural aspects inherent in English and Hindi is examined. Leveraging large-scale parallel corpora and advanced neural network architectures, this work proposes novel approaches to improve translation quality and efficiency. Experimental results evaluated using standard metrics such as BLEU score, shows the efficacy of the proposed NMT models in accurately capturing the semantics and preserving the naturalness of the translated text. Additionally, this study discusses the implications of findings for cross-language communication and access to information, particularly in the context of the growing importance of Hindi in a globalized digital domain. Overall, this research contributes to develop neural machine translation for English to Hindi to a higher level and highlights the potential of NMT in facilitating multilingual communication and knowledge dissemination.

articleTitle: Enhancing Liver Cancer Detection with AI-Powered Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This project aims to identify liver tumors using deep learning techniques. The core of our approach is a sophisticated neural network trained on real CT scans of patients with liver tumors. By leveraging advanced signal-processing algorithms and deep learning models, our AI method accurately distinguishes between tumors and healthy liver tissue. Accurate identification of liver tumors on CT images is crucial for planning effective radiation therapy. CT and MRI scans provide detailed images of the internal structure of the body by analyzing tissues. Our primary objective is to develop an AI-driven neural network that can reliably identify liver tumors in these images. Given the variability in liver location among individuals, our approach employs specific techniques to ensure precision. Using U-net technology, our goal is to enhance the speed and accuracy of tumor identification, thereby improving patient access to timely and accurate diagnoses. This project underscores the significant potential of deep learning applications in health care.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Breakthroughs in Leukemia Diagnosis: A Review of White Blood Cell Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: One of the most common and deadly forms of cancer is blood cancer. White blood cells (WBC) are produced abnormally and uncontrollably in the bone marrow at the start of leukaemia, a blood cancer. An effective cancer cure is more likely when leukemia is identified and treated early. Red and white blood cell counts (RBC counts) are one way to determine leukemia. A haemocytometer is used in the traditional way to count the number of red blood cells and white blood cells. These tests are lengthy and complex, so there's a chance they won't be correctly classified. Image processing of microscopic photos is another possible tactic for enhancing cancer cell identification because of the circuitry's simplicity. Despite the fact that cancer cells have been identified, the researchers' inability to simultaneously take into account all relevant factors, such as image identification, noise reduction, and image enhancement, casts doubt on the accuracy of their findings. The primary objective of this study is to develop a new system that can incorporate all of the aforementioned elements. Image acquisition, pre-processing, picture segmentation, edge detection, and feature extraction are among the process's numerous phases. These steps can be used to determine whether cancer is present and how far along it is. We now know more about how to measure WBCs and RBCs in blood samples, as well as their typical sizes and regularity or irregularity. The diagnosis of cancer is one potential application for this data.

articleTitle: Brain Stroke Prediction Using Logistic Regression with Logarithmic Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Stroke poses a significant burden on individuals and healthcare systems globally, highlighting the crucial need for timely identification and prediction of stroke risk factors. Predictive modelling through data science offers a promising approach for enhancing our understanding of stroke risk factors and improving the accuracy of stroke prediction. This research focuses on binary classification outcomes, with logistic regression emerging as a potential solution to address the challenges of stroke prediction in healthcare. By emphasizing data-driven methods to identify individuals at higher risk, stroke prediction has the capacity to reform healthcare by facilitating early intervention and personalized preventive measures. Logarithmic transformations of non-linear features are performed in model to improve binary prediction accuracy. The modified model performs better with an AUC value of 0.92 as compared to the basic model with an AUC value 0.91.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Trends in Future Prospect Analyzed by XGBoost- A Time Series Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study investigates the renewable energy perspective for the future generation prompt analysis using the time series model XGBoost. This is very important analysis to harness the power in renewable energy sector, since the fuel energy crisis is increasing rapidly throughout the world. A successful mentor in prediction of renewable energy prompt can mitigate the world energy crisis in near future. From the model analysis, it is found that the maximum renewable energy produced in Romania is 6645 MW where total maximum energy production is 9886 MW. From this scenario it is obvious that the renewable energy is a promising field to harness more power from this sector. The minimum renewable energy production recorded is 2862.420378 MW with a standard deviation of 904.584233 MW on the basis of last 5.5 years of data. This paper tries to present a graphical view of future generation of the renewable energy based on the previous data analysis with minimum RMSE value recorded as 308.45757 for validation data set.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Deep Learning Models for Efficient Sugarcane Leaf Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study explores the application of deep learning techniques to identify and classify the health status of sugarcane leaves, focusing on three categories: healthy, rust, and yellow leaf disease. A convolutional neural network (CNN) was developed and trained on a dataset of sugarcane leaf images, achieving an accuracy of 97%. The model's performance was compared with traditional machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), which achieved accuracies of 95% and 90%, respectively. The CNN model's superior accuracy underscores its effectiveness in disease prediction and classification, offering a valuable tool for farmers to manage sugarcane crop health. The study suggests future work to further refine the model by experimenting with various learning rates, optimizers, and additional models to enhance predictive performance.

articleTitle: Post-Exploitation Insights: Dynamic Analysis of C2 Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Recognizing and reducing the risks presented by malevolent actors in the realm of cyber security requires an awareness of post exploitation techniques. However, deThe study investigates post operational challenges through a dynamic analysis of command-and-control frameworks (C2) fenders are finding it difficult to keep up with the rapid development of C2 frameworks. Using the MITRE ATT&CK framework as a guide, this study explores a popular C2 server: Metasploit. Through extensive research, deployment, and exploitation in a controlled environment, the strengths and weaknesses of each framework are assessed. Key metrics such as ease of installation, performance, security features, and community support are carefully researched to provide comprehensive insights. In addition, the project explores future frontiers by identifying potential modules that can enhance the capabilities of the selected C2 framework. By offering a detailed analysis, this study helps to understand the importance of the C2 frameworks in cyber security and provides valuable insights for security practitioners and researchers.

articleTitle: Advancing Skin Cancer Detection: Leveraging Deep Learning for Early Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research presents a novel approach for early skin cancer detection using a deep learning model based on DenseNet 201. The study utilizes the ISIC dataset, consisting of 1900 normal and 1597 cancerous images, to train and evaluate the model. The proposed methodology involves data loading, categorical labeling, normalization, and model building using Keras with TensorFlow backend. The balanced composition of the dataset ensures accurate evaluation, resulting in an impressive accuracy of 92.8%. The research highlights the significance of early skin cancer detection and the potential of deep learning models to improve diagnostic accuracy. The integration of DenseNet 201 demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in classifying skin cancer images.

articleTitle: Evaluating Disease Prognosis in Hospital Readmission Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study investigates the prognostic value of cardiac disease, Body Mass Index (BMI), diabetes, and hypertension in relation to hospital readmissions. The study aims to develop predictive models that can identify high-risk individuals and reduce the financial burden associated with readmissions. This study is conducted using electronic health records of individuals with a history of hypertension, heart disease, or both. The relationship between these factors and hospital readmissions within post-discharge was analyzed using ensemble learning techniques. The findings demonstrate that elevated BMI and glucose levels are significant predictors of hospital readmissions, independent of hypertension and cardiac disease status. These results highlight the importance of addressing these factors in preventing readmissions and improving patient outcomes. This research contributes to the development of effective strategies for reducing hospital readmissions and improving the overall quality of care for patients with cardiovascular conditions.

articleTitle: A Review Paper on Innovative Deep Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms for Improved Cervical Cancer Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Cervical cancer is a major problem, especially in nations with low or middle incomes where access to cutting-edge healthcare and regular screening is constrained. Early detection and precise diagnosis are essential for effective therapy and higher survival rates. The identification of cervical cancer has shown outstanding and more accurate results with recent methods in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). More accurate and efficient diagnostic tools are required since the use of conventional screening methods, like Pap smears and HPV tests, is restricted.
