The research looks into feature extraction techniques like Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) in addition to machine learning approaches like support vector machines (SVM), random forests, and k-nearest neighbors (k-NN). Convolution neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning are addressed in order to achieve better performance on fewer datasets. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), two cutting-edge deep learning techniques, are also studied. Some of the future directions include the development of individualized medical strategies, the application of ML and DL models to clinical practice, and the fusion of multiple communication data sources to increase diagnosis accuracy.

articleTitle: Gas Pipeline Rust Detection System Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This project focuses on the development of an IoT -based gas pipeline rust detection system using the NodeMCU ESP8266, a voltage sensor, and a rusted iron pipe, with real-time monitoring via the Blynk app and ThingSpeak for visualization. Recent rust detection techniques rely on complex sensors, high-cost hardware, which face challenges such as high deployment costs, limited scalability, and the need for frequent maintenance. The proposed system addresses these challenges by offering a low-cost solution that measures voltage changes on the pipe's surface to detect rust. Challenges such as wireless data transmission reliability, and accurate rust detection were tackled in the design. It is powered by a 12V supply and programmed using Arduino IDE, the system enhances pipeline maintenance and safety by detecting rust early, thus preventing leaks and potential hazards. The integration of IoT technology in this system demonstrates the potential for scalable, smart industrial maintenance solutions.

articleTitle: Optuna-Optimized Machine Learning Technique for Accurate Diabetes Prediction and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Diabetes is a life-threatening chronic condition af-fecting millions worldwide., making timely prediction and risk classification crucial for effective intervention. Various machine learning techniques., such as deep learning., decision trees., random forests., and support vector machines (SVM)., have been applied to this task., but they face significant challenges. These challenges in-clude handling imbalanced datasets., optimizing hyperparameters., preventing overfitting., and maintaining high accuracy while en-suring interpretability. Additionally., adapting models for person-alized treatment based on clinical and demographic data requires precise hyperparameter tuning., which can be time-consuming and complex. This study addresses these challenges by introducing an Optuna optimization framework for diabetes prediction and clas-sification. Optuna is a powerful hyperparameter optimization tool that efficiently explores the parameter space to identify optimal configurations for improved model performance. Using a compre-hensive dataset of diabetic patients., we apply machine learning models such as logistic regression., SVM., and random forests., which are fine-tuned through Optuna's automatic tuning process. The results demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy., precision., recall., and Fl-score over conventional methods., leading to better diabetes prediction and risk stratification. This study highlights the potential of Optuna to enhance machine learning models., improving their applicability in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Parkinson's Disease Prediction Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a predominant neurological disorder that requires early discovery for treatment. This paper presents a comprehensive strategy for predicting PD using progressed machine learning methods. Our approach includes hybrid validation and assessment measurements to guarantee robust and dependable execution over differing scenarios. This involves sensitivity and specificity in early PD discovery. We make strides in symptomatic precision by utilizing choice trees and outfit classifiers like XGBoost. This thinking contributes to the field by providing a dependable prescient apparatus for PD, advancing early mediation, and encouraging a personalized understanding of care. Our discoveries emphasize the potential of machine learning in health care, especially for neurological disarrangements, and highlight the significance of fastidious methodological approaches in demonstrating advancement. By and large, this investigation progresses the understanding and administration of PD, advertising promising for progressing in understanding results and healthcare quality.

articleTitle: Sustainable Farming: Crop Prediction and Detection of Crop Deficiency using Various Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Selection of crop suitable to the environment and soil of the farm land is very crucial for sustainable agriculture. According to The CropLife India and Yes Bank report India faces an annual crop yield loss of approximately INR 2 lakh crores due to various factors, including not proper usage of fertilizer use and unsuitable crop choices for specific soil and climate conditions. Traditional farming methods often depends on intuition and experience, leading to inefficient resource utilization and reduced crop yields. The existing systems are particularly designed for large farms which leaves small scale farmers in despair. So, we have developed a model that predicts the best suited crop for that particular land by considering N, P, K levels, humidity, rainfall, temperature and pH levels of the soil and experimented with various algorithms such as Naïve's Bayes algorithm, Random Forest, Decision tree, SVM, Logistic Regression, Linear Regression, k-NN out of which Naïve's Bayes achieved highest accuracy of 99.54%. The proposed model not only gives the best suited crop but also tells what nutrients are deficient and need to be improved for better yield recommended by official government website of agriculture domain thereby contributing to both agricultural productivity and sustainability. This work underscores the potential of smart systems to support sustainable farming by enabling precise, informed decision-making that optimizes resource use and minimizes environmental impact.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurological condition characterized by a wide range of symptoms. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective intervention and support. This research reviews the established diagnostic tools, including clinical assessments, behavioral observations, genetic testing, and neuroimaging techniques. Additionally, we explore the potential of emerging technologies like machine learning and AI-based approaches in enhancing ASD diagnosis. By analyzing the strengths and limitations of various detection methods, this research provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of the field. The findings highlight the importance of continued research and innovation in improving ASD diagnosis for the benefit of affected individuals and their families.

articleTitle: Project Mate: A Modern Solution for Professional Networking and Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The emergence of modern technologies has revolutionized the way people seek professional connections, particularly with the rise of remote work. The traditional platforms such as LinkedIn are frequently used, however, there is a lack of highly specific solutions. To counter this, we created the “Project Mate” - a web-based application builds with the help of MERN stack as the core including MongoDB, Express JS, React JS, Node JS as the back-end framework to help professionals likeminded to connect and collaborate. The application provides the means for the users to search for ideal partners using keywords and is also set up to match users with similar interests. Users can then be able to communicate and negotiate on the type of collaboration they require within a closed space. The purpose was to develop an anonymous platform to establish business connections with the help of HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and the latest web advances.

articleTitle: Network Security Attack Detection Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study deals with network security attack detection using machine learning algorithms. Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Decision Tree algorithms are analyzed in the paper. In this paper, we have applied the NSL-KDD dataset and compared the performance of the stated algorithms to find the most accurate detection among various types of network attacks. All these three performed very well in our experiments; however, Decision Tree algorithms were always outperforming others in accuracy, precision, and recall. Excellence in performance by the Decision Tree is because a decision tree can handle complicated decision-making processes and is robust enough to manage various attack patterns. This research points out that, compared with other machine learning techniques, decision trees may enhance intrusion detection systems both in effectiveness and dependability, making the concept of defense against cyber threats more watertight.

articleTitle: Secure and Transparent Client Fund Collection Protocol Enabled by Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Blockchain technology has evolved as a formidable instrument in the financial technology space, providing unrivalled security, transparency, and efficiency. This article presents a groundbreaking approach for safe and transparent client fund collection using blockchain technology. Addressing the flaws of traditional money collecting systems, such as security risks, opacity, and inefficiency, the protocol uses blockchain's inherent properties to revolutionize fund collection. The protocol, initiated by the client, permits fund collection requests through a secure client interface, with the blockchain network authenticating transactions using cryptographic techniques to ensure only authorized transactions are performed and immutably recorded on the blockchain.. Notably, the protocol's openness and security, which are supported by strong encryption algorithms and cryptographic protocols, reduce the danger of fraud and embezzlement while establishing trust in stakeholders. This protocol, which leverages blockchain capabilities, provides a disruptive solution for money collection, increasing responsibility and confidence in the financial industry.

articleTitle: ML based Text Summarization for Sentiment Analysis in Information Retrieval using Feature Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Sentiment analysis plays a crucial role in understanding user preferences and opinions in the field of information retrieval. This research focuses on developing a system that combines text summarization and machine learning techniques to improve sentiment analysis accuracy. The proposed approach employs extractive and abstractive summarization techniques to reduce lengthy texts into concise summaries while preserving key information. Feature engineering is then applied to extract sentiment-related elements from the summary text, providing valuable insights for the SVM model. The SVM model, enhanced with feature engineering, is expected to effectively summarize text and accurately detect sentiments expressed in documents. This research contributes to the advancement of sentiment analysis techniques and provides valuable insights for decision-making and content development.

articleTitle: Optimizing Music Genre Classification Using CNN Sequential Models and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This work classifies musical genres using convolutional neural networks (CNN) housed inside a sequential model framework. Deep learning methods are applied in this work to try to raise the accuracy and efficiency of automated music genre classification systems. The proposed model treats unprocessed audio data using a method. Using convolutional layers, meant to capture hierarchical patterns inherent in some genres, this process extracts pertinent innovative features. In machine learning, sequential architecture helps to acquire temporal relationships, hence the model can detect intricate subtleties and variations in musical compositions. The work accesses a heterogeneous dataset including many genres in order to increase the resilience and adaptability of the model. The aim of this work is to verify if the CNN Sequential Model can properly categorize musical genres. The work intends to greatly advance automated music analysis and classification systems by strict experimentation and evaluation. The results of this study have significant consequences for many various applications including safety-based content tagging for clean music to protect early childhood of children in school environments, music streaming services, and music recommendation systems.

articleTitle: Automatic Fish Species Identification Using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Accurate identification of fish species is critical for applications in fisheries management., biodiversity monitoring., and conservation efforts. Conventional manual identification techniques take a lot of time and are prone to mistakes., particularly when working with big datasets and species that have similar physical characteristics. Automating tasks related to species identification has shown promise in recent breakthroughs in machine learning., especially in deep learning techniques like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and transfer learning. However., these systems face several challenges., including high variability in fish appearances., limited availability of labelled datasets., and the computational overhead required for real-time classification. This research study presents a fish species classification system using a transfer learning approach based on MobileNetV2. MobileNetV2., known for its efficiency and lightweight architecture., is fine-tuned on a custom fish dataset to enhance species identification accuracy while minimizing computational requirements. To increase the model's resilience and ability to generalise to new species., data augmentation approaches are used. The system is designed to deliver high classification accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency., making it suitable for deployment in real-world applications with limited resources. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves significant improvements in accuracy compared to traditional methods., while also addressing the challenges of dataset variability and overfitting.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Methodology for the Detection of Lung Cancer: A Four-Step Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Lung cancer is a significant health concern affecting both males and females, leading to a rise in mortality rates. Computer-aided detection systems have emerged as valuable tools for assisting in the diagnosis and management of lung cancer. This research presents a novel hybrid deep learning model that combines DenseNet and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks for improved lung cancer detection. The model was evaluated using a publicly accessible CT imaging dataset (IQ-OTH), demonstrating exceptional performance with a success rate of 97%, sensitivity of 95%, and specificity of 96%. The proposed approach offers a promising solution for enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of lung cancer diagnosis. By developing and validating such algorithms, we can contribute to the development of software suites for routine pathological procedures, alleviating the burden on healthcare professionals.

articleTitle: Deepfake Detection Using Multi-Modal Fusion Combined with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The proliferation of deepfake technology poses a significant challenge to the authenticity of digital content. This research explores the application of multimodal fusion techniques to enhance deepfake detection accuracy. By combining visual and audio features, the proposed method leverages the complementary nature of different data types to detect discrepancies introduced by deepfake manipulation. An attention mechanism is incorporated to focus on salient regions within each modality, further improving detection accuracy. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) are employed for feature extraction, followed by feature fusion for deepfake detection. This approach demonstrates the effectiveness of multimodal fusion in combating the evolving threat of deepfake technology. By advancing deepfake detection techniques, this research contributes to safeguarding the integrity of digital content and preserving trust in media.

articleTitle: Time Series Analysis by XGBoost Model for Future Prediction of Power Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study tries to investigate the power consumption in Romania taking the concern of time series analysis. This time series analysis has been done to forecast the probable consumption of the power based on past data record of 5.5 years. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) has been incurred in this dataset to analyze the power consumption profile throughout the years, since power consumption strategy can play a vital role for minimizing the critical condition in near future. From the data analysis it is observed that power consumption is relatively high from Monday to Friday in every week whether the overall power consumption variation throughout the year is almost same. The maximum power consumption recorded is 9615 MW with minimum of 3889 MW throughout the years of dataset where standard deviation is 1043.65 MW. From the data analysis it is seen that minimum RMSE recorded is 119.05 for the training dataset and 144.98 for the validation dataset.

articleTitle: Analysis of Internet of Things Build Autonomous Crops the Sustainability Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The increasing global population has driven a surge in agricultural production, emphasizing the need for efficient and high-quality crop yields within shorter timeframes. To address this challenge, modern agriculture is seeking innovative solutions that maximize resource utilization and minimize waste. This review study examines the potential of IoT-based precision agriculture systems in optimizing crop production processes. Specifically, we focus on a prototype that employs an ESP32 development board and Arduino Cloud platform to monitor and control various agricultural parameters, including irrigation, fertilization, temperature, soil humidity, and electrical magnitudes. The integration of a 3D printer for precise planting and a photovoltaic system for sustainable energy generation further enhances the system's capabilities. This review concludes that IoT-based precision agriculture systems offer a promising approach to improving resource efficiency, reducing environmental impact, and ensuring sustainable food production.

articleTitle: Marker-Based AR Application for Better Understanding of Electrical Circuits and Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This paper proposes a marker-based Augmented Reality (AR) electric circuit meant to help students grasp the knowledge of electrical circuits, especially the usage of capacitors. Recognizing components like the battery, switch, capacitor and bulb, the AR software allows students to engage with real-time representations of electrical activity including capacitor charging and discharging. The interesting and dynamic AR environment helps abstract ideas to be more interactive and accessible, therefore improving knowledge. Early evidence indicates that, when compared to conventional teaching methods, the AR tool greatly increases student attention and knowledge even if there are some technical limitations such inconsistent marker recognition problems. Positive remarks suggest that AR may be a helpful tool for questioning concepts in electrical engineering. Future initiatives will focus on enhancing the technical aspects of the system and extending its contents to provide a more whole learning experience in numerous educational situations.

articleTitle: Probable Risk Factors of Heart Disease with Accuracy Performance by Various Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Heart disease is a serious health concern worldwide and it is continuously increasing irrespective of the ages. According to the WHO., 17.9 million deaths are caused by CVD., which is 32% of all global deaths. Precautionary measure is very essential to avoid this escalation. By Machine learning approaches this analysis is predicted to find out the risk factors for heart disease. LR., SVM., GNB., DT., KNN., RF- six classifiers are used in this study to analyze factors behind the disease. Results before data preprocessing and after preprocessing were investigated where the Random forest algorithm has given the highest accuracy. Accuracy of the other four models is in the range of 86-89% with data preprocessing. Precision., recall., f1-score are also improved significantly. By using machine learning a satisfactory prediction of such a critical disease is very much impressive for health care.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuned EfficientNetB0 Transfer Learning Model for the Detection and Classification of Peach Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Peach trees are vulnerable to numerous diseases impacting fruit production and quality. Early and accurate disease detection is essential for managing these diseases effectively. Traditional manual inspection methods are labor-intensive and prone to human error, underscoring the need for automated approaches. In this study, a fine-tuned EfficientNetB0 transfer learning model is developed for detecting and classifying peach leaf diseases. The proposed model leverages the strengths of the EfficientNetB0 architecture, which balances computational efficiency and accuracy, to classify peach leaf conditions, including healthy and diseased leaves. A dataset of 2,635 peach leaf images is used to train and validate the model. Results show that the model achieves high accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores, making it a reliable tool for automated disease detection. This research contributes to precision agriculture by providing a scalable and efficient solution for disease management in peach cultivation, potentially reducing the need for manual inspection and improving agricultural productivity.

articleTitle: A CNN Centric Approach to Acute Lymphoblastic Luekemia Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Leukaemia is a serious malignancy that impacts both adults and children, presenting as either a chronic or acute condition. Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) stands as the most prevalent type of blood disease and remains a leading cause of death. This aggressive cancer invades the blood, spreading via surrounding bodily systems and organs. The conventional method for classifying cancer cells and non-cancer cells involves manual diagnosis, where specialists inspect cell images under a microscope and annotate the labels. However, this manual microscopic analysis is not only tedious but also susceptible to potential false diagnoses. In response to these challenges, this project seeks to leverage a pre-trained model for automated de-tection and classification of leukemia subtypes, including benign, early, pre, and pro stages. By utilizing a pretrained model, the proposed system aims enhance its ability to accurately discern and classify leukemia subtypes. By leveraging pre-trained models, the proposed approach aims to improve classification accuracy, efficiency, and reduce the risk of misdiagnosis compared to manual analysis. This research contributes to the advancement of automated leukemia diagnosis, paving the way for potential clinical applications.

articleTitle: Improving Access to Skin Care with a Multi-Factorial Strategy Using Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research explores the use of digital health technologies to address skin health disparities in underprivileged communities. By leveraging Vision Transformers (ViT), mHealth apps, telemedicine, social media, virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and geographic information systems (GIS), the study aims to enhance community engagement, improve access to care, and improve early detection of skin health conditions. The research findings demonstrate a significant increase in community participation (40%), improved access to treatment (30%), and enhanced diagnostic accuracy (20%) through the implementation of these digital health technologies. This approach has the potential to reduce skin health inequities and promote more equitable outcomes. By utilizing the power of technology, this research contributes to advancing healthcare accessibility and improving the well-being of marginalized communities.

articleTitle: MediExchange: A Smart Web Portal to Buy and Sell Unused Medicines
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In today's world, medication waste poses significant environmental, economic, and social challenges. “MediExchange: Buy & Sell Unused Medicine” is an innovative web-based platform designed to mitigate these issues by enabling individuals and pharmacies to buy and sell unused, unexpired medications. This system allows users to upload photos, descriptions, and expiration dates of their surplus medicines, facilitating secure and efficient transactions. MediExchange aims to reduce medication waste, lower healthcare costs, and improve access to essential medicines for those in need. This paper explores the development and implementation of the MediExchange platform, focusing on its technical architecture, security features, and user experience. It also examines the potential impacts on public health and the pharmaceutical industry, as well as the regulatory and ethical considerations involved in such a marketplace.

articleTitle: Robust Android Security: A Random Forest-Based Approach to Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: With an accuracy of 97.03°/0, this work offers a method for identifying Android malware utilising a Random Forest model. Growing frequency of malware aimed at Android devices calls for sophisticated and dependable detection techniques. Using a strong ensemble learning method called Random Forest, applications are categorised as either benign or malicious depending on a thorough collection of features gleaned from them. The model uses several decision trees, each of which helps to produce a consensus decision, hence improving the general predictive performance and lowering the overfitting risk. On a varied collection of Android applications, extensive tests and evaluations were carried out to show the model's capacity for precisely spotting malware. The great accuracy rate highlights how well the Random Forest method is in differentiating between good and bad uses, so providing a potential means of enhancing Android security. This approach guarantees strong protection for Android users by not only offering dependable detection but also changing to new and developing threats.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence of Sustainability and Internet of Things Industry 4.0 Automation Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The AI Industry 4.0 is relevant to improving the productivity, quality, and efficiency of long-term sustainable smart production. It is crucial to identify the primary motivators, obstacles, and dangers in the industry 4.0 implementation plan in order to preserve material flow stability and the sustainability of the supply chain. The impact of quality control, risk assessment, and change management now becomes apparent because the transition process entails many risks, interruptions, unanticipated events, and changes. This review paper outlines the future research scope, sustainability in through-life smart manufacturing, and main obstacles and opportunities for applying technology of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. It includes cutting-edge technology designed to advance the circular economy, maximize resource efficiency, boost energy efficiency, regulate air pollutants, efficiently handle waste, and advance sustainable goods, services, and behaviors

articleTitle: Smoke-Free Zones: Enhancing Smoker Detection with MobileNetV2 and CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Smoking is still a major global public health concern since it causes a lot of avoidable illnesses and early deaths. Planning an intervention and a course of treatment effectively depends on accurately identifying smoking behaviour. With the help of MobileNetV2, a portable and effective deep learning model, the convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture in this work presents a unique method for smoker categorization. This method minimizes computational resources while improving classification performance by utilising the hierarchical features that MobileNetV2 learned. Model refine the pre-trained MobileNetV2 model on the smoker categorization task by transfer learning. The efficacy of suggested method is demonstrated by the experimental results, which achieve cutting-edge performance in terms of smoker classification precision, sensitivity, and specificity. Moreover, model demonstrates resilience in many data modalities, indicating its potential for practical use in healthcare environments. A viable method for automated smoker classification is provided by the suggested CNN + MobileNetV2 framework, which will help with early diagnosis, personalized intervention, and better patient results in attempts to quit smoking which could lead to healthy lives.

articleTitle: Smart Streetlight Fault Detection and Location Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: One of the most prevalent needs among people worldwide is electricity; while it may be produced, it does not exactly meet demand. Energy conservation and improved streetlamp control are achieved through the usage of IoT technologies. The Project aims at designing smart street light fault detection and location tracking system. With the help of the LDR sensor, the lights are turned on and off automatically based on the amount of sunshine. The system sends an alert message to the user via the Blynk app via by checking the faults in the streetlight. With a PIR sensor, the motion of an item is sensed. The light will illuminate brightly if an object approaches the infrared sensor. In the absence of such, the light will be faint. Current and voltage sensors are used to check the power supply and any voltage variations in the supply. This project effectively conveys the idea of energy conservation, effective light monitoring, and the reduction of accidents caused by insufficient light.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology for Safeguarding Against Counterfeits
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Blockchain technology has gained significant attention in recent years due to its transformative impact on financial transactions. However, its potential extends beyond the financial sector and can be applied to address various challenges, including counterfeiting. This study explores the application of blockchain technology in combating counterfeiting, examining existing anti-counterfeiting solutions and highlighting the key features of blockchain that make it well-suited for this purpose. The research findings emphasize that a comprehensive approach is necessary to effectively address counterfeiting, combining technological innovations with complementary strategies such as awareness campaigns, legal action, and robust alert systems. Blockchain technology offers several benefits, including improved product authentication, streamlined transactions, and increased stakeholder trust. Its transparency, immutability, and decentralized structure provide a strong foundation for combating counterfeiting and safeguarding consumer interests in the digital era. This study highlights the importance of combining technological advancements with complementary strategies to create a comprehensive and effective approach to combating counterfeiting. By leveraging blockchain technology, organizations can enhance product authenticity, streamline supply chains, and protect consumers from fake goods.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Early Prediction of Heart Disease: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The major causes of death worldwide are heart diseases, and they call for highly sophisticated prediction models for early detection and treatment. This research paper compares the output of ML algorithms, Logistic Regression with an accuracy of 82.8%, Decision Tree Classifier with 70.3% accuracy, and Random Forest Classifier with 78.1 % accuracy, in predicting heart disease. Every model is evaluated in line with accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC). The findings demonstrate clear differences in model performance; however, this study emphasizes the prospects of ML techniques in enhancing heart disease prediction, thereby providing researchers and medical practitioners with interesting analysis. By means of the discovery of the most effective ML methods, our work helps the ongoing endeavors to improve diagnosis accuracy and patient outcomes in cardiovascular illnesses.

articleTitle: A Study on Large Language Models in Multi Modal Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)

authors.preferredName: Adharapurapu V S M Ashok Kumar

abstract: Data in today's applications is becoming more complicated and diverse; therefore, models have had to be developed that can process and merge information not only from text but also from images or even sound. Two important areas where LLMs have also been applied include natural language processing (NLP) as well as multimodallearning. This paper investigates how LLMs have been used in multimodal learning environments. Specifically, this study investigates how these models are adapting themselves for them to be able to handle text, visual but more especially audio data. Exploring the techniques used to cross these modalities so well enables us to understand all what it imposes. Thus, this study traces the laying points of observations starting with new horizons addressing some of the strengths and weaknesses of current modalities to capture what it means for future research ideas and application purposes. In this perspective, an attempt has been made to comprehend all the possible ways that exist when dealing with LLMs and multi-modal activities through creating dialogue in line with its current relevance.

articleTitle: Detection of Eye Disease Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The human eye is a complex organ that can perceive a wide variety of visual inputs. However, its functioning can be severely impaired by diseases such as cataract and diabetic retinopathy which have the potential to cause permanent blindness which not only disrupts the productivity and mobility of patients but also causes a socio-economic impact that decreases the quality of life. This paper reviews the recent advancements in deep learning for diagnosing retinal diseases such as diabetic retinopathy (DR), cataract and glaucoma. The paper presents an extensive comparative analysis of 4 definite deep learning models - Vision Transformers (ViT), ResNet, GoogLeNet and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The results from the conducted experiments show that ViT has the highest accuracy followed by CNN. The outcomes highlights the potential of deep learning models in revolutionizing eye disease detection technology.

articleTitle: Design of a Floating-Point ALU for Calculating Shortest Distance Between Two Floating Point Numbers
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study presents the design of a floating-point ALU which calculates shortest distance between two floating point numbers. Such a unit is used extensively in cluster algorithm. This design has been carried out on ZedBoardZynq 7000 Evaluation and Development kit, part no:xc7z020clg484-1. Verilog HDL has been used to use the Software version of the zedboard

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks and Their Variants for Precise Fruit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study carefully compares various generative adversarial networks (GANs) and their variations in object detection, focusing on fruit recognition in image datasets. The study assesses the efficacy of InfoGAN, CycleGAN, ConditionalGAN, and StyleGAN in enhancing object detection accuracy. To improve object detection models, test each version of GAN by creating fake images. The process is achieved by conducting a lot of experiments with different fruit datasets that include both common and rare varieties. In addition to traditional evaluation metrics like peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), this research introduces a novel approach. The study finds the GAN variant that makes synthetic images work best for finding objects by making a link between PSNR and SSIM values and how well they work for finding objects. The findings offer valuable insights into the relationship between GAN-generated image quality and object detection efficacy, highlighting each GAN variant's strengths and weaknesses in fruit recognition. This comparative analysis serves as a foundation for advancing computer vision systems for object detection tasks and provides direction for future research in this field.

articleTitle: Automized Mango Leaf Disease Detection Using Various Optimizer of CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Mango is one of the most grown fruits and is considered to be one of the most consumed around the world. Despite being so crucial economically and nutritionally the farmers are not aware about the different diseases that mango plants can adhere to. The research is intended to find out an efficient way for the farmers to determine the disease at an early stage and cure the plant accordingly so that it does not affect it for the whole life span. To achieve the objective deep CNN was chosen as it is the best in image classification, furthermore tuning of the optimizer was done to find the best fit for the model. Optimizers used were Adam, Adamax, SGD, RMSprop, Adadelta. After many experiments we determined that the best fit optimizer for the deep CNN is “Adamax” with an accuracy of 94%. This is an ideal accuracy for a classification model over a real life dataset.

articleTitle: Brain Stroke Prediction by Machine Learning Algorithm Along with Boosting Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: A stroke is a medical emergency when blood circulation in the brain is disrupted or outflowing due to a burst of nerve tissue. Diagnosis at the proper time is crucial to saving lives through immediate treatment. Machine learning techniques show good accuracy in predicting the likelihood of a stroke from related factors. Ten machine learning classifiers have been considered to predict stroke namely, logistic regression (LR), Random forest (RF), Decision tree (DT), Support vector machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbors (KNN), Gaussian Naïve Bayes (GNB), and four boosting classifiers which are Gradient boost, adaboost, Xgboost and lightgbm. SMOTE is applied to balance the imbalance dataset and then again used in all the models. It is found that Random forest has the highest 96% accuracy, extreme boost and lightgbm both have 95% accuracy. Here traditional logistic regression and Gaussian Naïve Bayes have higher error, which is 21% and 24%.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Prediction: Hyper Parameter Tuning Based Ensemble Learning and Voting Classifiers Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: As per the observations of World Health Organization (WHO), heart related issues are the prominent reason for the loss of life and is becoming more common every year. Timely therapy raises the possibility of cure. For this, early prediction and good diagnosis are essential. Today's technology development allows for more accurate and precise predictions. Researchers in prediction modeling are interested in machine learning (ML) methods because of their accuracy, precision, and predictability. An attempt is made here to predict cardiac diseases using ML techniques, including Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Multi-Layer Perceptron(MLP). The cardiac disease dataset was acquired from the Kaggle website, and the prediction was done using an ensemble of the standard ML methods based on hyper parameter tuning and voting classifiers. Finally, the findings are compared and concluded based on the ensemble model voting approach and the predictive performance metrics.

articleTitle: Smart Energy Optimization Harnessing IoT and Advanced Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The paper gives an extensive investigation of the research findings on the optimization of energy management in smart microgrids. The study specifically focuses on integrating renewable energy sources with the Internet of Things. Smart microgrids have become an essential option due to the increasing global energy demand and environmental problems arising from the use of fossil fuels. These grids assure better efficiency in renewable energy usage energy storage, and improved user interaction using IoT-based technologies. This research investigates the application of machine learning algorithms to predict energy consumption patterns, electricity prices, and optimal energy storage management strategies. The main idea of the proposed mathematical model in this paper is to minimize the cost of energy procurement under the condition of a balanced energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>upply/demand based on the optimization problem. This model is simulated with several scenarios using the linear programming tool of MATLAB software and confirms high cost savings and system efficiency. This study also investigates how EVs and BESS in the grid exert better optimization of smart energy systems.

articleTitle: Fingerprint Image Enhancement: Multi-Filter Approaches and Stage Timing Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The performance of fingerprint recognition and verification systems heavily depends on the quality of the input fingerprint images. This paper introduces a multi-filter image enhancement strategy tailored for enhancing low-quality fingerprint images. The objective is to enhance the visibility and definition of ridge patterns, tackling problems stemming from irregular skin contacts and contaminated sensor surfaces. Author incorporates a new normalization technique that adjusts for finger flexibility, improving the correction of anomalies and boosting overall image quality, especially in detecting fine details. Experimental evidence shows that technique surpasses previous methods in effectiveness.

articleTitle: Smart Cow Care: IoT-Driven Automatic Feeding and Temperature Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Dairy housing arrangements vary considerably across the world based on climate, dairy size, and feeding tactics. Housing must give access to food, water, and protection from relevant environmental conditions. Temperature extremes are a challenge for cow housing. Heat stress in cattle can reduce fertility and milk output. Giving shade is a frequent approach for minimizing heat stress. Dairy housing arrangements vary considerably across the world based on climate, dairy size, and feeding tactics. Housing must give access to food, water, and protection from relevant environmental conditions. Temperature extremes are a challenge for cow housing. Heat stress in cattle can reduce fertility and milk output. Giving shade is a frequent approach for minimizing heat stress. Barn architecture may also include fans or tunnel ventilation. Many automatic feeders have been offered on the market throughout the years, but none of them can solve several difficulties such as high temperature and feed control. The goal of this project is to leverage the internet of things to solve the challenges produced by present feeders and to design an efficient autonomous feeder. This automatic feeder is controlled by a micro controller and has an interface with a DC motor, relays and motor drivers. To conduct actions like as spinning motors and switching relays on and off, software code is loaded into the micro controller. Using blynk software, a mobile phone controls the feeding system[8]. The user can able to control the water intake of the cow through blynk app. When the temperature of the barn is above the predetermined level, the fan will be turned on automatically and it will reduce the temperature. While the user is away from the location, he may still feed the cows on time and can control the temperature of the barn.

articleTitle: Enhanced Prediction of Cervical Cancer Risk by combined Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Cervical Cancer constitutes a profound global health challenge, affecting a substantial number of women annually. If this cancer is not diagnosed and attended with hypervigilance, it can spread to other body parts, damage tissues, and typically deteriorate the immune system of the body. Deviating from the conventional methods of Cervical Cancer Prediction using Machine Learning (ML) Techniques, the proposed work Risk Prediction of Cervical Cancer focuses on the development and prediction of a model for early prediction of Cervical Cancer using combined ML techniques. The combined ML techniques proposed in the work includes - Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Gradient Boosting (GradBoost), Decision Tree (DT) and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) techniques are employed to accurately anticipate cervical cancer diagnosing patients early and achieving better outcomes. The study's methodology involves dataset analysis, preprocessing, model training, and evaluation, culminating in the identification of Random Forest as an effective classifier. The proposed work outlines the necessity of combining ML techniques by achieving a significant result of Accuracy - 96%, Precision - 98%, Recall- 98% and F1-score - 98%. The proposed work underlines the necessity of collaboration between researchers, healthcare professionals, and governments to reduce cervical cancer worldwide and suggests future directions for improving prediction accuracy through the integration of new technologies and data enhancement.

articleTitle: Design of Error-Resilient Approximate Multiplier for Image Processing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In the ever-growing quest for efficient computing, approximate multipliers offer a compelling trade-off between accuracy and resource consumption. This work delves into the design of such multipliers, targeting three crucial aspects: efficiency, error resilience, and its application. The idea to propose an approach that leverages truncated partial products and strategically placed approximations to significantly reduce hardware complexity compared to exact multipliers. This enables substantial savings in area, making the design ideal for applications with tight resource constraints. However, reducing complexity often comes at the cost of increased errors. To combat this, integration of error recovery modules adapted from existing research is proposed. Significantly reduces error metrics like ED, NMED and MRED, ensuring acceptable accuracy for targeted applications. Furthermore, inherent biases can creep into approximate multipliers, skewing their outputs. This will further refine the accuracy of the design, solidifying its potential in a wider range of real-world scenarios. Overall, this work paves the way for highly efficient and adaptable approximate multipliers. By balancing resource savings with error control and bias mitigation, a promising alternative for applications where computational power and flexibility is offered. The obtained results are further applied into image processing applications and is proved to be fruitful. Paper proposes a novel 4:2 approximate compressor which comparatively takes 20% less area with an approximate increase an error in 10% which is proven to be acceptable. This paper also goes with the six bit truncation which improves the compute time, area and PDP.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Healthcare: Decision Trees for Asthma Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: A chronic respiratory condition marked by hyperreactivity and inflammation of the airways., asthma presents serious health problems worldwide. Asthma prediction done early and precisely can result in better patient outcomes and care. The effectiveness of many machine learning algorithms in asthma prediction is investigated in this work., with an emphasis on a performance comparison of Decision Tree., K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN)., and Random Forest classifiers. Created prediction algorithms to detect people at risk of asthma using a large dataset including clinical., environmental., and genetic variables. Among KNN and Random Forest classifiers., the Decision Tree method outperforms them with the maximum prediction accuracy of 81 0/0. The Decision Tree model outperforms others because of its interpretability., which offers precise understanding of the decision-making process., and its capacity to manage complicated relationships between elements. The possibilities of Decision Tree models in asthma prediction are demonstrated by these results., which also emphasize the need of choosing suitable machine learning methods for efficient illness prediction. This work offers a potential method for early asthma diagnosis and customized therapeutic techniques., therefore supporting the continuous attempts to use machine learning in healthcare.

articleTitle: FootwearFusion: Convolutional Neural Network for Shoe, Sandal, and Boot Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: A fundamental task in computer vision, footwear categorization finds many applications in the retail, security, and fashion industries. This paper employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to compare and categorize three popular footwear types: shoes, boots, and sandals. The collection is made up of photos that were gathered from several sources and feature a range of footwear brands, colors, and styles. High accuracy rates on both training and validation sets show how effective CNNs are at differentiating between shoes, boots, and sandals based on experimental results. It also examines the effect of class imbalance and dataset size on model performance, offering solutions and insights into possible problems. The present study serves as a standard for assessing future developments in this field and delivers insightful information about the use of deep learning algorithms for footwear categorization in manufacturing technology. Promising outcomes and practical deployment in real-world applications, such as automated inventory management, e-commerce product categorization, and security screening systems, are possible with the created model.

articleTitle: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Tear Detection: ML and DL Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries are a major problem in sports and physical activities; prompt and precise diagnosis is generally necessary for appropriate treatment and recovery. Even if they are trustworthy, traditional diagnostic techniques can be expensive, time-consuming, and prone to human mistake. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), are viable options for ACL injury categorization and detection. This study summarizes the state-of-the-art research on the use of ML and DL for ACL injury identification, emphasizing different approaches, datasets, and performance measures. We explore the benefits and drawbacks of current methods and point out directions for further study to improve clinical integration and diagnostic precision.

articleTitle: H Yperparameter Tunning to Improve Deep Learning Model Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Deep learning models have become a powerful tool in various domains, including fraud detection in credit card transactions. In this paper, we explore the crucial aspect of hyperparameter tuning to enhance the performance of deep learning models in the context of credit card fraud detection. We investigate four different combinations of optimization algorithms (Adam and Adagrad) and weight initializers (Xavier and He) with and without batch normalization. Through comprehensive experimentation using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on a credit card fraud detection dataset, we find that the combi-nation of Adam optimization with batch normalization and the He initializer consistently yields the highest accuracy compared to the other configurations. Our study not only highlights the significance of selecting appropriate hyperparameters but also provides insights into achieving superior performance in fraud detection tasks.

articleTitle: A Health Monitoring System with Multi-Sensor Information Fusion (HMS-MSIF) using a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In recent years, the Health Monitoring System (HMS) is a complicated technology that offers numerous benefits over conventional patient health management systems. These systems comprise a wearable wireless device, such as a bracelet, with sensors, incoming sensors, EEG sensors, and other features linked to a smartphone application that allows a doctor to obtain medical data remotely through a cloud platform. The cloud platform handles the information storage and retrieval management. Multi-sensor management involves managing or coordinating various sensor resources to govern environment perception activities. The innovative study on multi-sensor fusion is becoming the most significant factor in creating and researching modern multi-sensor-supported healthcare systems. Therefore, this research finds a solution by designing a health monitoring system with multi-sensor information fusion (HMS-MSIF) using a deep neural network. This model designs a deep neural network for learning sensor representations from the raw sensor-based health data. The simulation results show the highest prediction accuracy of 97.58%, reliability ratio of 97.23% and signal-to-noise ratio of 98.64%. The proposed model gives the lowest error rate of 19.76%, thus suggesting real-time implementation.

articleTitle: Human Safety Using GPS and Geofencing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study explores the integration of GPS and geofencing technology to enhance women's safety in both urban and rural settings. By combining real-time location tracking and virtual boundaries, these technologies provide a powerful tool for monitoring, alerting, and responding to potential threats. The proposed safety system incorporates GPS tracking, emergency alert features, and automatic notifications to predefined contacts and authorities when users enter or leave designated safe zones. Geofencing technology creates secure virtual boundaries around specific areas, such as homes, workplaces, and educational institutions, providing an additional layer of protection. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of GPS and geofencing in improving situational awareness and enabling timely responses to potential threats. By empowering women with these technologies, the proposed system contributes to enhancing their safety and well-being. By implementing these technologies, communities can take proactive steps to prevent and address safety concerns, enabling a more secure and inclusive environment for all.

articleTitle: Blood Cell Classification and Counting in Hematology through Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Medical diagnosis is one of the areas that has been greatly influenced by the progress of computer vision technologies. This study presents a unique approach for the detection and counting of blood cells in hematology: You Only Look One algorithm version 7 (YOLOv7). YOLO is designed for real-time object detection, making it ideal for applications such as blood vessel detection where speed is critical. The architecture allows the model to process images faster than other recognition models, such as R-CNN or SSD, which is very important for situations that require fast results, such as analysis automatic blood at clinical sites. The purpose of the proposed method is to overcome the shortcomings of conventional methods and to accurately and quickly identify blood cells in mechanical images. The YOLOv7 model has been utilizedbecause it can detect objects in real-time with highprecision and speed. The methodology for bloodcell counting involves the use of YOLOv7 togenerate bounding boxes around each detectedblood cell in an image, where the count of these bounding boxes directly corresponds to the number of cells. This advancement in hematology not onlyimproves blood cell analysis efficiency but also expedites the process of diagnosing and planningtreatment in various medical situations. This paper details how YOLOv7 was modified and adjusted to meet the specific requirements of hematologicalimage analysis, including training models, preparing datasets, and evaluating performance. The study also addresses the potential impact of this technology on clinical workflows, highlightinghow it might help medical practitioners make decisions more quickly and intelligently. Hematology analysis systems including YOLOv7 are able to improve laboratory diagnostics and help patients by providing better care and results. This workconcludes by demonstrating the revolutionary potential of YOLOv7 in blood cell identificationand counting in hematology, paving the way for accurate and better diagnosis, ultimatelyimproving patient outcomes and capabilitiesor health care professionals.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Design and Execution for Residential Construction Through Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Today's construction industry's scenario is changing on a daily basis. Customers' and clients' needs for facilities and amenities are growing. Traditional documentation, such as two dimensional sketches and written specifications, are used to communicate architectural design details. This technique is extended and typo, and it reflects the achievable direction of the construction project. Information acquired from the construction industry, however, have demonstrated that creative Architectural plan methods utilizing latest Information and Communication Technology (ICT), tools like Virtual Reality (VR), may boost ability and cut construction times. Virtual Reality has been the only software utilized at times in the construction industry until now, generally to help clients visualize the product Architectural Design. The objective of this study was to see the use of virtual reality and thus 3D may be used in planning and architectural design. The key hypothesis during the study was that using virtual models rendered using VR technology, drives it simpler to recognize, assess, coordinate, and communicate the product Architectural Design, resulting in better decision- making and, as a result, a better final product. In the construction sector, both virtual reality and augmented reality play critical roles. VR has a large significance over real - world technologies.

articleTitle: Adaptive Compressive Sensing for Natural Images Using Schur Decomposition and Optimized Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) is growing as an effective method for efficient imagine capture and recovery by harnessing the fundamental sparseness of natural images. The paper presents a unique framework for CS of live images employing Schur decomposition, a matrix decomposition approach that improves the detection and reconstruction processes. The suggested technique utilizes Schur decomposition to enhance the sensing matrix, facilitating more effective sampling by collecting essential imagine information in both spatial and frequency domains. The Schur-based sensing matrix, in contrast to conventional random sensing matrices, is designed to use the structural characteristics of real pictures, hence enhancing the precision of image reconstruction from a reduced quantity of observations. The integrated Schur decomposition with an iterative image reconstruction algorithm, incorporating Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) promotes sparsity. The combination improves the robustness of the recovery process while reducing reconstruction artifacts. Extensive simulations demonstrate that proposed Schur-based framework achieves superior performance compared to conventional CS techniques, particularly in terms of Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). The proposed method improves the quality of reconstructed images and expedites the convergence of the reconstructing technique, hence reducing computational complexity. The framework is assessed over several natural imagine datasets, demonstrating substantial improvements in image quality and computing efficiency resulting in a PSNR of 37.263 dB and SSIM 0.813 for CAT image. The Schur decomposition method for CS is an effective solution for applications necessitating quick picture capture and high-quality reconstruction, including medical imaging, remote sensing, and real-time image processing systems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Temporal Weather Patterns: ResNet-50 Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The classification of weather and time has a wide range of applications, some of which include improving the accuracy of weather forecasting, enhancing the performance of autonomous vehicles, and optimizing the planning and activities that take place outside considering environmental impact and improving quality of life. Utilizing the ResNet-50 neural network architecture and making use of the CCF BDCI dataset, which is comprised of 2600 photos that have been manually tagged, investigate the categorization of weather and time in this study. Dataset has divided these photographs into five distinct weather conditions: overcast, sunny, rainy, snowy, and foggy. Additionally, images have been divided them into five distinct time periods: dawn, morning, afternoon, dusk, and night. Initially, the ResNet-50 model was trained for a total of twenty epochs. This model had previously been pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset and had been fine-tuned for particular classification objective. Following that, the training period was extended to a total of fifty epochs in order to assess the effect that further training had on the overall performance of the model. During the entirety of the training process, crucial parameters such as accuracy and loss were monitored on both the training dataset and the validation dataset. The purpose of this research is to demonstrate that the ResNet-50 model is capable of accurately categorizing weather and time circumstances, as well as to evaluate the ways in which longer training epochs contribute to enhanced classification accuracy and overall model robustness.

articleTitle: Academic Performance Analysis of the Students with Feature Retraction Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research investigates the application of machine learning algorithms to predict student academic performance based on historical data and current factors. Five machine learning algorithms were employed to analyze thirteen features related to student demographics, academic background, and other relevant factors. The study evaluates the performance of the algorithms using classification metrics, including the classification matrix and confusion matrix. The results demonstrate that after data preprocessing, four out of the five classifiers achieved 100% accuracy, while K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) achieved 80% accuracy. Random Forest (RF) exhibited a significant improvement from 92% accuracy before preprocessing to 100% accuracy after preprocessing. Chi-square analysis reveals that age and gender features has no significant impact on academic performance. This finding suggests that other factors, such as study habits, motivation, and socioeconomic conditions, may play a more influential role in predicting student success. The research contributes to the understanding of factors influencing student academic performance and provides valuable insights for educators and policymakers. By leveraging machine learning techniques, this study demonstrates the potential for predicting student success and implementing targeted interventions to support student achievement.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of ResNet-50 and GoogleNet for Damage Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Accurate and rapid assessment of structural damage is critical for maintaining the safety and integrity of infrastructure, especially following natural disasters. Traditional methods of damage assessment, which rely on manual inspections, can be labor-intensive and subject to human error. This study exam-ines the use of ResNet50 and GoogLeNet convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automate the classification of damaged structures. The models were trained on a diverse dataset that includes images of both damaged and undamaged structures, ensuring their adaptability to different conditions. Evaluation metrics such as precision, recall, accuracy, and F1-score were used to measure performance. The results demonstrate that both ResNet50 and GoogLeNet are effective for assessing damage in post-disaster contexts. However, GoogLeNet shows a slight advantage achieving testing accuracy of 97.5% as compared to ResNet50 achieving 97.2% accuracy. This suggests that GoogLeNet offer a more reliable option for real-world disaster response applications.

articleTitle: AI Powered Crypt-Analysis for Identification of Encryption Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In modern world, cryptographic algorithms are critical for securing sensitive data, ensuring confidentiality, and protecting against cyber threats. With the increasing number of encryption algorithms and modes, identifying which algorithm was used in a ciphertext becomes a difficult job. To tackle this we present a machine learning-based solution that automates the identification of cryptographic algorithms using the Random Forest classifier. The system processes a large dataset of “encrypted-data”, consisting of 39 different algorithms and modes, by first extracting key features such as byte frequency and entropy from the ciphertexts. These features are used to create a 257 -length cipher-descriptor for classification. The dataset is split into 19 subsets, each containing data from two algorithms, and 19 different Random Forest models are trained. During testing, a sequential model loading approach is employed to manage computational resources. The best-performing model, in terms of confidence score, is used to predict the encryption algorithm for a given input ciphertext. Finally, the system is integrated with a Gradio web interface, allowing for real-time, user-friendly interaction. Our approach provides a scalable and accurate tool for cryptographic analysis, significantly improving upon traditional methods.

articleTitle: Security Issues and Solutions in Government to Citizens (G2C) Services – A Detailed Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research review explores the security challenges and solutions within Government-to-Citizen (G2C) digital interactions. It highlights the importance of securing citizen data against breaches, unauthorized access, identity theft, and cyberattacks, including phishing, social engineering, malware, and ransomware. The study recommends encryption, data protection, secure software development practices (such as continuous code reviews and penetration testing), regular security audits, and user education to mitigate these risks. It also presents case studies from various countries, offering a comparative analysis of different security strategies to identify effective approaches and common challenges. This analysis aids in informed decision-making, knowledge sharing, and the development of future strategies. Additionally, the thesis discusses the potential of emerging technologies like blockchain, biometrics, AI, and IoT to enhance G2C security further. Keywords include E-governance, G2C, Security, Cyber Security, Government, and Citizens.

articleTitle: Prediction of Stability of Real Time Network Control System for Pressure Process Station
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: As network technology has advanced, the research and application of Networked Control Systems (NCS) have garnered increased attention from researchers. While NCS facilitates the easy and convenient control of large systems, a significant challenge remains: the limited bandwidth available to the system and packet loss during the transmission of data. The proposed work is to control and monitor a pressure process under networked environment and control valve process system, specifically addressing delays from network connection and noise. A Smith predictor based Proportional Integral (PI) controller with Internal Model Controller (IMC) and Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) are utilized as control strategies. Proposed control was conducted using User Datagram Protocol (UDP) data transfer. Based on the results indicated that the FLC is effective in mitigating the difference of network induced delays with and without noisy environment. The stability of designed controllers are also analyzed under the networked environment.

articleTitle: Design of an Integrated Collaborative Environment for Projects with Plagiarism Checker
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Integrated platforms, often referred to as integrated software or integrated systems, bring together different functionalities and tools into a unified environment. These platforms offer several advantages by streamlining processes, enhancing collaboration, and improving efficiency. The aim of this project is to create a comprehensive and integrated website for hosting student projects, with a focus on plagiarism checking and support for project contributors. The website will provide a platform for individuals to collaborate, manage, and showcase their projects in a centralized location. In addition to the traditional project management features, the website will also include a plagiarism checker to ensure that all work submitted is original and meets ethical standards. The website will also provide support and guidance for individuals who are contributing to projects, including incident handling using a chat bot. To enhance the user experience, the website will also feature a customized version of the chat GPT, where users can ask questions and resolve their doubts. By providing these additional features, the project aims to create a comprehensive solution for students and organizations looking to host and manage projects with ease and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Clustered Feature Representation Model for Predicting Crop Health and Optimizing Yield
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Machine learning applications' revolutionization of data processing and decision-making techniques has several implications for the global economy. Due to the increased need for food worldwide, agriculture is being significantly impacted. This research examines the benefits of combining machine learning algorithms with modern agriculture. Through deliberate decisions on agricultural production, these algorithms maximize crop yield while minimizing waste. To provide outcomes with great accuracy, this paper describes the use of a machine clustering mechanism for optimizing crop yield. The study includes collecting extensive data about the farm, merging online data received in real-time, and collecting data from the farmers about the verdicts that affect the crops. After analyzing fifteen distinct algorithms, the best method is determined, and an upgraded algorithm with a new feature scheme is awarded. This investigation infers a 98% classification accuracy using a clustering technique. Robust infrastructure and comfortable surroundings result from higher output rates and lower effective farming expenses.

articleTitle: Analyzing Players Performance Using PSO-CNNModel
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In the modern technological era, the applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) have been growing exponentially. The sports industry has also experienced an increased demand for AI and Machine Learning (ML) techniques to enhance both the sports business and athletic performance. By making use of deep learning models and other ML techniques, it is now possible to significantly boost an athlete's performance. These methods offer improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional manual coaching where traditional athlete performance analysis is obstructed by subjectivity, limited data, and a lack of real-time feedback. It overlooks detailed insights, offers little personalization, and focuses on past performances rather than predicting future trends. Although there are recent techniques such as GWO-CNN which are implemented, they lack simplicity and data quality. This research aims to implement the most effective optimization algorithms and deep learning techniques to enhance the performance of individual athletes as well as teams. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm-based Machine Learning model has been identified as an optimal solution for predicting athletic performance. This study also seeks to provide a deeper understanding of how ML methods can be employed to further improve player performance.

articleTitle: Development of Computer Vision Based Aluminium Scrap Sorting Using Real Time Metal Scrap Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The aluminium manufacturing industries face numerous challenges when it comes to sorting metal scraps, particularly when scraps are small in size. Traditional methods like flotation and gravity separation are inefficient, energy-intensive, and often fail when dealing with size variations. Recent advancements in computer vision and deep learning algorithms, including intelligent robotic systems, offer promising solutions. However, challenges such as accurate detection in complex environments, varying lighting conditions, and overlapping objects still persist. Newer techniques like YOLO (You Only Look Once) for real-time object detection, and Transfer Learning to improve model accuracy with smaller datasets, have shown potential. This research aims to overcome these challenges by developing an AI-powered, computer vision-based sorting system that can identify and classify aluminium scraps by color and shape at high speed. The authors developed a custom dataset and trained models using CNN architectures such as DenseNet-161, ResNet-152, and VGG 19. By employing ensemble techniques, this research achieved an 75% of accuracy.

articleTitle: Colour Recognition Using CLAHE Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
