abstract: Recently, the development of assistive devices for blind people have been increased because of the need in the society. One crucial aspect of this technology is color identification. These assistive devices are increasing their way of living and help them become less dependent on others. One of the significant challenges faced by visually challenged people is color perception. The ability to distinguish colors depends on the environmental factors. In this research, the Image restoration, Gaussian filter, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) algorithm for real- time color recognition is thoroughly studied. CLAHE is used to improve the visual contrast, which is useful during times when there are variations in lighting. The goal of the proposed method is to obtain the robust and accurate color identification in different environmental conditions. The proposed algorithm identifies the 10 colors of red, green, blue, cyan, yellow, pink, magenta, navy, beige and maroon with a precision of 94.6% and accuracy of 96.8%.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based Fraud Detection, Data Security and Privacy for Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Globally, fraud is increasing and has the potential to cost firms billions of dollars and inflict serious financial harm. Scholars hailing from several domains of application have put forth distinct methodologies. Examining these concepts can help us see the problems more clearly. Examining several approaches to fraud detection and prevention in the communications industry is the aim of this article. This paper gives a summary of the various categories of telecom fraud, problems that arise throughout the detection process, and some recommendations for how to solve them. The efficacy of the existing methodologies is documented at, succeeded by suggestions and suggestions for selecting the performance measurements that best suit the needs. There has been a notable shift in the use of advanced AI-driven solutions for fraud management in the telecom industry. The development of Generative AI is a significant breakthrough, giving CSPs powerful instruments to fight fraud. As a result of the transition from conventional to AI-based methodologies, fraud management is becoming more proactive and predictive, enabling CSPs to stay one step ahead of criminals.

articleTitle: A Smart Fire Rescue Bot Using Sensors and Arduino IDE
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The Fire Rescue bot is designed to enhance fire detection and suppression in confined spaces. Equipped with advanced sensors, including flame intensity and temperature detectors, the bot navigates through restricted areas autonomously, swiftly identifying fire outbreaks. Its compact design allows it to maneuver efficiently in tight spaces where human intervention may be challenging. Upon detecting a fire, the bot activates a small water pump mechanism to suppress the flames, mitigating potential hazards swiftly and effectively. This integration of detection and suppression capabilities provides a comprehensive solution for fire emergencies in confined environments, improving safety outcomes and minimizing property damage.

articleTitle: Optimizing Resource Allocation using Metaheuristic Approach for Load Balancing in Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Load balancing ensures equal resource allocation for optimal utilization and high user satisfaction. Recent algorithms like PSO (Particle Swarm Optimization) and ILOA (Improved Lion Optimization Algorithm) enhance Quality of Services (QoS), throughput, response time, energy consumption, and fault tolerance in cloud environments. This paper reviews load balancing techniques and parameters, showing that PSO compared with ILOA has 40% better results, than ILOA's 25%, Power Conversion's 20%, and Power Time Expense Reduction's 15%.

articleTitle: Homophily and Sentiment Analysis for Political Issues Related Discussions in Twitter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study investigates the interplay between homophily and sentiment analysis in the context of Twitter discussions surrounding Indian political issues. With the growing influence of social media on shaping public opinion and political discourse, understanding how users interact within like-minded communities and the sentiment they express towards political topics is crucial. The phenomenon of homophily, wherein individuals tend to connect with others who share similar beliefs or characteristics, has profound implications for the formation of echo chambers and polarization on social media platforms like Twitter. Concurrently, sentiment analysis techniques offer insights into the prevailing attitudes, emotions, and opinions expressed in tweets related to Indian politics. By combining homophily analysis with sentiment analysis, this study aims to reveal the dynamics of online political discourse, identify patterns of interaction within ideological communities, and determine the emotional tone surrounding key political issues. Through an interdisciplinary approach, this research sheds light on how social media platforms facilitate the amplification of certain viewpoints, the polarization of public opinion, and the implications for democracy and civic engagement in the Indian context.

articleTitle: Predicting Early Risk of Diabetes using Hierarchical Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In recent years, diabetes has become a common disease that has affected people worldwide. Many factors make people have diabetes, like heavy body weight, increased cholesterol levels, lack of physical activity, bad food habits, family history, and so on. People with diabetes for a long time can get several complications like heart disorders, kidney failure, nerve injury, foot ulcer, diabetic retinopathy, etc. However, if the disease is predicted early, the risk of body complications can be reduced and people can live healthy for long periods. In this context, we have put effort into developing an early prediction model for diabetes using the Fuzzy Logic model and implemented it through MATLAB. The human reasoning rules are formulated based on Mamdani's principle taking three inputs; FPG, 2h-PG, and HbA1c. We have conducted extensive experiments with real-time data of diabetes patients collected from a local area in Hyderabad, India to analyze the model's performance. Further, we have developed a Hierarchical Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) called Fuzzy Tree to calculate the risk factor. The performance of the Fuzzy Logic and FT models are compared. The result of the study suggests that if the input features of the human body are selected correctly, the proposed models may predict the risk of diabetes proficiently and appropriately. However, the Fuzzy Tree provides a better output than the Fuzzy Logic model.

articleTitle: Autonomous Boat: Floating Trash Collector and Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The rapid growth of floating trash in water bodies poses a significant environmental challenge worldwide, necessitating innovative solutions for efficient collection and management. Previous approaches, often relying on manual labor or stationary collection systems, have proven limited in scope and effectiveness. Some researchers have explored remote-controlled boats for trash detection and retrieval; however, these lack the autonomy and versatility required for comprehensive trash collection. This project addresses these limitations by combining autonomous navigation capabilities with a robust trash collection mechanism. By integrating GPS and intelligent sensors, our boat can autonomously navigate water bodies, and detect, and collect floating trash, and separate waste into metal and non-metal categories using an inductive proximity sensor. Additionally, the system features a backtracking capability to return to its original position for efficient waste disposal. The scalability and adaptability of our system holds promise for addressing water pollution on a larger scale, contributing to efforts toward cleaner and healthier aquatic ecosystems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Music Composition with Marker-Based Augmented Reality Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study describes the development of a marker-based Augmented Reality (AR) music composition application aimed to merge physical engagement with digital music production. Using AR technology, the program creates original music combining real-time scanning of physical markers-each coupled with a different audio beat. Designed using Unity and integrated with Vuforia, the program offers an immersive and simple interface that lets users with different musical knowledge create music via physical interactions. The ideal balance of AR and audio processing in the application provides a fresh way for music production, therefore enhancing accessibility and appeal. Emphasizing the potential of the instrument to change the way music is produced and experienced, the paper addresses conception, design, construction and instrument testing. The results show that, especially in interactive music composition, this creative exploration tool not only improves but also highlights the great artistic possibilities of AR technology. Investigated also are future advancements and possible uses for AR-based creative tools, therefore indicating a greater range of AR-based creative instruments.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Feedforward Neural Network and LSTM Model for Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Load forecasting is crucial and very vital in the management and in the control of power systems for appropriate distribution. There is need to have an efficient and accurate system to avoid wastage of energy and at the same time to forecast the demand in order to ensure that there is a reliable supply. Efficient model can generate better result and also enhance reliability. This paper aims at comparing between two neural network-based models, namely LSTM network and feedforward neural network to determine the most appropriate model to use in load forecasting. These models are developed with data of a power station in Beijing that contains temperature, humidity, wind speed and load data. The outcome of each model is assessed using ‘mean squared error’ (MSE), ‘coefficient of determination’ (R2) and the ‘mean absolute error’ (MAE). The results obtained infer that the LSTM model is better than the feedforward neural network in capturing temporal dependencies found in load data to give better predictions.

articleTitle: Implementation of Signal Processing Approach for the Intensity Transformation in Autonomous Cars
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Road transportation is a cornerstone of daily life for many, yet it also brings increased risks of accidents stemming from human error. Autonomous vehicles, driven by advancements in technology and artificial intelligence, offer a promising solution by enhancing road safety and security. Leading companies such as Google, Uber, and Tesla are heavily invested in the development of these self-driving vehicles. A critical technology underpinning autonomous cars is image processing. Cameras positioned at the vehicle's front capture data, enabling it to navigate autonomously. Effective lane detection is pivotal for these systems, involving the conversion of video input into images using techniques such as RGB to HSV thresholding. These advancements represent a significant leap towards safer and more efficient transportation systems for the future.

articleTitle: A Novel High Speed 2-Step TDC-Based All-Digital DLL for DDR SDRAM Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In sequential digital systems both Delay Locked Loops (DLLs) and the Phase Locked Loops (PLLs) are utilized for enhanced timings, i.e., to reduce the detrimental effects of distortion and instability in the circuit. An effective DLL structure with a linear delay feature has been proposed in this work. Function is accomplished by altering traditional hardware architecture. A high-speed design for All-Digital Delay-Locked Loop (ADDLL) appropriate for DDR1-DDR5 applications has been done. The suggested architecture offers the features with synchronous mirror delay and Delay Locked Loop (DLL) in a single design. TDCs are common circuits in several applications demanding final time calculations; this study offers a broad range TDC-based All-Digital Delay lock loop (AD-DLL) that is ideal for DDR usage. The AD-DLL has been implemented using 90 nm standard CMOS library at 1.2 V supply. The working range obtained from measurement results of proposed AD-DLL is 1.7 GHz to 5GHz.

articleTitle: Webcam-Guided Rover Control for Medical Waste Transport
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study aims to address the health risks posed by improper medical waste management by implementing an innovative solution: a web cam-guided rover control for medical waste transport. It is a robot that can be programmed to communicate with MATLAB over Wi-Fi to carry out different tasks. The rover autonomously navigates along the predefined paths, utilizing image processing to identify and collect medical waste. This approach eliminates the need of human intervention, thus reducing the risk of infections associated with manual waste handling. The rover hardware components incorporates Arduino Nano 33 IoT, Arduino Nano Motor Carrier, DC motor with encoder, Servo motor, Fork lifting. Wheels, Web cam and Ultrasonic Sensor.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms for Online Handwriting Recognition: A Brief Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: An online handwriting recognition system is a software application that enables the conversion of handwritten text or symbols into digital form. This system utilizes various technologies such as the processing of images, recognition of patterns, the context of machine learning, and computational intelligence to interpret handwritten content accurately. In this system, users input their handwriting through a stylus or mouse, and the software recognizes information and converts it into machine-readable text. The system can be used for a wide range of applications, including the processing of documents, note-taking, and signature verification that impacts the online handwriting system. The accuracy and efficiency of online handwriting recognition systems have improved due to technological breakthroughs in research development, making them a popular choice for various industrial innovation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Multiscale Wavelet Compression for Preserving Critical Diagnostic Features in Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: X-ray., MRI and CT scans are indispensable tools for diagnosing and treatment planning but the growth of the number of HR images is a problem in terms of storing and transmitting them. These challenges, therefore, require efficient compression techniques that will help overcome them, but at the same time maintaining key diagnostic details. In this paper, we introduce an adaptive multiscale wavelet-based method for compression of medical images. Our method uses a novel ROI detection algorithm along with a content-adaptive compression approach that compresses the different ROIs by a different level of compression since they have different diagnostic significance. Our approach was able to achieve a compression ratio of twenty to one while only breaking down 98. The quantitative analysis yielded insignificantly different structural similarity index (SSIM) of 5% for the ROI and 95 % for non-ROI area. There were no statistically significant difference between affirmative and negative images as identified by radiologists F1 scores for compressing images were statistically equal to F1 scores of original images p> 0. 05. It minimized on storage by 85% and transmission times by 78% than the uncompressed images. The research work suggested adaptive compression method provides a significant solution for bio signals and medical imaging data storage as planning, organizing and controlling the overwhelming increased usage of data in clinical and telemedicine environment.

articleTitle: Tomato TriSort: Smart Sorting System for Size, Color, and Pest Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The agricultural sector is a basic component of the national economy. The tomatoes add nutritional value to dietary items. India ranks 2nd in tomato production globally, but there is still a gap between demand and supply due to population growth. Traditional methods of grading tomatoes involve manual sorting by labor; manual sorting is expensive, with rising costs daily, and has the risk of inefficiencies, errors, etc. So, to meet the challenges, we propose a tomato sorting system that uses advanced technologies like machine learning and automation to increase accuracy and efficiency. The proposed system uses three main techniques: color sorting, size sorting, and pest detection. Color sorting for differentiating between ripe and unripe tomatoes. Pest detection uses deep learning and image processing to check the surface to detect the health of tomatoes. Size sorting to ensure uniformity. Automation reduces reliance on labor, minimizes human error, and post-harvest losses, and boosts the quality of tomatoes. The ability to grade tomatoes based on size, ripeness, color, and quality using a single system makes it unique over existing manual and flexible systems. The system is market-ready, supporting both farmers as well as traders. The system is scalable, manageable, and easy to use; moreover, it is more sustainable and profitable for agricultural practice. It is crucial in meeting the increasing demand for tomatoes and achieving the title of modern agriculture.

articleTitle: Crop Yield Prediction Based on Various Environmental Factors Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The increasing impact of climate change and global warming highlights the urgent need for sustainable agriculture practices to ensure food security. This research focuses on utilizing machine learning techniques to accurately predict crop yield based on weather conditions. By analyzing historical weather data and crop yields, the proposed machine learning models provide valuable insights for farmers in selecting suitable crops for cultivation. This approach offers a more data-driven and reliable alternative to traditional methods that rely solely on farmers' experience and local knowledge. The study evaluates the performance of various machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, XG Boost, and KNN. These models demonstrate exceptional accuracy in predicting crop yield, with values ranging from 92.12% to 97.56<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. This research contributes to the advancement of sustainable agriculture by providing farmers with a powerful tool for optimizing crop selection and improving yields. By leveraging machine learning techniques, farmers can make informed decisions and mitigate the challenges posed by climate change.

articleTitle: Internet of Things (IoT) Based BIOFLOC Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In traditional aquaculture, there remain several difficulties and challenges such as the imbalance of temperature, deficiency of oxygen and cost etc. resulting in making the fish farming process inefficient. Biofloc technology overcomes the difficulties in indoor fish culture with the help of IoT by making a suitable environment for fishes and making the culture system effective, efficient, and productive. An IoT based aquaculture model has been proposed, where different conditions of water in the culture medium are sensed by sensors. The system collects different water conditions, sends data to an associated mobile or web application via an intermediate coordinating device. Again, the imbalanced water condition is fixed via the mobile or web application with the help of the controlling device. The system can sense water temperature level and fixes it as per requirements. Changing of water in the culture medium is also possible in this system. The user can control the system's functionality via Wi-Fi access using the inbuilt Wi-Fi in NodeMCU. The NodeMCU, relay module, temperature sensor, oxygen and water pump and wireless communication protocol are the system's key components. The task is completed using open-source software and hardware with embedded devices.

articleTitle: From Queue to Score: Enhancing Effective Organ Allocation using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Transplantation of organs is a drastic measure in the treatment of persons with organ dysfunction on the terminal stage of organ failure. Nonetheless, the existing organ allocation system that depends on a seniority basis on the waiting list is not efficient enough to respond to the degree of the patients' urgency since it disregards the patient's medical status resulting in poor performances, and avoidable deaths among the patients. The research paper presents a new approach to the allocation of organs that focuses on the machine learning of the patients' severity scores which are based on patients' vital signs. Research Methodology is explorative in nature Since the approach builds upon an always available dynamic database that updated with data on what it is as regards to the patient's lung and heart conditions, blood pressure, and oxygen levels. This information is then examined by applying multiple regression analysis as a form of machine learning to derive a comprehensive severity score that indicates the level of emergency in each patient's case. Concerning the key problem of patients' deaths while waiting for transplants, the proposed system intends to improve the relationship between the degree of organs' allocation and medical necessity. The use of real-time data and a sophisticated set of AI techniques increases the equity and effectiveness of the distribution process, making it possible to deliver organs to patients requiring them most. This paper also compares patient databases in other countries including India, the probabilistic use of machine learning to arrive at severity scores and the ethical parameters of the application of AI based systems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Smart Interface for Next-Gen Monitoring in EV's
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The automotive industry is undergoing a transformative shift with the introduction of electric and hybrid vehicles, demanding a paradigm change in monitoring systems. This project introduces the “Smart Interface for Next-Gen Monitoring,” a comprehensive solution designed to transcend the limitations of traditional dashboards. The left frame of our smart interface amalgamates critical real-time parameters such as time, clock date, high and low beam indicators, speedometer, battery temperature, voltage, stability detection, smoke detection, stand alert, and three distinct operating modes. Additionally, our innovative interface introduces state-of-the-art features, including the display of the State of Health (SOH) and State of Life (SOL) of the battery, providing users with a complete understanding of their battery's performance. Furthermore, the dashboard screen is equipped to display alerts for overcurrent events, enhancing user safety and facilitating proactive maintenance. On the right frame, users access an intuitive map interface, a user-friendly keyboard, and advanced voice command functionalities. Moreover, our interface provides insightful metrics on the state of health and life of the battery, ensuring users are equipped with crucial information for optimal decision-making. This study proposes a new methodology, encompassing requirement analysis, literature review, user-centric design, integration of advanced technologies, and iterative refinement. As a result, the Smart Interface for Next-Gen Monitoring emerges as an effective solution to redefine vehicular monitoring and enhance the user experience in the era of advanced automotive technologies.

articleTitle: Low Power Linear Operational Transconductance Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The demand for transconductors that can provide linear performance under supply voltages below 0.5 V is increasing, particularly for low-power applications such as in biomedical fields. This work presents a flipped voltage follower (FVF)-based bulk-driven (BD) double diffusor double differential pair (D4P) transconductor, designed using 0.18 μm technology. The proposed design effectively operates at ±0.5 V, with a linear range of 0.2 V, a transconductance (Gm) of 1.07 μS, power dissipation of 0.365 μW, a gain of 27 dB, and a gain-bandwidth product of 27 kHz. Further analysis shows that the proposed transconductor has figure of merit values FOM1 and FOM2 of 240 and 38.06, respectively, with a linearity enhancement factor of 1.7, indicating promising performance. Monte Carlo analysis demonstrates that the Gm, gain, and total harmonic distortion have mean values of 1.48 μS, 26.13 dB, and −48.45 dB, respectively, which are close to the nominal values. The total layout area of the transconductor is 20204.54 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, providing a compact yet efficient design for low-voltage applications.

articleTitle: 128-Bit LFSR-Based Counter with Backward Carry Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: A high-speed counter is a device that is used to accurately count the events in a very fast manner. This design concept presents an LFSR referring to a Linear Feedback Shift Register-based counter with Backward Carry Propagation consisting of three stages resulting in a high counting rate due to constant delay. The first stage is implemented with the LFSR State Extension counter which covers all 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> states by making use of the State Extension counter which is integration of State Detection circuit and Galois Linear Feedback Shift Register. The second stage is the BCP counter referring to Backward Carry Propagation which is used to achieve both binary count and constant delay and it is followed by the third stage, which is the Conventional Binary counter. The LFSR State Extension circuit drives the counter and sets the counting rate maintaining constant delay. From this, we can say that speed is independent of the size of the counter. The proposed architecture is simulated and synthesized in Cadence Genus using 90nm CMOS technology with a supply voltage of 1.8V. It is operating at 2.15GHz clock frequency.

Author Keywords: Linear Feedback Shift Register State Extension counter

articleTitle: Advancing Renal Health With Inception V3: A Kidney Image Classification Study
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The efficient diagnosis and treatment of renal diseases are significantly improved by the automated classification of kidney images. An accurate and resilient kidney image classification system was developed in this research utilizing the potent Inception V3 deep learning architecture. The model under consideration is trained using a compilation of renal images that depict a wide range of pathological conditions. A series of exhaustive experiments are conducted to validate the efficacy of the kidney classification system based on Inception V3, with a comparative analysis of its performance against other cutting-edge models. The outcomes highlight the model's capacity to generate precise and dependable prognostications, thereby demonstrating its potential for pragmatic clinical implementations. The significance of outsourcing the classification of kidney images through the use of deep learning techniques, specifically the Inception V3 architecture, to increase diagnostic efficiency and accuracy. The prospective assimilation of the developed model into clinical workflows could significantly contribute to the progress of precision medicine concerning renal health.

articleTitle: Intelligent Classification System for Visual Inspection of Casting Products Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study presents a thorough method for categorizing visual examinations of casting products with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The methodology entails a comprehensive gathering and preparing a dataset comprising casting product photographs. This is done to ensure consistency and precision in training the model. The study outlines the CNN architecture, specifically built to efficiently catch and acquire complex patterns and characteristics from the images. The model attains an outstanding accuracy rate of 99% by undergoing intensive training, highlighting its strong and dependable capacity to classify casting products by visual inspection. The performance measures, including Precision, Recall, and F1-Score, are computed for the “Ok” and “Defective” categories. The results consistently demonstrate high values, indicating the model's strong capability to accurately differentiate between the two classes. The results highlight the ability of CNNs to automate and improve quality control procedures in production, offering more efficient and dependable inspection solutions for the sector.

articleTitle: Dental Cavity Detection Using U-NetArchitecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Dental cavities, which are sometimes referred to as dental caries or tooth decay, are one of the most common chronic illnesses globally and provide serious obstacles to dental treatment. The aim is to provide a proactive approach to oral health by identifying and preventing dental problems early on through the use of cavity detecting technologies. By utilizing deep learning techniques more especially, the U-Net architecture the dental cavity detection seeks to create a reliable system for the early and accurate identification of dental cavities. The system seeks to identify different dental disorders from photos utilizing the U-Net architecture with a focus on cavity identification. Model training and evaluation are made easier with the use of an annotated dataset of grayscale images. The U-Net model is trained and tuned to efficiently separate and identify dental cavities from X-ray and normal dental images by utilizing avaried dataset of dental images that have been labelled with disease information. Furthermore, accessibility is improved via a user-friendly interface, which makes it easier for people to access and use the dental detection system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Trajectory Data Privacy through Information Gain-Fused Semantic Generalization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research proposes the Information Gain-Fused Semantic Generalization Trajectory (IGFSGT) model to address the challenges of privacy preservation in digital data. Traditional trajectory data often suffers from inaccuracies and variations, hindering its effectiveness in classification and generalization. The IGFSGT model employs an optimized information gain utility function to achieve accurate node segmentation while adhering to privacy requirements. By adjusting threshold values, the model ensures that the most informative splits are selected, maximizing information gain. To further enhance performance, the model incorporates nodal transformation through semantic distances and fuzzy logics. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of IGFSGT in terms of both privacy protection and data utility compared to existing models. This research contributes to the development of privacy-preserving data publication techniques, enabling the sharing of valuable information while safeguarding sensitive data.

articleTitle: AI Powered Plant Identification and Plant Disease Classification System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Agriculture is the livelihood for thousands and thousands of people and appreciably contributes to the monetary boom of countries. a major venture in agriculture is figuring out illnesses as a result of pests and finding effective solutions for restoration. This venture ambitions to locate vegetation and their sicknesses within six one-of-a-kind families of vegetation. It includes 3 modules: preprocessing, identification, and supplementary. in the preprocessing module, the uploaded picture is in comparison with pix to be had inside the plant leaf dataset the use of augmentation techniques. The identification level includes spotting the plant and its diseases the use of a CNN. The supplementary level offers guidelines for important fertilizers to enhance the plant's situation. The undertaking makes use of a plant village dataset, overlaying six households of culmination and a total of 39 sicknesses. The device analyzes the photograph to determine if the plant is in appropriate circumstance or suffering from a sickness, and if affected, it recommends the essential dietary supplements for treatment. This proposed plant sickness category device pursuits to obtain better accuracy compared to existing systems.

articleTitle: Integrating AI for Improved Brain Tumor Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Brain cancer is one of the greatest health difficulties owing to the various and intricate structures. It is very important to identify them at an early stage and classify them correctly to enhance patients' outcomes and monitor clinical decisions. This proposed work aims to develops an effective method of improving various aspects of brain tumor detection coupled with its classification mechanism through artificial intelligence. This research work has three modules such as Brain tumor detection, segmentation and tumor classification. Algorithms and sophisticated microscopes are used for crafting a dependable method of diagnosing without the invasion of the patient's body. The approach especially involves Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) applied on large and varied brain tumor medical image datasets to classify various types of brain tumors with considerable accuracy. The proposed system utilizes brain MRI Brain Tumor dataset. Such strategies as data augmentation and transfer learning are performed in order to enhance both, model reliability and its performance. The brain tumor classification system provides higher accuracy compared to other classification techniques.

articleTitle: Stress Prediction in Higher Education Students Using Psychometric Assessments and AOA-CNN-XGBoost Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Research backs up the common perception that the years preceding up to college are the most difficult, showing that students report higher levels of discomfort and worse self-esteem during this switch. Positive personality qualities such as optimism, hope, and happiness were examined in this system along with 215 first-semester Israeli university students' ratings of functional impairment, psychological distress, and self-esteem. The three stages that make up this suggested method are data preprocessing, model training, and feature selection. In order to process data that would be infeasible to process without data preprocessing, the data can be adjusted to meet the specifications of each data mining technique. Beginning with different forms of feature classification or aggregation and progressing to individual activity levels, several levels of feature granularity were investigated in order to employ a feature selection technique. The proposed approach used an AOA-CNN-XGBoost for the whole model training phase. This novel method outperforms CNN and AOA with an average accuracy of 89.27%.

articleTitle: ML-Driven Multifaceted Classification Framework for Transport Service Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study presents a multifaceted classification framework using machine learning (ML) to evaluate transport services. The framework integrates feedback analysis, sensor-based monitoring, and travel time evaluation to provide a comprehensive assessment. The system employs LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) for sentiment analysis, categorizing feedback into Positive, Neutral, and Negative sentiments. Simultaneously, sensor data from GP2YI0I0AU0F (dust), ADXL345 (acceleration), and MQ135 (odor) undergo anomaly detection using autoencoders, classifying conditions from Excellent to Very Poor based on predefined thresholds. Travel time deviations are evaluated using autoencoders, categorizing travel experiences from Excellent (minimal deviation) to Very Poor (significant deviation). These strategies are integrated through a unified classification function, combining LSTM sentiment analysis, Random Forest rating prediction, and autoencoder-based categorizations. This approach enables actionable insights to enhance service quality through comprehensive feedback analysis, sensor monitoring, and evaluation of travel time. This ML-based framework leverages advanced techniques to improve transport service assessment, supporting informed decision-making and operational enhancements.

articleTitle: Phishing Attack Prediction using Several Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: With significant improvements in social media, banking, web technologies, smart grids, cloud, and online mobile environments, etc., cyber security is a rapidly evolving area that require close consideration. Cyber-attacks involve an organization using cyberspace to destroy, disrupt, disable, or maliciously control an IT infrastructure or compromise data confidentiality, integrity or steal organized information. The state of cyberspace bodes well for the future fragility of the Internet and the growth of its customers. Many attacks such as DoS attack, phishing attack has been identified from the review paper. Various machine learning techniques have been effectively used to solve such serious problems in the field of cyber security. Machine learning techniques are used in many scientific fields due to their unique properties such as scalability, ability, adaptability to predict security problems and quickly adapt to new and unknown problems. Deep learning methods, ensemble learning, Behavioral analysis, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Hybrid approaches and metaheuristic algorithms are used to solve the challenges like adaptability to evolving phishing tactics, data scarcity and class imbalance. This article predicts phishing attack using machine learning such as Support Vector Classifier, Logistic Regression and Random Forest Algorithm to achieve higher accuracy. The presented hybrid method will help network users to verify genuine websites, reducing the threat of phishing websites and ensuring a safe Internet experience.

articleTitle: Smart Composting Solutions for Organic Waste Management and Soil Enrichment in Agriculture with IoT and Gradient Boosting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Modern agricultural operations have significant challenges due to organic waste management since conventional approaches often prove ineffective and unsustainable. To overcome these challenges, this research suggests a new method for smart composting that combines IoT with gradient-boosting algorithms. This system accurately manages and optimizes the composting process by employing Internet of Things (IoT) sensors to monitor important factors, including temperature, moisture, pH, and oxygen content. Real-time data analysis is then performed using Gradient Boosting algorithms. By combining the IoT with gradient boosting may preventatively measures to maximize decomposition and microbial activity, which speeds up the composting process and reduces resource waste. The produced compost has higher nutritional content and more diverse microbes, making it useful as a soil supplement in farming. In addition to improving organic waste management, this novel method helps with soil enrichment and sustainable agriculture, promoting efficiency and resource conservation. Accurate sensor readings, data integration, real-time tracking, and quickly achieving optimal composting conditions are all challenges.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey on Anomaly Detection in Social Media Networks: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Social media networks have developed into a rich source of user-generated material and interactions in the quickly changing digital age. The identification of abnormal behaviour, such as spam, fake news, cyberbullying, and organized disinformation efforts, has become a crucial task due to the overwhelming volume and velocity of data collected. An extensive overview of anomaly detection methods in social media networks is given in this study article. It examines the most recent approaches, stressing the underlying algorithms, benefits, and drawbacks of each. Along with examining the difficulties encountered in real-world applications-such as scalability, data heterogeneity, and the dynamic nature of social interactions-the study also covers a variety of anomalies unique to social media platforms. This survey attempts to provide a thorough road map for researchers and practitioners seeking to improve the security, reliability, and integrity of social media platforms by looking at recent developments and highlighting open research problems.

articleTitle: Boosting Lung Cancer Prediction Accuracy Through Advanced Data Processing and Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)

authors.preferredName: N S Koti Mani Kumar Tirumanadham

abstract: This work proposes a complicated voting ensemble model for exact feature selection using AdaBoost, Catboost, XGBoost, and LARF (LASSO and Recursive Feature Elimination). This approach seeks early detection of lung cancer. Sophisticated machine learning in the model increases prediction accuracy above previous techniques. With its 94.81 % accuracy, precision, recall, and fl-scores for both “NO” and “YES” events, the ensemble approach becomes beneficial in spotting positive and negative lung cancer patients. LARF improved feature selection by giving predictive qualities top priority, hence improving model interpretability and performance at once. This model has practical applications as its speed and accuracy exceed past criteria. The results imply that the employment of numerous sophisticated algorithms to handle complicated medical data may help early and accurate detection of lung cancer be facilitated. Investigating how well the model fits in many clinical settings and how to use it with bigger patient datasets will help to validate and enhance its effectiveness.

Author Keywords: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Interquartile Range (IQR)

articleTitle: Enhancing Accuracy in Image Recognition for Deep Faked Images using Convolutional Networks Compared with Decision Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study's main goal is to improve deep fake image identification accuracy by using convolutional neural networks (CNN) and contrasting the outcomes with decision tree algorithms. Examining methods like feature extraction, transfer learning, and model evaluation can help deep fake detection systems become more reliable and effective. A dataset from Kaggle. For training and assessment, a combination of real and deep faked images is used. The dataset contains samples produced using different circumstances and methods for deep fake production. In this work, two different groups were implemented, each using a different algorithmic strategy for image identification. Group 1 utilized CNNs, or convolutional neural networks. Group 2 used the Decision Tree Algorithm, a hierarchical tree-like topology. With 20 samples in each group, there were 40 samples in total. In order to provide sufficient statistical power for further analyses, the sample size was determined. Using Clincalc.com, an a priori power analysis was performed with the statistical power (G-power) set at 80%. Behavioural science conventions were followed while choosing the significance level (alpha, a) and type II error rate (beta, β). The values selected were 0.2 and 0.05, respectively. A 95% confidence interval was chosen to assess the precision of the estimated effectiveness of the two algorithmic approaches. The accuracy of the Decision Tree was 79.2%, while the CNNs outperformed it with a 97.36% accuracy. A two-tailed significance test result showing a statistically significant p-value of 0.001 (p < 0.05) for accuracy further supported the CNN model's superiority over the Decision Tree model. This suggests that there is statistical significance to the observed variations in accuracy between the two models. Convolutional networks performed better than other models, which was explained by their skill in extracting features from pictures. To distinguish between real and deep faked images, the model must be able to recognize complex patterns and spatial correlations, which is made possible by the hierarchical convolutional layers. A priori power analysis was used to establish the sample size that was selected, which gave the study enough statistical power. The results' validity was reinforced by the 95% confidence interval, which demonstrated a high degree of accuracy in predicting the algorithmic approaches' efficacy. As seen by the significant gains in accuracy and precision measures, the study confirms that the novel CNN routinely outperforms the conventional feedforward decision tree algorithm in the field of deep fake image identification.

articleTitle: Optimising Diabetic Retinopathy Classification using EfficientNetB7
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a significant cause of vision impairment and blindness in individuals with diabetes, necessitating early and accurate detection of its various stages for effective treatment. This study applies EfficientN etB7, an advanced deep learning model, to classify different stages of diabetic retinopathy and compares its performance with other established models such as DenseN et121, Inception V3,and VGG16. The study uses datasets like the Kaggle Diabetic Retinopathy Detection and Messidor datasets, which provide annotated retinal images across multiple stages of DR: mild, moderate, severe, proliferative diabetic retinopathy, and normal. Key preprocessing techniques are employed to enhance the quality of the input data. These include noise reduction, contrast enhancement using CLAHE, and data augmentation to enhance the model's reslience. EfficientNetB7 is selected due to its optimal network depth, width, and resolution balance, which facilitates high accuracy with fewer computational resources. The model's performance is evaluated using metrics including Fl score, accuracy, precision, and recall, which are crucial for assessing the reliability of medical image classification models. Comparative analysis reveals that EfficientN etB7 outperforms DenseNet121, InceptionV3, and VGG16 across all evaluation metrics. Specifically, EfficientN etB7 achieves superior accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl score in classifying the different stages of diabetic retinopathy. These results highlight the effectiveness of EfficientN etB7 in providing reliable and efficient detection of diabetic retinopathy, highlighting its potential for improving clinical outcomes through early and precise diagnosis.

articleTitle: Order Reduction of Autonomous Microgrids using Pade and Routh Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Model order reduction (MOR) is an analytical or numerical methodology of reduced dimension. A specific computational process to create a low-order approximation that preserves the unique property of the high-order model and retains the basic characteristics of the model. The primary benefits of MOR include enhanced understanding and modeling of complex subsystems with dominant accuracy, acceleration of the design cycle, improved system efficiency, and reduced computational demands. This paper presents a methodology for reducing the model order of autonomous microgrids using both the Routh-approximation method (RAM) and the Markov Parameters (MaPs) & Time Moments (TiMs) method. This novel approach simplifies the power system model while ensuring stability and accuracy. Specifically, the methodology involves numerator reduction using MaPs & TiMs and denominator reduction via the Routh Approximation Method. An eighth-order microgrid model is reduced to second and third-order models. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations demonstrate that these reduced models adequately capture the key features of the full system, making them suitable for control and stability studies. Different responses, including step response, impulse response, phase response, and Nyquist response, are provided for the proposed autonomous MG. The chief strength of the mixed-methods approach is that it always brings out a simple and stable structural lower order to preserve the critical features of this type of virtual space organization system. The accuracy of this proposed work is highly effective and significant in the following aspects.

articleTitle: Optimizing Hospital Stay Duration Prediction using IoT and Linear Regression Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Accurate hospital stay length prediction is critical for effective patient care and resource allocation. To improve the precision of hospital, stay length prediction, this research presents using the Internet of Things (IoT)-assisted Linear Regression (LR) model. Using IoT devices and sensors installed across healthcare facilities, it collects real-time data on various variables impacting patients' stays, including vital signs, room occupancy, prescription delivery, and staff actions. It builds an LR model that can accurately predict the length of hospital stays by integrating this rich information with past patient records. Due to factors such as the ever-changing nature of patients' ailments, the intricacy of medical treatments, and the unpredictability of healthcare procedures, the proposed method overcomes some of the challenges inherent in predicting the length of a hospital stay. The algorithm improves prediction accuracy by responding to changing conditions in real time by monitoring patient data and ambient variables using IoT devices. The most important factors for stay length prediction to improve the model's performance are chosen using feature selection approaches. The effectiveness of the IoT-assisted LR model is assessed using real-world hospital data and conventional regression methodologies. This method outperforms the competition in estimating how long patients will remain in the hospital, improving patient care, streamlining hospital operations, and making better use of available resources. Challenges include making sure models are accurate and understandable, managing real-time processing needs, and managing patient conditions that might vary widely.

articleTitle: Improving Microgrid Reliability and Efficiency Through Energy Storage Systems with a Pyramidal Dilation Attention Convolutional Neural Network for Renewable Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Microgrid (MG) design and deployment are heavily reliant on reliability. Integrating renewable energy sources (RESs) into power grids poses considerable challenges for maintaining grid reliability due to their intermittent nature. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhance grid stability by incorporating Energy Storage Systems (ESS) coupled with Pyramidal Dilation Attention Convolutional Neural Network (PDACNN). The goal of the proposed method is to improve efficiency and lower electricity costs. The proposed PDACNN optimizes the control of Energy Storage Systems by providing more trustworthy forecasts of energy demand as well as supply. By, then the proposed method is implemented in MATLAB and evaluated their performance with various existing methods. The PDACNN method surpasses existing techniques in both efficiency and cost-effectiveness. It achieves a high efficiency of 95.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and reduces total electricity costs to $650/kWh, outperforming the Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Recurrent NN (RNN) and Convolutional NN (CNN) methods.

Author Keywords: Pyramidal Dilation Attention Convolutional Neural Network

articleTitle: Optimized Siamese Humboldt Squid Attention Network Architecture for Cyber-Attack Detection in IoT 4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The rapid expansion of IoT within Industry 4.0 has heightened the risk of cyber-attacks, underscoring the need for advanced detection mechanisms. Existing cyber-attack detection systems in this context often struggle with reduced accuracy, high computational time, complexity, and elevated error rates. This study addresses these challenges by proposing an Optimized Siamese Humboldt Squid Attention Network (OSH-SqAtNet) architecture for cyber-attack detection in IoT Industry 4.0 environments. The input data, sourced from datasets like CSE-CIC-IDS2018, undergoes preprocessing via a Mixture of Conventional Fast Bilateral Filter (MC2FB) to enhance data quality. A Gold Rush Optimizer (GRO) is then employed for feature selection, isolating the most significant features to optimize classification performance. The preprocessed and optimized data are classified using the OSH-SqAtN et architecture for accurate cyber-attack detection. For secure data transmission, Rabin Fuzzy Cryptosystem assisted Elliptic Curve Cryptography (RFC-ECC) is utilized. Experimental simulations conducted on the Python platform reveal that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques, achieving higher accuracy (98%) and recall (0.993%). These results demonstrate the approach's superior efficacy and potential for advancing cybersecurity in IoT Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Impact of AI and ML on Employee Job Satisfaction and Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research thoroughly investigates the impact of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence(AI) on employee work performance as well as job contentment. Six distinct algorithms were evaluated: Random Forests, XGBoost, AdaBoost, Support Vector Regression(SVR), Decision Trees, and Linear Regression for predicting staff satisfaction and efficiency based on factors such as department, experience level, access to training, and other variables. The investigation employs data preprocessing techniques, like StandardScaler, to ensure each feature contributes equally to the analysis, and uses train-test splitting to separate information for training and evaluating models. Among the algorithms tested, SVR emerged as the top performing model, displaying superior precision in anticipating worker outcomes. SHAP values are used to point the components that significantly affect the model's forecasts of productivity and satisfaction. Some employees thrive in roles that continuously introduce them to new problems, whereas others prefer tasks that do not frequently change. This methodology offers an inter-pretable and accurate way to identify and evaluate most relevant factors of employee outcomes. With the power of these cutting-edge ML methods, organisations can delve deeper into analyzing their employees' performance. This data-driven approach will result in better work environment, focused training programs and finally a happy working force. The study reiterates the promise of AI-ML in addressing intricate workplace nuances to drive strategic workforce policy changes meant to boost employee happiness, and organisational efficiency.

articleTitle: Developing a Diabetes Prediction Decision Support System with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Chronic diseases like diabetes pose a major threat to global healthcare, with estimates suggesting an increase from 382 to 1 million cases in 2013 to 692 million by 2050. Characterized by high blood sugar and symptoms such as increased thirst and hunger, diabetes complications occur if a person has this ailment and does not take care of her health properly. Normally, our body converts food into fuel (glucose), and the pancreas produces insulin, a hormone that unlocks cells and allows glucose entry. There are different types of diabetes of which the main categories are type 1 and type 2. To improve early detection, scientists are using machine learning, a field that allows machines to learn from experience. This project explored the combination of various machine learning algorithms for more precise identification of early diabetic symptoms. After evaluating the accuracy of various algorithms, including Gaussian Naive Bayes 96.43%, Support Vector Machine 96.69%, Linear Regression 98.52%, and Decision tree 98.86%, we have chosen the decision tree algorithm for its superior performance.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey of Image Segmentation for Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Medical imaging is the field in which doctors take the images of different interior body parts with the help of different techniques. This helps the medical professionals to do the diagnosis and treatment. Medical image analysis enhances the results of clinical research and it also helps to give better treatment solutions to the patients. Medical image processing includes tasks such as registration, segmentation, feature extraction, and classification. Segmentation of the medical images is a critical stage in the medical images processing, particularly as a necessary precondition for effective diseases diagnosis and therapy. Deep learning has gained popularity as a method for segmenting images. U-Net and its variations are currently the most extensively used method. Additionally, transformer-based models like TransUNet have given remarkable performance on different medical image datasets, with the higher success of pre-trained models in natural language processing field. The other hand these techniques have undergone some drawbacks. Considering CNN, It focuses only on local data and ignores global data. U Net networks are slow to utilize, parameter-heavy, and computationally demanding. The Transformer-based model has significant computational overhead. We have surveyed by summarizing segmentation methods in medical imaging. Additionally, we talked about well-liked segmentation strategies as they would be helpful to researchers in the future.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Mentor Service Advising Application for Timely Course Completion using RNN/LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: To be precise, time is a very sensitive factor that concerns course completion in colleges. MOOCs and other such sources of online learning have begun to make education accessible to everyone. One of the significant problems that exist in the course of studying is the fact that so many students flunk. The study recommends an AI-based mentor service thus integrating an advising app that will ensure that students complete their courses on time. The program applies the AI and ML to provide the academic planning of performance and direction, immediate assistance and constant feedback to students, resulting in higher scores and enhanced satisfaction levels. Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN s) and in particular the implementation of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are applied to an innovative virtual mentor service which allows the generation of individual learning pathways and enhancement of completion time for online students. The LSTM network determines and categories how the students are transitioning throughout the course content and distinction between the zones of strength and areas that might require the students to be guided. Possible Challenges With the help of the technology, a student might indicate such problems as being lost at a topic or lagging behind Growth of learning patterns can be estimated. Proposing specific actions As regards barrier-related knowledge deficits, the system provides specific recommendations in terms of special approaches. Such interventions may comprise of suggesting new resources that include products, or skillful practice sessions, or even different learning resources. Accelerate Completion The technology to complete courses in time based on students' performance as well as recommendations. It was used for Comparing therapies and suggestion using experiments hence used as AlB Tool. The rationale of this approach is to enhance timely completion of courses and consequently the results of learning processes.

articleTitle: Automated Heart Disease Diagnosis and Monitoring System Using Similarity-Navigated Graph Neural Networks with Leopard Seal Optimization in IoT Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: One of the leading causes of death worldwide continues to be heart disease; therefore, early detection and precise diagnosis are essential to better patient outcomes. The conventional methods of diagnosing chemotherapy-induced nail changes involve a great deal of laboratory testing, which is more than exhaustive. In order to tackle these obstacles, this research introduces a novel methodology for the automated diagnosis and continuous tracking of heart diseases in the IoT -based health care system, integrated with deep learning algorithms. The proposed system includes several state-of-the art techniques to improve diagnostic reliability and speed. First of all, min-max normalization is used as a pre-processing technique that aims at pre-scaling the data of patients to a consistent level and, as a result, enhancing the performance of the model. The Mud Ring Algorithm is then used for feature selection, whereby the best features are chosen together with the reduction in dimensionality to decrease computational intensity, thus improving diagnostic accuracy. The core diagnostic engine is based on Similarity Navigated Graph Neural Networks (SNGNN) and has been enhanced with Leopard Seal Optimization (LSO), a new meta-method motivated by the hunting patterns of leopard seals. This combination enables the system to relate various features and give the correct prognosis for heart diseases. These techniques, applied within the IoT framework, enable real-time monitoring and diagnosis and therefore have the benefit of being a scalable solution for modern health care systems. The results show that the proposed method for providing diagnosis of heart disease is accurate, timely, and reliable and thus has the potential to revolutionize patient management in healthcare based on the IoT.

articleTitle: Advancing Reversible Data Hiding using GAN-Enhanced Steganography and Cryptography Synergy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In today's world, data security and privacy remain as significant challenges. Reversible data hiding (RDH) is a technique used to embed data into cover media in a manner that allows both the embedded data and the original media to be recovered. Unlike traditional data hiding techniques, which permanently alter the cover media, RDH ensures that the original content can be restored exactly as it was before embedding. The concept of RDH relies on the fact that the embedded data does not cause irreversible distortion or permanent damage to the cover media. In addition to this feature, it is crucial to enhance the data security of hidden information. This paper introduces a methodology that combines Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) with steganography and cryptography techniques to advance reversible data hiding and enhance data security. By integrating Generative AI -enhanced steganography, the paper aims to embed data within cover images in a reversible manner, ensuring that the original media can be recovered with improved image quality compared to the original image. Furthermore, the integration of cryptography techniques ensures the integrity and confidentiality of the concealed data, making it resistant to unauthorized access and detection. The synergy between Generative AI -driven steganography and cryptography in RDH helps sustain key elements of reversible data hiding, including reversibility, embedding capacity, and data security. Enhancing performance can be applied in various fields such as medical imaging, forensics, intellectual property protection, secure communications, and military applications.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of FUTCOM and NASDAQ Commodities for Gold using Machine Learning and Technical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This paper covers commodity stock market (FUTCOM and NASDAQ) data using machine learning and technical analysis. Commodity stock markets play a crucial role in global economies, affecting everything from raw material prices to consumer goods. Their inherent volatility and sensitivity to geopolitical and economic factors make them challenging to predict. Addressing the prime problem of price fluctuations, this research highlights the need for accurate forecasting models, where machine learning can significantly enhance decision-making and risk management. It includes data preprocessing, RNN model creation, future price prediction, descriptive stats, correlation analysis, volatility, trend analysis, seasonality, volume analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation. Using Pandas, NumPy, TensorFlow, and Plotly libraries, it provides insights into market trends and forecasting. Results are intended for market participants and decision-makers,

articleTitle: Building a Secure and Scalable Finance Chatbot: Client-Server Architecture, Load Balancing, and TLS Security
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research introduces a new and improved model for a financial chatbot based on deep learning, machine learning, and natural language processing to provide suitable financial services and increase the financial literacy of users. It utilizes a detailed financial database, another complex machine learning structure for market forecasts., and natural language processing to parse user questions. Moreover, there is the customer resource management feature that applies machine learning in the analysis of financial data and natural language processing for understanding the user”s intent. The paper also looks into the use of transport layer security (TLS) encryption to secure the flow of the sensitive information, the data that is to be transmitted from the chatbot server to the user clients. By integrating the dimensions of concepts such as financial analysis, personal finance advice, and data transmission, this research provides an extensive and secure approach to improving one”s financial situation.

articleTitle: Efficient Vehicle Tracking and Authentication with YOLOv8: Integrating Deep Learning and OCR for Real-Time License Plate Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Computer vision plays an important role in this technology-driven world. Using computer vision, the images can be acquired and processed to achieve the high dimensional data of the images. In late 1960s computer vision was start emerging which is considered as the colonist for the latest technology Artificial intelligence. The machine learning and deep learning comes under the artificial intelligence as the subsets. The object detection falls under the category of computer vision. Tracking of each license plate is considered as a most difficult task as the population increases massively day by day. Also, to identify whether a vehicle is authorized or unauthorized in distinct environment is a challenging one. When the population becomes higher and higher leads to many complications such as vehicle theft, misusing vehicles, and unauthorized accessing of vehicles. To overcome these issues many algorithms are handled and the best method is done with the deep learning algorithm. The project aims at designing a system by training the model using deep learning which allows to detect the number plate accurately using open cv module and then the text of number plate is extracted using optical character recognition (OCR) and thus fixed database is compared with the code written in python and thus the vehicle can be detected whether it is authorized or unauthorized. By implementing this project, the complications associated with the detection of vehicles can be overcome. This project aims at designing a most efficient and conceded way for detecting the license plates. For this purpose, the deep learning method is handled which follows the basic algorithm CNN (convolution neural networks) and the model created using the deep learning method follows the YOLOv8, the latest version used for the object detection. In this process the YOLOv8 (you only look once) is handled to make the detection easier since it follows the single neural network to identify the boundary boxes and the class of the trained model. CNN is the considered a for the mathematical calculation as it is the best method for the detection of license plate in real time through openCV camera.

articleTitle: Securing Mobile Adhoc Network with Quantum Key Distribution: An Experimental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Mobile adhoc networks (MANETs) are characterized by their dynamic and decentralized nature, making them inherently vulnerable to security threats. This paper proposes a novel security framework that integrates Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) with error correction, privacy amplification, and distributed key management to enhance the security of MANETs. The experimental analysis was conducted using simulations to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework across various node densities and mobility patterns. Our results demonstrate improved security in key exchanges but also highlight trade-offs in network performance metrics such as throughput and latency.

articleTitle: Securing Neural Network in the Cloud: A Systematic Approach of Cloud Security Based on ANN-SVM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Many services have made the transition to the cloud because of the increased reliability and efficiency of cloud computing. Due to their capacity to ease service access while also securing communications in the public network, the three-factor Mutual Authentication and Key Agreement (MAKA) protocols are seeing increased use in multi-server designs. A lack of formal security proof or high communication and computation costs makes the limited three-factor MAKA protocols that are currently available susceptible to a wide range of attacks. The proposed approach consists of three phases, which are preprocessing, feature selection, and model training. Text scheduling and normalization make up preprocessing. In feature selection, the PSO is an optimization method that uses a population-based approach to find optimal solutions. An ANN-SVM was employed throughout the model's training phase. With an average accuracy of 93.30%, the proposed technique surpasses ANN and SVM.

articleTitle: Navigating the Dark: Advances in Robotic Night Patrol with D-Block Mask Electric EEL Dense Nested R-CNN for Enhanced Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Ensuring safety and security during nighttime operations remains a critical challenge for automated surveillance systems, often hindered by limited visibility, sensor noise, and inadequate data processing techniques. To overcome these limitations, an advanced robotic night patrol system is proposed, utilizing the D-block Mask Electric Eel Dense Nested R-CNN (D-Mask-EEDN-R-CNN). This system acquires data from multiple sensors implemented on robotic units, which saves it in a Firebase database instantly. The noise that hinders the correct interpretation of the data is eliminated and data quality improved in the pre-processing stage with the help of Improved Sage-Husa Adaptive Kalman Filter (SHAKF). The data is then passed through feature extraction and, classification by the proposed D-Mask-EEDN-R-CNN network which is fine-tuned by the E2FOP for better performance. This system has been developed in Python and the efficiency of this system, in fact, is very high, it is 99.9% accuracy and 99.8% improvements on average thus yielding better recall results than existing methods. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing the accuracy and reliability of robotic night patrols, providing a robust solution for improving nighttime safety and security.

articleTitle: Influence of COVID-19 in Tourism: A Sentiment Analysis of Twitter Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study investigates the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on Thailand's tourism-driven economy by analyzing English-language tweets related to tourism from July to December 2020. Utilizing advanced machine learning models-Logistic Regression, Decision Tree Classifier, XGBoost Classifier, and the Pelican Optimization Algorithm-we aimed to understand the sentiments and intentions expressed in these tweets. The research analysis revealed high predictive accuracy, with Logistic Regression achieving 98%, Decision Tree Classifier 99%, XGBoost Classifier 96%, and Pelican Optimization Algorithm 94.5%. These results highlight the importance of addressing concerns related to COVID-19 and political tensions to support the recovery of Thailand's tourism sector. The research also highlights the critical role of information and communications technology (ICT) in managing and revitalizing the tourism industry, especially in the context of reduced consumer spending and travel restrictions. Social media platforms, particularly Twitter, were used to gauge public sentiment and inform recovery strategies. The proposed methodology included extensive data collection, cleaning, and natural language processing, followed by the application of various machine learning algorithms to analyze and interpret sentiment data. The findings offer actionable insights for enhancing tourism marketing strategies and improving the sector's resilience amid ongoing pandemic challenges.

articleTitle: Cloud-Connected Wearable Devices for Lone Worker Protection With Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Various sectors continue to prioritize lone worker safety, which requires creative ways to provide quick support and monitoring. To safeguard lone workers, this paper introduces a new method that makes use of cloud-connected wearable devices that are coupled with Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). The system design relies on sensors embedded in wearable devices that can monitor a range of environmental elements as well as the vital signs of workers. A central cloud platform receives data in real-time via wireless communication from these devices and processes and analyzes it. The system may detect possible dangers or crises using smart techniques and immediately notify those who are supposed to react or the proper authorities. Cloud computing also makes it easy to store, analyze, and monitor large amounts of data over time, which is great for doing proactive risk assessments and improving safety standards. It demonstrates solution's capacity to improve lone worker safety, reduce reaction times, and mitigate hazards via simulations and actual deployment scenarios, efficacy and dependability. This growing body of knowledge on how to protect lone workers in various workplaces by using the power of IoT and cloud computing.

articleTitle: Optimizing Predictive Maintenance in Mechanical Engineering: AI and ML for Lathe Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) of machines using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) is an emerging and rapidly growing field within Mechanical Engineering. By leveraging AI and ML algorithms, engineers can analyse vast amounts of data collected from sensors and other monitoring devices to predict when machinery components will likely fail. In continuous flow production systems, the combination of AI and machine learning ML for PdM is presently reaching a peak., yet its penetration into machines within small and medium-scale enterprises remains comparatively subdued.
