This complexity, coupled with the of-ten poor long-term survival rates for brain cancer patients, under-scores the critical need for advanced diagnostic tools and method-ologies. By combining the advantages of VGG-16 and ResNet-SO, the proposed hybrid model improves the performance of existing brain tumor detection models, resulting in more reliable and ac-curate feature learning. In contrast to conventional models that depend on a single CNN architecture, the hybrid model makes use of ResNet-5O's residual learning to capture intricate patterns and VGG-16's capacity to extract detailed features. This combination improves the model's capacity to identify cancers more accurately. Utilizing both architectures also reduces overfitting and improves generalization across various datasets. The hybrid model provides a more complete diagnostic tool by classifying different tumor types (meningioma, pituitary tumors, and gliomas), whereas many existing models concentrate on binary classification. Through the division of brain images into smaller sections for in-depth examination, the integration of these advanced techniques enables more precise tumor detection. After being trained on three publicly accessible brain MRI datasets, the model exhibits exceptional resilience and applicability, with an average of 97% for ac-curacy, precision, recall, and Fl-score. This excellent performance highlights the model's capacity to distinguish between tissues im-pacted by tumors and those that are not, thereby offering physi-cians a useful tool. Patients with brain cancer may benefit greatly from this model's increased precision and effectiveness in terms of early detection and treatment results. This method is useful in clinical settings since it speeds up the tumor diagnosis process and lessens the need for radiologists' manual skill. The practical solutions this research offers to improve early diagnosis and increase survival rates in cases of brain cancer go beyond its scholarly achievements. In the end, this paradigm gives medical professionals a more precise and effective way to rec-ognize and categorize brain tumors, which enhances patient out-comes and care.

articleTitle: TDA-SSNN: Efficient Hybrid Top-Down Attention Siamese Sparrow Neural Network for Automatic Drone Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly employed in diverse applications such as military operations, delivery services, traffic and architectural monitoring, and aerial surveillance. These drones often encounter challenges in navigating complex and dynamic environments, including irregular object shapes, occlusions, and varying contrasts with backgrounds. To overcome these obstacles, this study presents a novel hybrid approach that integrates Top-Down Attention with a Siamese Sparrow Neural Network (TDA-SSNN) for efficient and data-driven drone navigation. The methodology begins with sourcing input images from publicly available datasets, including those from Udacity's project. To enhance image quality, the Robust Generalized Maximum Blake-Zisserman Total Correntropy (RMB-ZTC) adaptive filter is employed for preprocessing. Feature selection is performed using a novel Gorilla Troops Optimizer with Artificial Hummingbird Optimization (GTO-AMO). For automatic drone navigation, the TDA-SSNN is utilized, enhanced by an advanced Sparrow Search Algorithm to optimize the performance of the Top-Down Attention-based Siamese Neural Network. The proposed approach achieves a remarkable accuracy of 99.6%.

articleTitle: An Intensive Review on Deep Learning Approaches in Non-Invasive Fetal Healthcare Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Fetal health care is one of the most crucial concerns in today's world. Evaluating fetal well-being has always been challenging. Proper development and monitoring of the fetus are indispensable for its growth and healthy life. Monitoring and diagnosing abnormalities at the right gestational age is very significant. There are remarkable technical advancements in fetal well-being evaluation, bridging the gap between prenatal medicine and Artificial intelligence. This study provides an intensive review of various modes of non-invasive data that can be used for fetal health monitoring and decision support. Also, existing studies on fetal health care that use deep learning techniques for diagnosis and monitoring are explored. Also, a generic framework designed for an Automated Fetal healthcare Monitoring system using AI approaches is presented.

articleTitle: Real-Time Traffic Flow Optimization using Adaptive IoT and Data Analytics: A Novel DeepStreamNet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Thisstudy introduces the DeepStreamNet model, an advanced framework for enhancing real-time traffic management in urban environments using adaptive IoT and sophisticated big data analytics. Central to our approach is the integration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and long short-term memory (LSTM) units, which synergize with IoT devices to facilitate dynamic adaptation to fluctuating traffic conditions. The model excels in operational performance, achieving a notable accuracy of 94.7% in congestion prediction with an exceptionally low latency of only 45 ms per decision cycle and the capability to process up to 50,000 data points per second. These technical achievements have marked significant improvements over traditional traffic management systems, enhancing traffic flow efficiency and reducing congestion effectively. The results underscore the transformative potential of the DeepStreamNet model in urban traffic management and public safety, offering actionable insights for intelligent transportation systems and setting the stage for more informed urban planning. Looking forward, we suggest extending the application of our model to areas such as logistics and broader smart city initiatives, highlighting its adaptability and broad utility in various urban contexts

articleTitle: Enhanced CNN Model for Lettuce Disease Identification in Indoor Aeroponic Vertical Farming Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: India, like many other nations, heavily relies on agricultural exports to fund its national budget. Economic losses may occur when crop and plant diseases reduce production quality and quantity. Hence, it is crucial to detect infections early on in crop farming. Commercial crops grown using aeroponic vertical farming techniques include lettuce in particular. To increase the crop yield, the crop should be free from disease-causing agents like viral, bacterial, or fungal. As a response, scientists have utilized deep learning algorithms for the automatic identification of abnormalities in both indoor and outdoor farming crops by capturing leaf images. In this work, fine-tuned convolutional neural networks (CNN) were utilized to identify diseases in the aeroponic lettuce crops in an effective manner. Further, the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) were fine-tuned by training them on lettuce images. While testing, a higher accuracy of 95.6258% was achieved. Hence, this research work signifies that the proposed model would be appropriate for lettuce disease classification in controlled environment agriculture.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Communication with Parrot-Optimized Orientation-Aware Graph Neural Network for Next-Generation IoT Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Effective communication between autonomous vehicles is essential for ensuring their safe and efficient operation. This research introduces Parr-OrAGNet, a novel approach that addresses the limitations of traditional communication methods in IoT automotive networks. Parr-OrAGNet integrates Macro-Micro Depth Normalization (MaMiDN) for accurate data normalization, Orientation-Aware Graph Neural Network (OrAGNet) for enhanced neural network modeling, and Parrot Optimizer (ParrOpt) for optimization. This combined approach effectively reduces packet loss, communication overhead, and latency. The evaluation results demonstrate significant improvements in communication efficiency, with a 97% reduction in packet loss and a 95% decrease in communication overhead. Additionally, Parr-OrAGNet achieves exceptional performance metrics in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of autonomous vehicle communication by establishing a new benchmark for performance and scalability. Parr-OrAGNet offers a promising solution for addressing the challenges of IoT automotive networks and paving the way for the realization of fully autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Innovative Solar Ironing System: Combining Renewable Energy with Advanced Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study introduces an innovative solar-based ironing system that integrates renewable energy with advanced deep-learning techniques to optimize energy consumption in household ironing operations. The system harnesses solar panels to collect solar energy, ensuring efficient ironing during daylight hours. In cases of insufficient solar generation, the system automatically switches to a conventional power supply, guaranteeing uninterrupted functionality. A key feature of this system is incorporating a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, which predicts solar power output based on historic data and real-time climate information sourced from the OpenWeatherMap API. This predictive capability enhances energy management by providing timely insights into expected solar energy availability, allowing users to plan ironing tasks effectively. Data preprocessing techniques, including imputation of missing values using the median and normalization, ensure the quality and reliability of the input data for training the LSTM model. The model is assessed using various performance metrics and compared to traditional forecasting methods, including ARIMA, Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Feedforward Neural Networks (FNN). The results demonstrate that the LSTM model significantly outperforms these alternatives in predicting solar energy generation. This research contributes to sustainable living by promoting renewable energy usage in everyday tasks and illustrates the potential of combining deep learning with solar technologies for improved energy efficiency in household applications.

articleTitle: Intelligent Performance Enhancement of Sentiment Analysis for Social Data Collection in Big Data Management
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: With the widespread popularity of social networks, effective data analysis is the current research focus. This study focuses on improving the performance of sentiment analysis in social data collection under the big data management framework. Social network datasets have become an important source of understanding social behavior and providing effective information. With the widespread application of the magic of big data, the scale of these highly concurrent, rigidly complex data sets continues to increase, which requires powerful methods to analyze the data while addressing user preference issues. Therefore, this study proposes a new intelligent approach model to enhance sentiment analysis by enhancing the big data management tools and techniques. Key methodologies include using advanced data processing frameworks such as R and Python for text mining and social network analysis, leveraging Spark's distributed processing capabilities, and implementing stable indexing and query capabilities through Elasticsearch. In addition, the research integrates efficient web crawling technology and secure data access protocols (such as OAuth 2.0) for social data collection. Experimental results conducted on Tencent Weibo data show that the accuracy of sentiment analysis significantly improves over multiple tests, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The accuracy gradually improved from the initial 78.5% to 93.5%, confirming the reliability of the implemented algorithm and framework.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Load Prediction with Advanced Metering Infrastructure Using Relational Bi-Level Aggregation Graph Convolutional Network and Coronavirus Mask Protection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) in smart grids (SGs) facilitates detailed energy usage monitoring and load forecasting, but it faces drawbacks related to data accuracy and error rates in measurements. These inaccuracies can lead to flawed load predictions and inefficiencies in power distribution. Moreover, the reliability of AMI systems can be compromised by errors in data transmission and processing. To overcome these drawbacks, this manuscript proposes an AMI with power distribution in SG for short-term load prediction using RBAGCN- CMPA approach. The data are collected from historical dataset of Taiwan. Subsequently, the data are given to pre-processing. In pre-processing, removes the missing values and normalization in the data utilizing Maximum Correntropy Quaternion Kalman Filter (MCQKF). The pre-processed output was fed to feature selection using High Level Target Navigation Pigeon Inspired Optimization (HLTNPIO) has selecting features of historical dataset. After selection the output was fed to Relational Bi-level Aggregation Graph Convolutional Network (RBAGCN) for predicting short-term three phase load of SG. The Coronavirus Mask protection Algorithm (CMPA) is used to enhance the weight structure of RBAGCN. The proposed RBAGCN-CMPA is utilized within the MATLAB platform. Performance metrics including precision, accuracy, recall and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), were examined in order to determine the proposed method. The proposed RBAGCN-CMPA technique yield 23.70%, 23.21%, 25.52% high accuracy, 21.17%, 25.22%, 25.35% high recall and lower RMSE when analysed the existing methods. The proposed RBAGCN-CMPA method is compared with the existing approaches for instance Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTMN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Multi Perceptron (MLP), respectively.

Author Keywords: Relational Bi-level Aggregation Graph Convolutional Network
High Level Target Navigation Pigeon Inspired Optimization

articleTitle: Artistic Fusion: AI Powered Artistry for Story Boarding
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Storyboarding is a crucial pre-production step in filmmaking, facilitating the visualization and planning of scenes. However, traditional methods have obstacles such as manual labour, artistic skill requirements, and limitations in dynamic scene representation. This paper presents an innovative AI-powered storyboard generator leveraging Stable Diffusion, implemented in PyTorch. The research addresses obstacles in traditional methods by automating the storyboard creation process, enhancing visual realism, and promoting collaborative filmmaking workflows. The AI-powered system integrates advanced generative techniques to simulate complex visual scenarios, from lighting variations to dynamic camera movements, ensuring a more accurate preview of the final cinematic experience. By utilizing text prompts, the model interprets narrative elements and mood, aligning generated visuals with creative intent. The integration of Stable Diffusion model allows for controlled noise introduction, enhancing realism and immersion in storyboarded scenes. Further, an average improved accuracy of 82% is witnessed when compared to existing methodologies like Dreambooth and LoRA. Key features include a user-friendly interface for intuitive operation, compatibility with diverse media types, and iterative refinement capabilities to fine-tune storyboard quality. Evaluation metrics such as Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) demonstrate the system's efficacy in producing high-quality visuals that meet filmmakers' expectations.

articleTitle: Intelligent Cyber-Physical Systems: Integrating Machine Learning and Federated Learning for Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The incorporation of Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) promises to revolutionize their capabilities, enabling autonomous decision-making, predictive analytics, and real-time data processing. Traditional CPS are prone to high latency and data privacy concerns due to centralized processing models. Federated learning facilitates united model training amongst numerous decentralized CPS nodes, confirming data confidentiality and security while minimizing bandwidth usage. The architecture includes core components such as data acquisition modules, federated ML model training, interference engines, and robust communication protocols. The results indicate enhanced predictive accuracy, reduced downtime, and increased operational efficiency. The challenges of deploying AI/ML in CPS, including computational resource constraints, real-time processing requirements, and the need for explainability and transparency in ML decisions, are also addressed. The importance of robust data management and secure communication channels to maintain system integrity and reliability is discussed. Future research directions include integrating advanced AI techniques such as reinforcement learning and exploring the ethical implications of deploying AI/ML in CPS. This research contributes to the field by offering a structured methodology for incorporating federated learning into CPS architectures, paving the way for more intelligent, autonomous, and resilient systems capable of adapting to complex and evolving environments.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Interpretability in AI and Its Implications for Trust in Critical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: With the advent of deep learning (DL) and other advancements in machine learning, artificial intelligence has recently taken the globe by storm. The requirement for openness and interpretability has arisen as computing power has reached superhuman capability; its absence is a serious problem in industries like healthcare and finance, where trust is crucial because of its enormous impact on human lives. This necessitates more interpretability, which often means understanding the algorithmic system. Unfortunately, there are still a lot of unanswered questions regarding the DL. Our knowledge of machine decision-making is still incomplete. We provide an overview and categorize the interpretabilities provided by different studies. However, there is a significant disadvantage with AI: people would see it as a “black box,” which would erode trust in its trustworthiness. In a field where decisions can literally mean the difference between life and death, this is a severe issue. Considering different application domains and activities, this study offers a thorough overview of the literature on the latest developments in XAI approaches and assessment metrics.

articleTitle: Optimizing Crisis Management with Advanced UAV Imaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The UAV systems that are fitted with current technology have helped in boosting the crisis management activities such as disaster relief operations, search and rescues, and policing. This paper integrates the developmental function of advanced detective UAVs into episodes of crises. These UAVs are capable of quickly and effectively assessing the damage, find people and observe post-disaster occurrences through with the help of complicated image analysis. It incorporates cameras with HD resolutions, thermal imagery systems, and numerous ML algorithms that allow entities and people to be identified besides detecting heat through barriers and thus increase the operational effectiveness during response operations. Indeed, the social implication as noticed with detective UAVs is highly useful in that it provides support services in disaster, bringing relief directly to the affected groups and guaranteeing the security of the rescue squads. Therefore, these UAVs enhance crisis consequence management, reducing death rates, the number of casualties and the extent of property damage. They do also help in safety and security to the public through assisting the police in surveillance and the fight against crime. Analyzing UAV's physical and virtual units, the challenges describe the UAV's use cases in different kinds of crises, such as natural ones, industrial failures, and criminal events. It also deals with issues such as restrictive policies, data security, and the requirement of professional personnel. From case studies and more personal accounts, detective UAVs' potential of crisis management is revolutionary: loss of life is avoided, damage to property is limited, and order is maintained. If further developed and properly integrated into the emergency management systems, UAVs will be the part of the equipment of the future for enhancing the efficiency of response to critical situations.

articleTitle: Natural Language Processing (NLP) based Phonetic Insights for Improving Voice Recognition and Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Voice analysis in Natural Language Processing (NLP) involves the processing of spoken language to develop applications such as speech recognition, synthesis, and speaker identification. This survey explores the phonetic intricacies of Tamil and other Dravidian languages, examining their impact on NLP. The extensive phonetic inventory of the Tamil Language is characterized by its complex vowel system, retroflex consonants, and the distinction between aspirated and unaspirated stops, which presents unique challenges and opportunities for computational linguistics. Phonetics helps to process the human language both accurately and naturally and it works as a bridge between the spoken and written communication forms. This paper emphasizes the necessity of developing specialized phonetic modeling techniques and robust algorithms. Additionally, it highlights the importance of creating comprehensive phonetic datasets and leveraging advancements in machine learning and deep learning to improve NLP tasks such as speech recognition and synthesis. A brief comparison on algorithms and applications associated with voice-assisted technologies. By advocating for interdisciplinary collaboration among linguists, computer scientists, and language technologists, this survey aims to inspire further research and innovation in processing Tamil and other Dravidian languages, ultimately contributing to more inclusive and efficient NLP systems for these linguistically rich languages.

articleTitle: SPEAR: Design and Implementation of an Advanced Virtual Assistant
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research presents the development and evaluation of SPEAR, an advanced voice-activated personal desktop assistant designed to address challenges in existing virtual assistant technology, such as limited language support, low recognition accuracy, and inadequate task automation. Despite recent advancements in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning, implementation in current systems remains subpar. SPEAR achieves an 88% overall command execution success rate, with a speech recognition accuracy of 92% and an average response time of 1.8 seconds, demonstrating efficiency in real-time interactions. Developed using Python and machine learning libraries, SPEAR supports 15 voice commands across multiple platforms, excelling in note creation (95% success), web searching (94%), and information retrieval (92%). Its natural language understanding score of 0.86 and context retention rate of 75% highlight its conversational capabilities. While the assistant performs well in messaging functionality (85% success) and currently supports three languages, expanding its multilingual capabilities is essential for broader user engagement. Metrics indicate a satisfaction score of 8.2/10 and an average of 12 daily interactions per user, showcasing its practical utility. Additionally, the system's text-to-speech quality (8.5/10) and error recovery rate (82 %) affirm its robustness. These findings contribute valuable insights for future research, focusing on enhancing multilingual support, broadening task categories, and improving context retention, ultimately positioning SPEAR to rival established industry leaders by offering a comprehensive suite of services.

articleTitle: DP-CDUN-GTO: An Enhanced Network Approach with Giant Trevally Optimizer for Accurate Air Quality Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Air pollution is a serious problem in smart cities that damages the environment and people's health. Predicting air pollution can provide pertinent parties the knowledge they need to act appropriately. Notwithstanding the importance of this field, there are problems with the current research, including low accuracy and inaccurate real-time updates. In order to optimize performance, this study offers a novel hybrid model called DP-CDUN-GTO, which is based on the Giant Trevally Optimizer and a Dynamic Path-Controllable Deep Unfolding Network(DP-CDUN). The suggested model uses a DP-CDUN layer to extract a feature set from the training dataset and uses the same network to accomplish sequencing learning. Furthermore, the model builds a novel motivating model by applying a Curiosity-based Motivation method, which improves the reconstruction of the deep unfolding network. The DP-CDUN weights are optimized by the Giant Trevally Optimizer in order to reduce prediction error. For comparison, the authors use an online dataset from Salt Lake City, USA's Air Pollution Monitoring, which includes five air quality indicators: SO2, CO, O3, NO2. The suggested attains R2-Score = 0.1124, Mean Absolute Percentage Error = 0.0784, and Mean Absolute Error = 0.0052.

articleTitle: Detecting Fake News on Social Networks: A Naive Bayes Approach to Enhance Information Trustworthiness
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In modern life, the influence of social network takes the first place. The news from a social network may be wrong, in the manner it's the necessary to check the trustworthiness of a news is very important. This article proceeds a novel approach to find a fake news on social media by implementing the machine learning algorithm. The classification of real or fake news using Naïve Bayes classifier and TF-IDF, NLP were used for tokenization, count vectorizer, and so on. Two different datasets (fake & real) were used here. Various types of machine learning algorithms such as logistic regression, SVM, Decision tree and random forest are implemented in the same datasets. While comparing the results Naïve Bayes give 95% of accuracy for the dataset. Various preprocessing techniques were employed here to achieve the results. It is efficient solution to find or classify, a news is real or fake on social media.

articleTitle: A Survey Based on Behavior Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Using Machine Learning Process
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Cybersecurity is a very crucial field that comprises various technologies, processes as well as practices and all are particularly aimed at safeguarding digital assets from various threats. As the number of inter-connected devices has been increased nowadays, cybersecurity has become more complex. It is very essential to note that as more businesses and services move online, there are more opportunities for cyberattacks and this also led to serious consequences such as financial loss and disruptions to services. The two key points about the changing landscape of cybersecurity threats have been highlighted in the study: Nation-State-Affiliated Adversaries are attackers that are supported or directly controlled by a government. Criminal Adversaries are attackers motivated by financial gain. Although the infrastructure for technology is associated with artificial intelligence in cybersecurity, and it is additionally known that these systems support a broad range of applications that helps to improve cyber defences more broadly. In recent times, advanced technologies like artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation have been utilized and these technologies make cybersecurity more complex. AI and ML have been utilized to a certain extent in order to make cybersecurity systems better at detecting and responding to threats as well. Furthermore, the proposed method in the study has been especially aimed to manage security incidents quickly by using AI and ML and in a very effective manner. The development of AI systems capable of detecting both simple and complex cyber threats with a high level of accuracy and speed have been explored thoroughly in the survey. Cybersecurity can be improved by using two key concepts: User Behaviour Analytics (UBA) and ICS Security Ontology.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Learning Based Land Cover Semantic Segmentation of Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Land Cover Semantic Segmentation plays a pivotal role in the field of remote sensing and geographical monitoring. By automated partitioning of image into different land cover classes, it can provide valuable insights into the diverse features on the Earth's surface which can be useful for a multitude of tasks including urban planning and infrastructure manage-ment, agricultural planning, crop monitoring, water resource utilization, forest, and woodland management, etc. Supervised deep learning techniques have seen enormous success in this field. However, their success can be attributed mostly to the availability of large-scale labeled datasets belonging to specific regions. However, this poses difficulties in the application of these techniques in the areas where labeled datasets are not readily available. This study uses self-supervised techniques to apply available supervised architectures on areas with unavailable data. Self-supervised training techniques - SimCLR and SimSiam have been the focus of this study. For fine-tuning and segmentation benchmark analysis, the popular architectures UNet, UNet++ and DeepLabV3have been studied. Ablation studies have been performend by applying self-supervision techniques on different quantities of labeled and unlabeled data. This study also explores the feasibility of the relatively newer LandCoverNet dataset released for the Asia region. This paper reveals how comparable results can be achieved with only a fraction of the labeled dataset using self-supervision techniques.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Shopping Experience Through Smart Trolleys with Integrated Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study presents an innovative smart shopping trolley system designed to enhance the retail shopping experience by integrating advanced deep learning techniques and sensor technology. The system begins with a secure membership card login process, enabling personalized customer interaction. Upon entry into the trolley system, products can be easily added and identified through a camera utilizing EfficientN et, a deep learning model trained on the store's inventory. The system incorporates an infrared motion sensor and a weight sensor to ensure accuracy in product registration, enhancing reliability and preventing errors. As the shopping process unfolds, a Transformer-based recommendation system analyzes real-time choices and shopping history to provide tailored product suggestions displayed on the trolley's LCD screen. To enhance security, an Autoencoder neural network monitors for anomalies in product identification and removal, alerting store personnel in case of discrepancies. Upon completing the shopping process, a QR code is generated for payment, streamlining the checkout experience. This smart shopping trolley system optimizes the shopping process, leveraging real-time data to improve efficiency, security, and overall customer satisfaction in the retail environment. The system aims to revolutionize traditional shopping methods by applying deep learning and IoT technologies and create a seamless, engaging consumer experience.

articleTitle: Advanced Process Control in Manufacturing Using IoT Devices and Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Optimization of industrial activities is significantly helped by Advanced Process Control (APC), which increases efficiency, decreases costs, and improves product quality. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and the Internet of Things (IoT) have greatly improved APC in manufacturing. It examines how APC systems may include ANNs and IoT devices in industrial processes. By connecting to a wide range of sensors placed strategically throughout a production facility, IoT devices may gather data in real time, allowing for managing and monitoring crucial parameters. To APC systems, ANNs are invaluable for predictive modeling and control due to their adaptability to changing process conditions and capacity to represent complicated nonlinear interactions. Manufacturers may gain better control over their operations, improving productivity and product quality, by using data from the IoT to train and update ANN models. Recent advances in APC using IoT devices and ANNs are reviewed in this study. Their applications in various industrial industries are discussed, and case examples are shown to demonstrate their usefulness. Further improvements in APC for manufacturing using IoT devices and ANNs may be guided by highlighting the field's problems and future research goals. Challenges with data security, integration challenges, and reliability impact the accuracy of predictive modeling, scalability, and performance of IoT systems.

articleTitle: Temperature Variation Modelling in Mushroom Growing Hall with IAN-Bidirectional GRU Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Modern developments in computing and electronics have made intelligent systems suitable for use in the mechanization of agricultural processes. This proposed used multilayered perceptron and radial basis function networks to forecast the temperature shifts in the mushroom cultivation chamber based on independent variables including water temperature, ambient temperature, water tap, fresh air and circulation air dampers, and water tap. Preprocessing, feature extraction, and training the model are the three phases that comprise this proposed method. Reflectance calibration, normalization, and spectral smoothing are the steps involved in data preprocessing. Feature extraction made quick work of extracting information from mushroom photos by employing the SIFT algorithm. The proposed model was trained using an IAN-Bidirectional GRU. When compared to more conventional approaches, the proposed methodology is superior. The method's application resulted in a 93.75% improvement in accuracy.

articleTitle: PIM-FFL: Evaluating Participation Index Metrics for Fairness Enhancement in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a technique that allows multiple devices to train a machine learning model without sharing their raw data, this preserves user privacy. However, traditional FL often suffers from problems like nodes failing to participate in training due to resource limitations. This negatively impacts the model's performance and fairness, making it harder for all devices to benefit equally. Ensuring fairness in FL is challenging due to the significant differences in clients' data quality, data size, and contribution levels. A notable issue arises when prime contributing clients do not receive fair rewards while underperforming still benefits. This disparity leads to an inequity causing complexity among contributors. As a result, clients may feel unappreciated, leading to a decrease in their interest in participating which ultimately compromises the complete reliability and effectiveness of the system. To address these challenges, a client clustering method is presented based on their participation index, which ensures that prime participants receive better model updates rather than underperformers which makes the system more reliable. Additionally, the Double Deep Q-Networks (DDQN) method is employed, as it determines the best actions through learning from past experiences and updating Q-values, which dynamically update participation count and reduce the model biases. Our experiments show that this clustering method substantially enhances fairness in Federated Learning, fostering a more efficient and cooperative learning environment that outperforms traditional methods like FedAvg and FedProx.

articleTitle: Enhanced Breast Cancer Relapse Prediction using Ensemble Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Breast cancer remains a significant health concern for women, and accurate prediction of recurrence is vital for effective treatment and improved outcomes. This research investigates the application of advanced ensemble learning techniques to enhance the reliability of breast cancer recurrence predictions. By combining Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) with traditional machine learning methods, the proposed approach demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1-scores, and areas under the curve (AVCs). The study utilizes two breast cancer relapse datasets, UMCIO and WPBC, to evaluate the performance of the ensemble learning models. The results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately predicting breast cancer recurrence. This research contributes to the advancement of breast cancer diagnosis and treatment by providing a valuable tool for clinicians to assess the risk of recurrence and tailor treatment plans accordingly.

articleTitle: Designing an Enhanced MobileNet Integrated Architecture with Optimization for Accurate Detection of ASD using Extracted Facial Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In the research, a new method is proposed to ensure the robust detection and extraction of facial features relevant for differentiating individuals with autism spectrum disorder. A multilevel cascaded Convolutional Neural Network (MCNN) architecture is designed for high-precision face localization in images, which can later provide a basis for subsequent fine-grained feature extraction from faces. Further, at the very initial stage of data preprocessing a very effective contrast adjustment (CA) technique is introduced that would efficiently enhance image quality and uniformity due to different lighting conditions. This improves, much better, the reliability of the facial features extracted and allows more accurate identification of discriminative emotional expression features for ASD. First, state-of-the-art high-precision facial landmark detection (FLD) techniques pinpoint key facial structures, thus helping extract relevant features for ASD classification. To further optimize feature selection, a Sand Cat Swarm Optimization (SCSO) method is introduced that identifies and maximizes subsets of facial features with maximal differences between ASD and non-ASD classes to boost classification accuracy. Finally, a customized hybrid Dense-MobileNet (DMN) architecture is provided that classifies ASD and non-ASD cases efficiently and accurately using the extracted facial features. This architecture synergistically puts together the advantages of dense layer to the MobileNet in order to guarantee high performance by achieving an accuracy of 99.22% in the identification of ASD-related features from the face.

articleTitle: Integrating Quantum Principles with Classical Transfer Learning Approaches for Pneumonia Detection from Chest Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Pneumonia is a severe and deadly lung disease, that kills millions of people around the world annually. If detected early, these death cases can be avoided by appropriate medical care. Yet, the regions with poor access to healthcare might find it difficult for early detection. The application with a pre-programmed chest X-ray pneumonia detection method is proper which can easily meet these issues and give reliable, accurate diagnosis. Automated pneumonia detection using chest X-rays is an active field of study. Taking together, the results collected from the experiments in this study underscore the effective combination of traditional machine learning(ML) with quantum machine learning(QML) for chest X-ray pneumonia diagnosis. Initially, few transfer learning approaches like ResNet-18, AlexNet, Inception-v3 and VGG-16 were taken to create the classical binary image classification models. Secondly, the aggregated classification model architecture was implemented based on the union of classical and quantum networks engineered utilizing the same blueprint based entirely on traditional transfer learning techniques. Compared to classical models of similar designs, the hybrid models trained and tested in this experiment display greater classification proficiency. The AlexNet model, when incorporated with the hybrid transfer learning classifier achieved an effective classification accuracy of 97.79 %, yielding a total improvement of 2.37 % over the models based solely on the classical approach of similar architecture. Optimal results were achieved by this hybrid model where AUC is 0.99 and other performance metrics like F1-score, recall and precision generated a value of 0.97.

articleTitle: Enhancing User Experience and Mitigating BIAS in Electronic Device Recommendations on e-Commerce Platforms: Leveraging NLP and GPT Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Electronic devicerecommendations on e-commerce sites enhance the user experience by assisting users in finding products that suit their requirements, interests, and preferences. By providing them with pertinent options, it helps users who are looking for specific gadgets save time and effort. Electronic devices commonly saw shorter product lifecycles due to the regular introduction of updated and new models. Users may feel under pressure to update to newer versions in order to access the newest features or upgrades, which could cause obsolescence problems. Previously NLP techniques are utilized for recommending electronic gadgets. Biased recommendations may result from NLP models inheriting biases found in the training set of data. As a result, there may be unfair or discriminatory consequences, such as more product recommendations for particular demographic groups or the reinforcement of preexistingpreconceptions. GPT may be used to construct chatbots or AIs that engage with customers using natural language. These assistance systems driven by AI are able to help customers make purchases, answer their questions, and make personalized product suggestions. Companies can improve the customer experience by responding quickly and giving useful information. One can use GPT to simplify customer service tasks like answering common questions and fixing problems right away. This can help companies help customers around the clock, speed up reaction times, and give human support workers less work to do. Support systems driven by GPT can also learn from exchanges with customers over time, making them better at what they do. High-quality material may be produced by GPT for use in blog entries, social media postings, marketingand copy, including product descriptions. One can use this material to get people interested in and buying from your e-commerce sites, show off product attributes and advantages, and attract new customers. We can also make GPT-generated content search engine friendly, which will increase its exposure and natural reach.

articleTitle: Enhancing House Price Forecasting with State-Action-Reward-State-Action Algorithm and Deep Q-Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The research aims to optimise housing pricing strategies using reinforcement learning algorithms, specifically SARSA and Deep Q-Network (DQN). The study employs the Kaggle House Prices dataset and focuses on variables such as year built, neighbourhood, and overall quality to enhance real estate price decisions. The SARSA algorithm was designed to dynamically change asking prices by providing incentives based on the difference between asking and actual selling prices, as well as a penalty for time on the market. This model fared well, with an average sale duration of 34.52 days and a total reward of around $1,640,667.27. The DQN algorithm used deep learning to find subtle patterns in the data in order to make better decisions. The DQN model outperformed SARSA, with an average total payout of $1,780,345.82 and a shorter average sale time of 31.75 days. The findings demonstrate how RL, specifically DQN, can be utilised to improve pricing strategies and provide valuable information about the real estate market. This study demonstrates the utility of sophisticated reinforcement learning approaches in complicated decision-making and identifies areas for further research into larger datasets and more complex models for better property price optimisation.

articleTitle: SoulNourish: A Comprehensive Machine learning Based Recommendation Yoga Prediction System Based on Health and Lifestyle Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The modern sedentary lifestyle has escalated health risks, underscoring the importance of tailored health solutions like yoga. This paper pioneers a method to determine yoga'srelevance for individuals by analyzing their lifestyle data. Using machine learning algorithms like Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, SVMs, and Neural Networks and KMeans with Convo-lution Neural Networks. We process data on activity, diet, stress, and sleep to evaluate yoga's potential benefits. We implementthe algorithms for recommending the customized yoga routines. Our experimental results show that Decision Trees give goodaccuracy in identifying candidates for yoga, offering a novel perspective for personalized health interventions and underscoring machine learning's role in enhancing public health.

articleTitle: Complete Plant Care Monitoring Using Internet of Things (IoT)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Due to the rapid spread and growth, there has been a notable surge in the need for nourishment in recent years. Currently, the worldwide agricultural production is inadequate to satisfy the nutritional needs of every people suffering from famine. The internet of things offers a wide range of potential for farmers to enhance their agricultural production, leading to a revolution in the industry. Agriculture depends on three essential factors for optimal functioning: soil nutrients, namely nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium; pH level; soil moisture content; and ambient temperature and relative humidity. Sensors installed in the field are used to measure soil moisture levels, NPK values, pH, temperature, and humidity. The ESP8266 wireless communication module only collects sensor data. This module enables the wireless connection, allowing the collected data to be transferred to the cloud for storage. The suggested system not only controls the water supply to the farm but also offers real-time monitoring capabilities based on agricultural parameters. By using a cloud-based web server, the system may provide the farm owner with the ability to monitor sensor values in real-time and operate them remotely.

articleTitle: Advancing Safety in Cooperative Vehicle Platooning Through IoT Connectivity and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Future transportation systems might benefit greatly from cooperative vehicle platooning, in which vehicles move near one another to decrease air resistance and increase fuel efficiency. However, ensuring everyone in these platoons stays safe is their primary priority. Combining the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and the connection offered by the Internet of Things (IoT), this paper proposes a method to improve the security of cooperative vehicle platooning. Firstly, the interoperability provided by the IoT makes it possible for vehicles to transmit important data such as location, speed, and sensor readings in real time. This makes it easier for platoon members to work together and initiates preventative safety actions. The second use of CNNs is in advanced vision tasks, which include lane tracking, object identification, and anomaly detection. CNNs can alert platoon drivers and the autonomous driving system to possible dangers and course deviations by evaluating data from various onboard sensors, including lidar and cameras. A hierarchical safety design that combines conventional safety features is adaptive cruise control and emergency braking systems with connected IoT devices and perception based on CNNs. Simulated outcomes show that the proposed method significantly improves responsiveness to dangerous situations and decreases accident rates within cooperative vehicle platoons to increase safety. Challenges include providing dependable communication, managing the complexity of sensor data, attaining real-time processing, and mitigating safety issues in dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence-Based Alzheimer's Disease Classification Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) presents substantial challenges in early diagnosis and classification, seeking innovative methods. This review study addresses various classification models developed for AD classification utilizing Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) data and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This study reviews the benefits and drawbacks of several AI-driven strategies, from advanced deep learning architectures to conventional machine learning techniques, through a thorough analysis. These models provide promising pathways for accurate AD diagnosis by utilizing MRI data, allowing for early intervention and individualized treatment plans. Nonetheless, issues including the lack of data, the interpretability of algorithms, and validation in clinical contexts continue to exist. In order to fully utilize AI's potential to enhance patient care and AD classification, this review emphasizes the significance of interdisciplinary collaboration and strong validation procedures.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Model for Human Detection-Enhanced YOLO Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Video surveillance systems employing closed-circuit television (CCTV) are crucial for public safety. Accurately detecting humans within video frames is a core component of this technology. This knowledge is crucial for numerous uses, including detecting possible dangers, observing crowd dynamics, and examining patterns of human behavior. This research introduces a new method called YOLOv8, designed to enhance human detection capabilities within CCTV footage. The proposed algorithm, YOLOv8, is built upon the popular object recognition framework, YOLO, but with significant enhancements to improve its accuracy and efficiency in detecting humans. YOLOv8 utilizes deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and advanced object recognition techniques to achieve high accuracy in human detection, even in challenging environments such as low light conditions, occlusions, and varying scales of human poses. To assess the effectiveness of YOLOv8, various tests were performed using standard datasets and real-world CCTV surveillance footage. The results demonstrate that YOLOv8 outperforms existing human detection algorithms regarding accuracy, robustness, and real-time processing capability. YOLOv8 achieved an average precision of over 95% in human detection, making it highly suitable for everyday CCTV surveillance. The proposed YOLOv8 algorithm has the potential to significantly improve human detection in security camera footage and enhance public safety. This research contributes to advancing human detection technology and can benefit various domains, including law enforcement, public safety, and video analytics.

articleTitle: Smart Agricultural System Using Machine Learning to Predict Rainfall and Conserve Water for Irrigation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The primary objective of this research is to conserve water through smart agriculture, by employing the Random Forest algorithm to predict rainfall. By avoiding unnecessary irrigation on rainy days, this system conserves water. The proposed method works on both hardware and software. The hardware comprises two boards, one of which is the ESP8266 for wireless connectivity to the internet, while the other utilizes an Arduino microcontroller with additional sensors to track soil moisture, temperature, and humidity of the farming land. The software is a website developed using the Random Forest algorithm for rain prediction. The project integrates hardware and software by providing the sensor outputs through the website to the machine learning model for rain prediction. If rain is predicted, land water utilized for farming is conserved. With an accuracy of 88.5%, Random Forest predicts rain on that day, whereas the other models give an accuracy of 83%. The Random Forest algorithm also outperforms logistic regression used for rain prediction, resulting in more accurate predictions.

articleTitle: Smart Flood Detection and Communication in Hazardous Zones via MANET-Based IoT and Parallely Distributed Slimmable Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Disasters can be mitigated by an early warning signal and proper communication within the hazardous environment using the MANET technology. However, the exact prediction of disaster situation is needed for the timely disaster management. Hence in addition to MANET technology, deep learning algorithms and Inter of Things (IoT) can also be integrated into disaster detection and communication systems. The presented research developed a novel parallely distributed slimmable neural network with orchard algorithm for the accurate flood disaster prediction. The model processed the dataset containing various measurements such as temperature, humidity, precipitation, air, soil moisture and rainfall level that are collected by the IoT sensor deployed in the various location of the hazardous environment. The gathered data are initially pre-processed using the correlation coefficient min-max normalization approach. Further, the relevant characteristics of the flood disaster from the data are extracted through spike driven transformer process. These refined and dimensionality reduced data are then entered into the proposed framework for the disaster prediction. Here the integrated orchard algorithm increased the disaster monitoring accuracy on the basis of better optimized parameters. The model resulted 95% accuracy, 93% precision, 94% recall and 96% f-score. Therefore, the presented method is an effective prediction mechanism for the disaster management in IoT MANET.

articleTitle: Boosting Fiber Layup Defect Classification: A Comprehensive Analysis of Explainable AI Techniques for Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research study presents a machine learning model capable of accurately identifying and classifying various manufacturing defects. The model demonstrates exceptional performance in recognizing defects such as alignment issues, fluid leaks, welding defects, electrical system failures, and imperfections. The model achieves high precision and recall values, ranging from 81.68% to 93.33% and 87.50% to 89.38%, respectively, indicating its ability to correctly identify and capture positive examples of each defect type. The Fl-scores, ranging from 85.01 % to 90.32%, further validate the model's balanced performance. The study also provides support percentage values to standardize the data and illustrate the relative representation of each fault type. The consistent accuracy values across all classes, including macro, weighted, and micro averages, highlight the model's reliability and generalizability. The findings of this research demonstrate the potential of machine learning to improve manufacturing quality control processes, leading to enhanced product quality and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Secured Digital and QR Code Payments: A Comparative Analysis of Payment Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The internet's explosive expansion has paved the way for a wide range of smartphone applications that use QR codes and digital wallets to facilitate online payments. Security is a major concern for web-based applications since they are being delivered over the Internet at a rapid pace. Due to unlawful access to many accounts, which causes problems with end-to-end security, the security of these applications has grown to be a top concern for both customers and business owners. This work has addressed the several models that are accessible for security applications, also provided a comparative analysis of all the models, taking into account their security privacy, adaptability, accuracy reliability, vulnerabilities and suitability for digital wallets and online payment systems through QR codes.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition Through Speech Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The research aims to develop a voice emotion identification system that utilises empirical feature optimisation techniques and all accessible acoustic data. The methodology used in this work involves gathering data from several emotive speech datasets and utilising audio visualisation techniques to interpret the data. Next, apply augmentation methods to the dataset, such as pitch shifting, temporal stretching, and noise injection. Key audio properties such as Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, Zero Crossing Rate, RMS value, and MelSpectrogram are involved in speech emotion identification. Pitch, tone, and energy shifts corresponding to various emotions are all captured in exquisite detail. A mixture of feature selection and applied deep learning model hyperparameter tuning-specifically, Convolutional Neural Networks-is used to achieve optimisation. The model's accuracy in identifying emotions from speech is evaluated using pre-processed training data and unseen testing data. In addition to improving customer service and mental health monitoring, the results of this project will help to make human-computer interaction more responsive and intuitive. The innovation in the research is ensured by combining the use of Convolutional Neural Networks as the hyperparameter tuning tool for deep learning models with an optimisation process feature filter. It will be ensured by this study that the model learns to recognise emotions from speech data in an efficient manner. The proposed methodology exhibits higher accuracy in identifying emotions from speech when compared to the latest related study. Assessing the model's performance against pre-processed training and unseen testing data, the results are extremely noteworthy.

articleTitle: Proposed IoT-Based Smart Garbage Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Considering the rapid growth of the urban population and rapid industrialization, the issue of efficient waste disposal has become very important. In response, authors here propose an idea in the form of an IOT -based waste management system designed to address the challenges at hand autonomously. The paper aims to propose solution for garbage management system. The system leverages IoT technology with sensor-based circuits and machine automation and models to streamline waste management processes. Traditional trash cans require manual operation, you need to press the lever to manually open the lid, monitor the trash can capacity, and adjust the garbage distance to prevent the trash can from overflowing. In contrast, this intelligent waste management model will work autonomously. The sensor will detect the presence of a person and automatically will open and close the lid. Additionally, location tracking will alert the authorities when waste processing capacity approaches its limits, facilitating timely disposal of waste and will prevent overflow. Additionally, there will be features such as voice detection to edit specific commands for executable access. By eliminating manual intervention and implementing intelligent monitoring capabilities, this system will provide a smarter and more efficient approach to waste treatment, ultimately leading to cleaner and more sustainable urban environments.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach to Optimal Power Allocation in MIMO-NOMA: Integrating DGNN and Tyrannosaurus Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: One of the primary technologies necessary for the upcoming sixth generation of communication networks (6G) is massive multi-input multi-output, or MIMO. However, enormous MIMO presents a challenge in reducing energy use and the sum rate demand due to the power use of the several radio frequencies (RF) links in 6G technology. Therefore, this research presented a novel Deformable Graph Neural Network (DGNN) with Tyrannosaurus optimization for the optimal power distribution that maximized the sum rate and energy efficiency of the MIMO NOMA system. The adaptive mechanism of DGNN enables more accurate and efficient power allocation decisions. The integrated Tyrannosaurus optimization ensures the model converging on optimal power allocation strategies that maximize both sum rate and energy efficiency. The efficiency of the recommended model is compared in regarding sum rate and Energy Efficiency (EE) with the some of the recent approaches. The proposed method gained the greater sum rate and EE outperforming all other compared models.

articleTitle: Improving Grid Stability and Power Quality in Advanced Technologies-Based Bidirectional EV Charging Stations: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Integrating renewable energy into electric vehicle (EV) charging stations is crucial to improving sustainability, reducing carbon emissions and improving energy management. In addition to these benefits, addressing power quality concerns is essential for the infrastructure supporting EV charging to operate reliably. The issues about the quality of energy associated with bidirectional EV charging systems, particularly in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) operations using advanced control methods and adaptive filtering to help address power quality issues by dynamically adjusting charging parameters and enhancing system stability. With EV sales rising quickly, significant obstacles such as voltage fluctuations, harmonic distortions, and grid instability have emerged, especially during peak charging periods. These issues with power quality do not just compromise grid reliability but also impact the infrastructure for EV charging's effectiveness and lifespan. The paper highlights important techniques for enhancing power quality, emphasizing advanced control schemes, including predictive and adaptive control, and innovative converter technologies. The objective of these methods is to maximize power flow, reduce energy losses, and strengthen grid stability. The focus will be on advanced power electronics, smart grid integration, and real-time monitoring systems to address the current challenges while supporting the widespread adoption of renewable energy sources in EV charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Securing Personal Identity in Facial Recognition: The Shift to Machine Unlearning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Machine Unlearning, which enables the successful removal of specific data from Machine Learning models, is a crucial approach for ensuring data privacy and compliance. Most existing unlearning techniques have been evaluated on conventional benchmark datasets, which often fail to replicate the complexity of real-world settings, especially when dealing with sensitive data such as private personal information. The majority of Machine Learning research has been conducted on traditional datasets, which may not fully capture the challenges encountered in real-world scenarios, particularly concerning sensitive and private data. To address this gap, the proposed method utilizes two datasets, MUFAC and MUCAC, specifically designed to evaluate the effectiveness of Machine Unlearning in facial recognition contexts. Following the training of the model using facial data, a Machine Learning framework is developed.

articleTitle: Seamless Service Evolution: Enhancing Customer Satisfaction Using AWS-Driven AI Chatbots for Restaurant Ordering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In the current restaurant business environment, factors have emerged in the manner in which consumers are attended to and the ways orders are placed. As good as these traditional systems may be, they do not offer the optimum flexibility and consumer convergence that today's client demands for fast and convenient services. Recent approaches using only basic form of automation and rule-based chatbots do offer some enhancements but lack adequate capabilities to deal with huge volumes of orders, custom recommendations and scalability according to demand. Further, the existing systems have problems with scalability, versatility to different customers' trends and needs, and real-time interactions. To overcome these challenges our work, will utilize modern advances in artificial intelligence and cloud technology. The proposed system uses Amazon Lex for NLU, A WS Lambda for processing multiple booking requests simultaneously without any intervention from the users and Amazon Polly for making interaction more interactive with personalized audio. In addition, Amazon Rekognition and A WS S3 for images will be used for analysis of images and proper storage of data respectively, enhancing the customer satisfaction by recommending products based on a past order. All these technologies integrated with A WS ecosystem in our solution will provide convenience, efficiency and passion to restaurant business proprietors to fulfill the increasing demands of modern customer. The system also supports linkage with some commonly used applications such as WhatsApp, guaranteeing that the customers receive timely updates. Thus, this solution is designed to create an improved status of restaurant ordering and eliminate the problematic experiences placed in current schemes.

articleTitle: An Innovative Method for Brain Stroke Prediction based on Parallel RELM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Strokes occur when blood supply to the brain is suddenly cut off or severely impaired. Stroke victims may experience cell death as a result of oxygen and food shortages. The effectiveness of various predictive data mining algorithms in illness prediction has been the subject of numerous studies. The three stages that make up this suggested method are feature selection, model training, and preprocessing. Missing value management, numeric value conversion, imbalanced dataset handling, and data scaling are all components of data preparation. The chi-square and RFE methods are utilized in feature selection. The former assesses feature correlation, while the latter recursively seeks for ever-smaller feature sets to choose features. The whole time the model was being trained, a Parallel RELM was used. This new method outperforms both ELM and RELM, achieving an average accuracy of 95.84%.

articleTitle: Extractive Multi-Document Summarization Using Transformer-Based Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The management and extraction of pertinent information from sizable text collections depends critically on multi-document summarization. Using Transformer-based neural networks, this research describes a technical method for extractive multi-document summarization. To capture the important information across many publications, we suggest a unique architecture that makes use of self-attention processes and contextualized word representations. To improve the summary generation process, the model is trained using a combination of supervised learning and reinforcement learning methods. We run thorough tests on benchmark datasets and evaluate our method against current state-of-the-art techniques. The outcomes show how well our suggested model performs in producing informative and cogent summaries from a variety of documents.

articleTitle: MangoLeafNet: Transforming Mango Leaf Disease Management with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Effective mango leaf disease detection is critical for optimizing crop health and yield, utilizing advanced models for accurate diagnosis. To discover important mango leaf diseases, this study uses two different datasets to investigate MangoLeafNet, an advanced deep-learning model based on EfficientN etB0. Four images are included in each dataset: healthy leaves, powdery mildew, Anthracnose, and sooty mold (also known as sooty mold). MangoLeafNet was chosen for its effective compound scaling methodology and evaluated for its classification performance. Metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl score were used to assess the Model's performance. In order to evaluate MangoLeafNet's comparative efficacy, it was compared with VGG16, MobileNetV1, and AlexNet, among other models. Because of its sophisticated feature extraction capabilities, the Model can classify data precisely, which makes it an invaluable tool for controlling diseases in the mango agricultural sector.

articleTitle: Communication Protocols for Electric Vehicles: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EV s) Significantly contribute to sustainable development goals (SDGs) by mitigating emissions, enhancing air quality, fostering renewable energy use, generating green employment, and facilitating access to sustainable transportation. In electric vehicles (EV s), multiple components require communication protocols to enable synchronization of subsystems such as battery management and charging infrastructure and ensure optimal efficiency and interoperability. There is a wide adoption of Electric vehicles (EV s) worldwide to create a sustainable environment. Based upon the above aspects, this article presents a thorough literature review of the communication protocols for EV s, where the key technical components of the EV ecosystem are summarized in detail. Further, this study presented an overview of communication protocols for EV s, covering front- end and back-end protocols. The significance of protocols in EV charging is discussed, including aspects like interoperability, communication and data exchange, plug- and-charge capability, monitoring, and smart charging. The findings of the study conclude that this communication protocol is used to integrate electric vehicles (EVs) into transportation networks. Front-end and back-end protocols govern the communication between electric vehicles (EVs) and charging stations, as well as between the infrastructure and third-party operators. Protocols like ISO 15118, OCPP, IEC 61850, and others are used for different purposes. Protocols are based on their openness, compatibility, maturity, and market adoption to determine their adequacy for adoption in the EV business. The review's novelty comes from its comprehensive analysis of communication protocols for electric vehicles (EV s), which encompasses both detailed elements and performing outcomes.

articleTitle: An Approach for Classification of Brain Tumor using Fully Connected Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) structures have played a vital part in various medical sectors due to their efficiency. It is likely becoming the most significant early identification approach for malignant tumor masses as digital systems and CNN technology advance. The research focuses on the early diagnosis and detection of tumors through deep learning with convolutional neural networks and convolution neural network approaches. It focuses on the processing, fragmentation, and categorization of various brain tumor pictures into malignant or benign tumors. The evaluation is done by incorporating several layers of CNN using a 70:30 and 80:20 splitting ratio. Conventional deep learning classifiers perform the comparative analysis of the routine of projected CNN prototypical, and the planned CNN model perceived accuracy of 97.92% using VGG16 and 98.20% using VGG19 deep learning frameworks. Furthermore, it is observed from experimental findings that the performance of various pre-trained models of VGG19 performs better than that of other models.

articleTitle: Review of Acoustic Features and Computational Models in Lung Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Respiratory diseases are increasingly prevalent, necessitating efficient diagnostic methods for healthcare providers to manage patient care effectively. This review addresses the growing need for non-invasive, cost-effective diagnostic techniques focused on acoustic properties of lung sounds. The primary objective is to explore contemporary methodologies and models used in the acoustic analysis of lung sounds for disease identification and characterization. The review examines and contrasts current signal processing techniques and machine learning algorithms applied to lung sound analysis, highlighting their strengths and limitations. By evaluating these methods, the review aims to identify promising applications for clinical settings and provide insights into how these technologies can be optimized. Additionally, the review offers recommendations for future research and practical applications of lung sound analysis to enhance differential diagnosis and prognosis of respiratory disorders. This work aims to contribute to the development of advanced, accessible diagnostic tools that can improve patient outcomes and streamline respiratory disease management.

articleTitle: Improving Tomato Disease Diagnosis Through ResNet50: An Innovative Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Tomato crops are vulnerable to numerous diseases that can severely affect both yield and quality. Early and precise identification of these diseases is indispensable for implementing active management and intervention measures. This research introduces an advanced approach to tomato disease detection by employing the ResNet50 architecture, pretrained on the ImageNet dataset. Through transfer learning, the ResNet50 model leverages its pre-learned features to classify tomato plant images affected by diseases such as Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV), Bacterial Spot, Blossom End Rot, Early Blight, and Late Blight. The ResNet50 model is fine-tuned with custom classification layers tailored to the specific diseases, allowing it to achieve high accuracy in disease detection. Preliminary results indicate that the ResNet50 model significantly outperforms traditional machine learning approaches, demonstrating its efficacy in accurately diagnosing tomato diseases. This study provides an effective solution for improving disease detection in tomatoes and highlights the transformative role of deep learning in advancing agricultural practices, fostering sustainability, and enhancing productivity.

articleTitle: Automated Skin Lesion Analysis and Classification Using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Skin lesions are becoming a major global health concern, and survival rates can be greatly increased by employing dermoscopic pictures for early identification. It is a difficult undertaking to classify these skin lesions from dermoscopic images. The application of deep learning models has significantly improved this classification's accuracy. Because convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are better at extracting features, which improves classification results, they have been shown to be quite useful in this field. In light of this, the article attempts to create deep learning (DL) algorithms using artificial intelligence (AI) to differentiate between skin lesions as benign or malignant in dermoscopic pictures. The study presents OSSAE-BPNN, an automated method for the detection and classification of skin lesions. This method uses a backpropagation neural network (BPNN) for classification and an optimized stacked sparse autoencoder (OSSAE) for feature extraction. To determine the damaged lesion region, the multi-level thresholding segmentation methodology is part of the proposed OSSAE-BPNN method.
