The OSSAE performs the feature extraction, and the BPNN handles the categorization. Furthermore, the SGO (seagull optimization) technique is used to optimize the SSAE model's parameters. Extensive testing were conducted on a standard dataset to show the OSSAE-BPNN method's efficacy. The OSSAE-BPNN methodology fared better than other current methods across a range of evaluation parameters, according to the results.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lung and Colon Cancer Detection Through Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Lung and colon cancers are among the deadliest and most prevalent cancers worldwide, posing significant challenges for diagnosis, treatment, and management. The World Health Organization estimates that lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths, accounting for 18.4% of all cancer fatalities, while colorectal cancer ranks third with 9.2% of cancer deaths. The co-occurrence of lung and colon cancers in patients presents additional clinical complexities that require a multifaceted treatment approach. Traditional diagnostic methods, though effective, often fall short due to high costs, invasiveness, and reliance on human expertise, leading to potential errors. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning particularly Convolutional Neural Networks offer promising alternatives for enhancing cancer detection accuracy and efficiency. This paper proposed a CNN model for detection of lung and colon cancer, detailing the methodology, performance metrics, and potential clinical implications. Proposed CNN model demonstrated high accuracy in classifying cancerous and non-cancerous tissues, significantly outperforming traditional diagnostic methods. These findings underscore the potential of CNNs to revolutionize cancer diagnostics, providing reliable and automated detection that can improve patient outcomes and streamline clinical workflows.

articleTitle: Transforming Checkpoints Experiences: Efficient Check-in and Check-out with Automatic Number Plate Recognition and Mobile App Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Traditional vehicle entry processes at checkpoints often rely on manual confirmation of entry details by security personnel, leading to potential human errors and inefficiencies. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing an automatic check-in/check-out system utilizing Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) technology. When a vehicle approaches the checkpoint, its number plate is captured by CCTV cameras, and ANPR algorithms automatically identify and store the plate number in a database for registration and surveillance purposes. This eliminates the need for manual data entry, enhances security, and reduces personnel effort. The system also offers benefits such as improved parking management and traffic monitoring. Furthermore, in line with the government's initiative to address increasing traffic on urban roads and congestion due to inadequate parking spaces, this paper suggests the establishment of public parking spots equipped with the proposed smart check-in/check-out system. These parking spots, managed through a mobile application, would enable users to easily locate available parking slots, receive tokens for entry, and seamlessly exit after their parking duration. This integrated approach not only addresses traffic congestion but also enhances convenience for urban commuters and mitigates the problem of blocked lanes caused by indiscriminate parking.

articleTitle: Naive Bayes-based Autonomous Illumination System for Urban Green Spaces with Cloud Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Improving urban cities' quality of life is one of the primary functions of urban green spaces. Efficient lighting solutions in these areas enhance safety and ambiance. This research introduces a new method for autonomously controlling the lighting in urban parks with the help of a Naive Bayes classifier and cloud computing. The system uses information gathered from several sensors to adapt the brightness of the lights in response to changes in the surrounding environment and the presence or absence of people. The system can generate accurate choices in real-time using machine learning methods, including the Naive Bayes algorithm. With the help of the cloud, remote monitoring and administration are made easier, which improves efficiency and scalability. The experimental findings prove that the proposed approach is reliable and efficient in enhancing urban green areas' energy efficiency and user enjoyment. Intelligent algorithms combined with cloud computing provide a viable option for smart city lighting control, opening the door to more responsive and environmentally friendly cityscapes.

articleTitle: Securing the Ballot: Ganache's Role in Modernizing E-Voting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Ensuring a fair and secure voting mechanism is crucial for any democratic system., allowing individuals to freely express their opinions. The current reliance on Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs)., which store data locally and centrally., poses significant vulnerabilities. Local storage until election day exposes them to potential hacking and instances of “booth hijacking” have been reported. Moreover., incidents of EVM hacking leading to election manipulation have surfaced in recent years., highlighting the need for a more robust approach to safeguarding voting integrity. Presently., there is a lack of means to verify individual votes and ensure EVM integrity. Blockchain technology., known for its decentralized and distributed nature., offers promising solutions across various industries. Integrating blockchain with e-voting systems presents an opportunity to mitigate current vulnerabilities., providing a nearly hack-proof method for recording transactions. This work proposes a secure electronic voting system built on the Ethereum blockchain and smart contracts. By enabling remote voting., it enhances accessibility while ensuring transparency and trustworthiness in the electoral process.

articleTitle: Crime Detection and Geospatial Alert System using LRCN and Streamlit for Smart City Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Advances in surveillance cameras that have risen with the need for increased security and prevention of real- time crimes have become very common in public. Advanced analyses in machine learning can detect crime from video footage, but problems persist with the current systems. Among the problems include being unable to pinpoint specific criminal activities and a lack of location-based alerts or real-time analysis. Most of the systems that exist cannot perform video feed analysis in real-time video feeds or cannot send alerts to relevant authorities promptly. As a result, such a solution would be of limited effectiveness for public safety. All these new techniques, such as CNN and RNN, have been implemented on crimes regarding action recognition and video surveillance. However, these approaches are often limited in precision, detection speed, and scalability. Specifically, a possible identified limitation is the precise detection of criminal activities within varied environments with a real-time response. Moreover, geocoding for localized alerts has not yet been well applied within the current systems. This paper presents a real-time crime detection system that uses the Long-term Recurrent Convolutional Network model to analyze live feeds from video surveillance systems. The system is meant to classify actions into criminal and noncriminal actions with a very good success rate of 98%. Even as criminal activity is detected, the system provides real-time alerts while storing video clips as evidence. Improving public safety and offering proactive crime prevention is a significant improvement that results from tackling issues of accuracy, real-time processing, and specificity of alerts by this system. Real-time analysis, generation of alerts, and evidence storage integrate into a solid solution in enhancing the security of public space.

articleTitle: IoT based Cloud Kitchen Optimization using Fuzzy Intelligence and Advanced Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The task of managing a kitchen is often regarded as challenging, notwithstanding numerous advancements in technology. Consequently, there is a clear need for kitchen operations to be streamlined for ease. The innovative Kitchen concept leverages the Smart Ecosystem in its design and incorporates a smartphone application as the end-user interface. Within the Advanced Kitchen, the grocery operations framework, a fuzzy logic framework for flexible cooking, and signal handling for detecting the cooktop's whistle are included. The grocery operations system is equipped with a single ultrasonic transducer to gauge stock levels, and a wireless connectivity module facilitates data enhancements to a specific cloud-based key. Through the mobile application, users are able to view the remaining quantities of items, receive shortage alerts, and access the shopping list. The hardware components for stock management and kitchen safeguarding it involves the transmission of data from sensors to the cloud. Sensor values can be accessed even if the user is away from home. Future research could explore the hardware implementation of fuzzy logic on Arduino, where inputs might be received through a keypad and outputs displayed on an LCD, achieving full system independence. Similarly, if whistle specimens are captured via a mic and the tally is shown on an LCD screen, the system would also become self-sufficient.

articleTitle: An Optimized Equivariant Quantum Network for Ingenious Building Monitoring and Control using an Android Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: For enhancing the security and functionality of smart environments, motion recognition, classification and intruder detection has to be added into the building monitoring and control system. This research developed a Self-Guided Efficient Net UNet based Equivariant Quantum Network with Alpine Skiing Optimization (SGENUN-EQN-ASO) for improving intruder detection in buildings by utilizing an Android application for real-time motion detection and categorization. To prepare the data for analysis, processing can be done on the Self-Guided Filtering (SGF). An enhanced approach is Essential Objectness, Cascade Networks, Equivariant Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks (EquivQCNN) to enhance the detection precision and EfficientNet-based EE-UNet for precise motion assessment. Thus, the Android application works as monitoring and control interface providing real-time notifications and the answers to detected intrusions. With the use of optimisation techniques like Alpine Skiing Optimisation (ASO), which is used to fine-tune the hyperparameters of Equivariant Quantum Neural Networks (EQNNs), the system is able to provide stable and flexible performance. The results demonstrating that the integration of the latest machine learning approaches into the solutions in smart buildings brings significant enhancement to the detection effectiveness and response times, as to the overall security and management.

articleTitle: An Implementation of Web Scraping IMDB Website
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Web scraping is a powerful technique for extracting data from websites, and it has numerous applications in fields such as data science, market research, and business intelligence. In this article, web scraping is applied to extract data from IMDb (Internet Movie Database), the popular online database of movies, TV shows, and other entertainment content. The goal of this system is to collect a comprehensive dataset of movies and TV shows from IMDb website, along with their associated metadata such as ratings, genres, cast and crew and plot summaries. This automates the data collection process, creates charts/visualisation, displays the distribution of movie ratings, the most popular genres, the top-rated actors, or the most profitable movies. Python and the Beautiful Soup library files are used to extract the data, and then store it in a structured format and also into a MYSQL server database. Extracted ratings are analysed with different parameters of movies. It is found that this system followed a robust technique with DOM parsing, Tree traversal algorithms, CSS selectors, Xpath expressions and finite automata. Results are analysed with respect to extraction of required parameters.

articleTitle: Optimized Weld Defect Detection: A Comparative Analysis of CNN and SVM Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research presents a comprehensive evaluation of a machine learning model for slag inclusion recognition in welding applications. The model demonstrates exceptional performance in accurately classifying various stages of slag inclusions. The model achieves high precision values, ranging from 81.47% to 93.98%, indicating its ability to correctly identify positive examples. The recall values, ranging from 86.80% to 88.66%, demonstrate the model's sensitivity in capturing relevant cases. The Fl-score, a balanced measure of precision and recall, consistently achieves an average of 88.2 %, further validating the model's effectiveness. Support percentage values provide insights into the distribution of slag inclusion levels within the dataset, highlighting the model's ability to handle different class sizes. The consistent performance across various evaluation metrics, including macro, weighted, and micro averages, emphasizes the model's reliability and generalizability. The findings of this research demonstrate the potential of machine learning to significantly improve welding quality control processes. By accurately identifying and classifying slag inclusions, the model can contribute to enhanced product quality and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Classification of Hidden Patterns in Cancer Genome using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The complex structures in cancer genomes are obtained through the revolution of high-throughput technology. The major challenge involves the interpretation of complex sceneries of genomic alterations with the impact of diagnosis and prognosis. The proposed system includes deep-learning techniques that provide optimum solutions for evaluating hidden patterns of the cancer genome. They help to extract important information such as mutation and detection of therapeutic targets. The proposed system involves the aid of a Convolutional Neural Network, Recurrent Neural Network with Long Short Term Memory networks. They help in obtaining intricate genomic data. This is achieved through the spatial relationship and sequential dependencies within the genetic elements. The large-scale genomic datasets are trained which helps to learn the differentiation between the driver and passenger mutations. The genetic alterations provide information regarding the cancer progression. The deep learning model helps in the identification of desperate mutations with exclusive patterns that contribute to tumor development. The important aspect involves the prediction of prognosis. This includes the model to train and learn from the cumulative knowledge of patients in accordance with the genomic profiles. An accurate prognosis and personalized treatments are obtained by analyzing certain parameters such as gene expression, gene mutation and clinical data structures. These optimization techniques help in the identification of complex relationships in the identification of therapeutical compounds.

articleTitle: Enhanced Condition Monitoring of Low Voltage Motors in Harsh Environments with Ladybug Beetle Optimization and Context-Aware Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Low voltage motors are essential in many applications in contemporary industrial settings, as they power machines and guarantee efficient operations. However, these motors often operate in harsh environments where they are exposed to factors such as extreme temperatures, moisture, dust, and vibrations, which can lead to premature wear and failure. This paper proposes a hybrid method for low voltage motor condition monitoring in challenging industrial environments. The proposed method is the combined execution of Ladybug Beetle Optimization algorithm (LBOA) and Heterogeneous Context-Aware Graph Convolutional Network (HCAGCN). Hence it is named as LBOA-HCAGCN technique. Initially, the input data is collected from Triboelectric vibration sensors. Then, the collected data is fed into preprocessing utilizing Generalized Multi-kernel Maximum Correntropy Kalman Filter (GMKMCKF). This filter normalizes and cleans the data by effectively removing noise. Recursive Hilbert Transform (RHT) is used to extract time domain features such as mean, Root Mean Square (RMS), Peak-to-Peak Value, Skewness, and Kurtosis. Then the extracted features are given to HCAGCN for classify the motor health conditions such as normal, broken-bar, bowed-bar, bowed-rotor, faulty bearing, and voltage imbalance. In general, HCAGCN does not express adapting optimization strategies to determine optimal parameters to classify motor conditions. Hence, the LBOA is used to optimize the weight parameter of the HCAGCN which accurately classify motor conditions. The proposed LBOA-HCAGCN is implemented in MATLAB. Performance indicators such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Precision, and Accuracy were used to analyze the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Comparing the proposed LBOA-HCAGCN methodology to other existing techniques like Deep Residual Neural Network (DRNN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Recursive Neural Network (RNN), it achieves 25.8%, 26.4%, and 24.7% greater accuracy, 26.7%, 29.4%, and 21.7% precision.

Author Keywords: Generalized Multi-kernel Maximum Correntropy Kalman Filter

articleTitle: Predicting Indian Sign Language Gestures Using Deep Learning and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Indian Sign Language is the language used by people with disabilities in India. Unfortunately, the general public's ignorance of sign language makes it difficult for the especially abled and the general public to communicate. We are releasing a strategy to reduce this difference. We have adopted two distinct strategies to deal with this problem. first by employing the depth+RGB data acquired with a Microsoft Kinect to make gesture predictions in real-time. To segment the hand region from the RGB-D camera data, we used affine transformation and 3D reconstruction to map the RGB and depth information. Convolutional neural networks were trained with inputs that were segmented hand images or videos. With 50 static Indian Sign Language hand gestures used for training, a 97.18% classification accuracy was achieved on test data. Furthermore, this model achieved a 97.71 % classification accuracy when we transferred learning American Sign Language. A convolutional kernel and an LSP were used to train twenty dynamic gestures. This model's classification accuracy was 98.88%. Nevertheless, as soon as we implemented this system, we found that the methodology was flawed. Essentially, it is absurd to need to carry around both a bulky Microsoft Kinect and a device capable of performing the computation required for human-to-person interaction. We attempted to address this issue by using semantic segmentation of the hands. U-Net and ResNet 101 were combined.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Hierarchical Feature Learning and Modified CNN with ACAF
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains one of the leading causes of vision loss and blindness today, making the need for accurate and reliable detection techniques paramount. This work presents a new method for feature extraction through combining two methods namely; vSLM and Wavelet CNN. The approach is complemented by a modified CNN model that is equipped with an AdaptiveConvolutional ActivationFunction (ACAF) for classification. As it was mentioned before, the vSLM technique creates detailed retinal maps, and thus can be effective for the detection of critical DR indicators such as microaneurysms, haemorrhages, and exudates. Wavelet CNN enhances the feature extraction procedure, taking into consideration both spatial and spectral features of the retinal images. The resolution provided by the proposed CNN model with ACAF demonstrates outstanding classification results with accuracy rates of 97.12% on DiaretDB0 dataset, 99. 12% on the public EyePACS Kaggle dataset and 99.15% on the DRIVE dataset and 98.12% on the CHASE dataset. These findings highlight the importance of using the feature extraction and classification approach for improving the accuracy of DR detection and classification. The findings point to severe advancements in the diagnostic tools of DR and the effect of these enhancements in the pragmatic aspect of identify and handling of DR.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in Solar Power System with Internet of Things using Multi resolution Sinusoidal Neural Network - Snow Geese Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Fault detection in power systems, including Photovoltaic (PV) systems, using Internet of Things (IoT) involves deploying sensors to monitor key parameters and analyzing the data identify anomalies. The accuracy of these systems can be compromised by issues such as noisy or low-quality sensor data, which may lead to false positives or missed faults. Additionally, the complexity of managing large volumes of data from numerous IoT devices can strain the system, further affecting detection accuracy. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper proposes an efficient approach for fault uncovering in solar power system grounded on IoT. The data are collected from solar power generation dataset. Subsequently, the data are nourished to preprocessing. In preprocessing segment removes the absent values in the data utilizing Reverse Lognormal Kalman Filter (RLKF). The consequence after the preprocessing data is transported to the Multiresolution Sinusoidal Neural Network (MSNN). The line-line faults, ground faults, line-ground faults and partial shading are successfully predicted and classified by using MSNN. The Snow Geese Optimization (SGO) is rummage-sale to optimize the weight structure of MSNN. The projected MSNN-SGO is utilized within the MATLAB platform. Performance metrics counting precision, accuracy, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), F1-score, and Mean Squared Error (MSE) were examined in order to determine the proposed method. The proposed DAGCN-COA technique yields 14.89%, 16.89%, and 18.23% higher precision, 16.65%, 18.85%, and 17.89% higher accuracy, 22.36%, 15.42% and 28.27% lower RMSE when analysed the existing methods. The proposed MSNN-SGO technique is associated with the existing methods for instance spatial-temporal recurrent graph neural network (STRGNN), convolutional neural network (CNN), and long short-term memory network (LSTMN), respectively.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Fair Profit and Transparent Supply Chain Platform for Small-Scale Farmers: A Case for Agricultural Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: India's agricultural sector is the backbone of the country, yet there are inefficiencies, a lack of transparency, and unequal farmer prices in its supply chain. Issues including inadequate market accessibility, inadequate infrastructure, and insufficient value addition exacerbate these challenges, especially for small and marginal farmers. Stakeholder collaboration is occasionally lacking in traditional supply chain systems, which leads to uneven farmer compensation and inefficient product delivery to consumers. Information and communication technologies (ICT) have been used to solve these problems in the past, but scalability, data security, and cost-effectiveness have all been shown to be lacking. With its core characteristics of automation, security, and transparency, blockchain technology presents a viable substitute. Blockchain technology can be used in the agricultural supply chain, but there are a number of obstacles to overcome, such as high implementation costs, complicated technology, and a need for major stakeholder engagement. This study investigates how blockchain technology could resolve these problems and transform India's agricultural supply chain. The goal is to create a system that leverages smart contracts to improve product traceability, increase trust, and automate procedures. Additionally, the study looks at certain blockchain applications including payment automation and farm-to-customer monitoring that make use of Node.js, Ganache, Truffle, and MetaMask technologies. This paper offers a thorough evaluation of earlier studies and offers a method for building an agricultural ecosystem that is more open, effective, and sustainable and that benefits supply chain participants, farmers, and consumers. The development of a blockchain-based software program is the main objective of this project, which attempts to increase the efficiency and transparency of the agricultural supply chain. No direct model comparisons have been done because the effort focuses on a software solution rather than a prediction model. The system's ability to improve transaction transparency, security, and traceability is the main focus of the performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection with MobileNetV2 and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: To save lives, early identification of breast cancer is essential. While medical imaging benefits greatly from the use of models such as AlexNet, VGGNet and ResNet their high computing demands make their adoption difficult in locations with limited resources. This study presents an innovative approach to breast cancer detection by leveraging MobileNetV2, a model designed for efficiency in low-resource environments. While the standard MobileNetV2 achieved an accuracy level between 85% and 87%, our implementation of a custom classification head significantly enhanced performance, achieving an impressive accuracy of 98.8%. The model also demonstrated a precision of 97.5%, recall of 98.2%, and an Fl score of 97.8%. To further improve transparency, we applied Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), which gave us significant understanding into the model's decision-making process. This integration of efficiency and interpretability offers a viable answer to affordable breast cancer detection, with substantial potential for application in resource-limited settings.

articleTitle: Hybrid Quantum Classical Convolutional Neural Network with Spider Wasp Optimizer for Enhanced Data Security in Cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The growing volume of sensitive data being handled and kept online makes data protection in cloud-based environments essential. Maintaining the integrity and confidentiality of cloud-based systems requires strong protection against cyber-attacks and data breaches. This research presents a novel method utilizing a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Convolutional Neural Network with Spider Wasp Optimizer (HQCCNN-SWO) in the search for cutting-edge data security solutions for cloud environments. Utilizing cutting-edge methodologies, this approach improves data security detection's precision and effectiveness. To ensure that the model covers a wide range of attack scenarios, it is trained and assessed using three widely-used datasets: NSL-KDD, KDDCUP99, and UNSW-NB15. To improve the resilience of feature extraction and normalize data, the methodology starts with global-local depth normalization-based preprocessing. This addresses variances in input distributions and improves consistency. After that, features are extracted using a geometric algebra transformer, which enhances feature representation by identifying complex patterns and correlations in the data. Utilizing the best features of both classical and quantum computers, the model's central component, HQCCNN-SWO, combines quantum-classical convolutional neural network architecture. By using its sophisticated search capabilities and adaptability mechanisms, the Spider Wasp Optimizer (SWO) optimizes performance by fine-tuning network settings. HQCCNN-SWO is a potent framework that can be used in MATLAB to detect security threats more accurately and with less computational overhead. This methodology constitutes a significant progression in the identification of data security, providing a resilient and effective instrument for cloud settings. HQCCNN-SWO is a top-performing solution in the field of cloud data security because it combines advanced optimization techniques with quantum-classical methodologies.

Author Keywords: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Convolutional Neural Network with Spider Wasp Optimizer

articleTitle: AppleDiseaseNet-B7: A Robust Solution for Apple Leaf Disease Classification and Model Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Apple leaf diseases, like cedar apple rust, black rot, and apple scab, pose severe obstacles to apple farming and impact crop productivity and quality. The sophisticated classification model AppleDiseaseNet-B7, known for its efficiency and outstanding performance, was created using the EfficientNetB7 architecture and is presented in this paper. The model improves its feature extraction capabilities by utilizing pretrained weights from ImageNet, which makes it a good fit for differentiating between various apple leaf diseases. AppleDiseaseNet-B7 incorporates numerous unique layers intended to increase classification precision. A Global Average Pooling layer streamlines feature maps, complicated patterns are captured by a dense layer with ReLU activation, overfitting is reduced by a dropout layer, and class prediction is accomplished by a final dense layer with softmax activation. The model's resilience is further increased using thorough data preparation, and augmentation approaches from the PlantVillage and Kaggle Apple Leaf Disease datasets. A comprehensive comparison is made between AppleDiseaseNet-B7's performance and other well-known models, including DenseNet121, ResNet50, and AlexNet. The analysis shows that AppleDiseaseNet-B7 regularly performs better than comparable models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, among other criteria. This comparison demonstrates how well AppleDiseaseNet-B7 performs in classifying apple leaf diseases, providing a reliable and effective method for managing and detecting agricultural diseases. The study emphasizes how crucial sophisticated model selection is to enhancing crop health monitoring and disease control.

articleTitle: Graph-Informed Neural Networks with Green Anaconda Optimization Algorithm Based on Automated Classification of Condition of Mental Health Using Alpha Band EEG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Mental Health Status (MHS) Using Alpha Band EEG Signal” is the process of evaluating and categorizing a person's mental state by examining the electroencephalogram (EEG) recording of their alpha wave activity, which usually occurs between 8 and 13 Hz. articleTitle: Advancements and Trends in Student Prediction and Course Recommender Systems: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In the era of AI, one of the most important fields that can make best use of it is Education. Be it the student, teacher or the institution, each one of them can use it for their benefit. One important aspect in education is Personalized learning, it has evolved from being the suggestions given by teacher or mentor to AI based system which are giving suggestions to students according to individuals capabilities and Interest. This article gives an in-depth idea about AI based research done as of now for student's performance prediction and course recommendation systems. Article discusses various methods such as Machine learning (ML), Deep learning (DL), Recommender Systems used by various researchers along with their comparison and accuracies. After studying and comparing the research articles, we have suggested our approach based on gap findings. articleTitle: A Mathematical Framework for Optimizing Lexical Analysis on Multi-Core Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: In the field of multi-core computing systems, optimizing the distribution of tasks across multiple cores is essential to harness maximum performance potential. Traditional static task allocation methods, often employed in lexical analysis-the initial and vital phase of compiling and interpreting source code-frequently result in imbalanced workloads and suboptimal resource utilization. This paper introduces an innovative and sophisticated mathematical model for dynamic task allocation specifically tailored to lexical analysis, aiming to revolutionize how tasks are distributed across multiple cores. By employing advanced dynamic allocation techniques, our proposed model not only ensures balanced workload distribution but also scales efficiently with varying computational demands. This novel approach significantly enhances the efficiency of lexical analysis in multi-core environments, leading to substantial improvements in processing times and resource utilization. Extensive experimental results validate the superiority of our method, showcasing dramatic reductions in processing latency and a more effective exploitation of multi-core capabilities. This dynamic model not only advances the field of lexical analysis but also sets a new benchmark for task allocation strategies in multi-core computing systems, promising broader applicability and future innovations in compiler design and resource management.

articleTitle: Resilient Framework for Next-Generation Heterogeneous Wireless Networks in Disaster Management
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: The growing occurrence and concentration of natural and artificial disasters necessitate the development of robust communication systems capable of maintaining reliable and efficient connectivity under adverse conditions. Heterogeneous wireless networks (HSNs) have emerged as a promising solution, offering the flexibility to integrate various wireless technologies and adapt to changing environments. However, the inherent complexity and dynamic nature of HSNs present significant challenges in ensuring resilience and reliability, particularly in disaster scenarios where network infrastructure may be severely compromised. This research investigates a Resilient Framework for Next Generation Heterogeneous Wireless Networks in Disaster Management, focusing on enhancing communication reliability and efficiency during critical scenarios. The study introduces Network Coding Enhanced COPE (NC-COPE), a novel algorithm integrating network coding principles into the COPE framework. Simulation analysis compares NC-COPE with existing algorithms: Optimized Link State Routing (OLSR), Coding-Aware Routing (CAR), and Dynamic Source Routing (DSR) using metrics such as Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), Routing Overhead, and Resilience to Node Failures. NC-COPE demonstrates superior performance in maintaining high PDR, reducing routing overhead, and enhancing network resilience under node failures. The findings underscore NC-COPE's potential to mitigate communication challenges in disaster management scenarios, highlighting its role in future wireless network deployments.

articleTitle: Intelligent Inhalation Therapy for Cystic Fibrosis Using IoT and Machine Learning Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Optimal patients result in the long-term management of cystic fibrosis (CF) and need personalized treatment strategies due to the hereditary disorder's impact on respiratory problems. One potential approach to individualized CF treatment is intelligent inhalation therapy systems that combine machine learning (ML) algorithms with Internet of Things (IoT) sensors. To provide CF patients with a predictive modeling framework that can personalize their inhalation treatment using the Random Forest algorithm. The algorithm is designed to predict individual-level outcomes, including the potential of an exacerbation and the efficacy of therapy, by mining a large and varied dataset that includes patient demographics, lung function measurements, medication adherence records, environmental factors, and reports of symptoms. The Random Forest method was selected due to its capacity to manage diverse data types, detect intricate relationships between variables, and provide insights that can be understood. It shows that the Random Forest model effectively predicts important outcomes for CF care by training, validating, and evaluating it using real-world data from CF patients. Exacerbation risks and patient-specific therapy responses may be better understood by feature significance analysis, allowing for more targeted intervention approaches. The proposed predictive modeling framework will improve the efficiency and effectiveness of inhalation treatment for managing CF. Healthcare practitioners may enhance the management of CF via ML analytics and data collected through the IoT. This allows for delivering personalized treatment regimens, optimizing resource allocation, and better patient outcomes. Challenges include ensuring data accuracy, managing extensive datasets, sustaining real-time monitoring, optimizing algorithms, and ensuring system stability.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Climate Sustainability: A Comprehensive Review of Applications, Challenges, and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: Climate sustainability plays a very crucial role in environmental sustainability and by considerable use of natural resources, and reducing pollution, we can make our planet beautiful and sustaining for the life of future generations. Climate changes constitute increasingly severe challenges, and with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the necessity for innovation in fostering climate sustainability has become increasingly evident. This review organizes an exhaustive inventory of which AI affects climate science. The challenges remain unmet in AI's various applications across sectors such as optimization of renewable energy, climate modeling, disaster resilience and environmental monitoring. This paper discusses the important roles of applying AI in overcoming climate change difficulties. These include energy management or conservation, cap-and-trade for carbon emissions, climate and weather forecasting, grid management, transportation, and agriculture infrastructure, or city planning. It also looks into how and the extent to which AI is adopted in resource management, increasing the adoption of renewable energy, fostering sustainable development, and overseeing resources such as water and forests. This study acknowledges various barriers that impede the effective application of Artificial Intelligence in combating climate change which include data restrictions, algorithms' bias, and ethical issues with AI operations. To solve the major challenges described, we improve the major findings of this extensive literature review and distill a set of practical recommendations for policy-makers, industrial actors and researchers. Which will in return assist in overcoming challenges and enhance the capacity of AI in combating climate change and environmental conservation.

articleTitle: Detection of ARP Spoofing with Optimized False Alarm Using Deep Learning Based Absolute Thresholding

articleTitle: Adaptive Feature Learning for Robust Pathogen Detection in Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This research presents an innovative deep learning method for classifying plant pathogens by using domain-adaptive feature extraction. The ResNet50 model has been adjusted and trained on the Plant Village dataset specifically for the purpose of extracting features. The retrieved characteristics are then inputted into a concise Deep Neural Network (DNN) with two hidden layers. The integrated model is then trained on a distinct dataset that is especially targeted against plant pathogens. The trial outcomes show how successful the suggested strategy is. Combined model achieves competitive results compared to a directly fine-tuned ResNet50 model on the plant pathogen dataset, highlighting the potential of domain adaptation for improving plant pathogen classification, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Real-Time Vehicle Tracking Model with Mobile Apps
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Sustainable Expert Systems (ICSES)
abstract: This study presents an AI-based real-time vehicle tracking model integrated with a mobile application for institutional use. The system is designed to improve the efficiency, accuracy, and reliability of vehicle monitoring and management by utilizing multiple sensors, high-precision GPS positioning, and advanced artificial intelligence algorithms. The core components of the system include a mobile application for real-time vehicle location display, a back-end server for data processing and storage, GPS devices installed in vehicles, and AI algorithms for data analysis. The methodology section details the implementation of these components and their integration. The performance of the system was evaluated through extensive experiments, which showed that the combination of the three core modules significantly improved the tracking accuracy. Module 1 alone achieved an accuracy of about 90%, which increased to about 95% with the addition of Module 2, and further to nearly 99% with the integration of Module 3. These results demonstrate the robustness of the system and its potential for application in various sectors, including logistics, public transportation, government, and the commercial vehicle management.
